# envoy-rust STATE.md — Historical Reference Archive

> This file holds historical narrative blocks relocated verbatim out of
> `STATE.md` per **ADR-0035** (see `docs/envoy-rust/DECISIONS.md`). It exists
> solely to keep `STATE.md` small enough to read in full at cold-start while
> preserving every prior-commit narrative byte-for-byte per doctrine D-3.4
> (context isolation) + D-3.5 (decisions/narratives are written, not deleted).
>
> **This file is read-on-demand, NOT required at cold-start.** The cold-start
> procedure (`BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §1 Step B) requires reading `STATE.md` in
> full; this archive is consulted only when a session needs the historical
> detail behind a `STATE.md` pointer.
>
> Content is append-only and preserved verbatim: every "THIS commit" reference
> inside a relocated block retains its original meaning (it resolves to the
> commit named in that block's own "Historical reference (preserved …)" header
> or subsection) and must not be rewritten. Original section/subsection
> headings and ordering are preserved. The `## Relocated from …` headings below
> are organizational wrappers added at relocation time to identify each
> block's origin in `STATE.md`.

---

**status:** **PHASE 110 §5 STATE-2 PLAN-WRITE COMPLETE — THE §6.1 SPLIT FIRED (ADR-0178) AND NO `PLAN.md` WAS WRITTEN** (§6.2 step 7). This session re-confirmed ALL TEN parent PLAN-VERIFY items (`110/SPEC.md` §7 V-1…V-10) FRESH against the `ENVOY_TARGET.md`-pinned `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (digest `sha256:56da5afd…70c2`, verified by `docker image inspect` BEFORE any probe; the probe container was torn down and `docker ps -a` confirmed zero remaining), probing with a **RAW-SOCKET** HTTP/1.1 client precisely because a header-dict client destroys the response header ORDER and CASE that V-2 and V-10 turn on. **FOUR INHERITED CLAIMS DID NOT SURVIVE, and each is load-bearing.** **(1) V-5 REFUTED — the H1/H2 boundary is NOT structural.** `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:518` calls **`envoy_http1::build_response`**, which reaches `synth_direct_response`/`synth_400`/`synth_404`/`synth_redirect` → `synth_with`; `envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:2127-2128` says so outright. **So the transform MUST NOT be installed in `synth_with`, in any `synth_*` wrapper, or in `build_response`** — that would transform H2's route-decision replies while missing H2's own `synth_h2_*` family, the ADR-0049 silent-divergence class. The seam belongs at the H1 wire funnels, of which there are **TWO** (`hcm.rs:1468` behind the `outgoing_direct` guard at `:1457`, and the io_uring worker's own `write_owned` at `uring.rs:292/313/338/389`). **(2) V-3 CLOSED IN SCOPE — `synth_redirect` IS transformed** (`200` + `location` SURVIVING + `content-type: application/grpc` + `grpc-status: 2` + `content-length: 0`), so it is covered by `110.1` rather than banked, and **CF-110-3 is REASSIGNED** to a NEW divergence this session measured: upstream emits `location` on a `direct_response` whose status is **`201` or `3xx`**, in BOTH directions, where envoy-rust does not — PRE-EXISTING and ORTHOGONAL to gRPC, but a live fixture hazard, so `110.2` forbids any `201`/`3xx` `direct_response` cell in `0089`. **(3) V-8 REFUTED — the parent's `grpc-message` rule is WRONG at the upper boundary: `~` (0x7E) IS ESCAPED to `%7E`.** The corrected rule is that a byte passes through iff it is in **`0x20..=0x7D` AND is not `%`**; everything else becomes `%` + TWO UPPERCASE hex digits, UTF-8 per byte. **(4) V-4 CORRECTED — `synth_with` has FOUR direct callers, not seven** (`synth_400`/`synth_404`/`synth_501` are depth-2 wrappers over `synth_status`). **V-2's own PREMISE is also refuted:** `diff_headers` compares a `BTreeSet` of LOWER-CASED header NAMES plus exact VALUES outside the 3-entry `HEADER_ALLOW_LIST` — **it never reads ORDER**, so the "harness byte-compares" sentence in `synth_with`'s doc block is a house convention pinned by unit tests, not a differential gate (the order was measured anyway: `[location,] content-type, grpc-status, [grpc-message,] date, server, connection, content-length`). **V-1 re-ran identically over 20 statuses plus controls; **status:** **PHASE 110 §5 STATE-0/1 NEXT-PHASE PICK COMPLETE (THIS session) — ROADMAP row `110` added `in-progress` UNDER `### gRPC family`, phase directory created, `SPEC.md` written, ADR-0177 FIRED.** This session picked the phase and wrote its SPEC and **nothing else**: no `PLAN.md`, no code, no test, no fixture, no banked finding fixed, no landed artifact edited, no `cargo` command run. **THE PICK RESTS ON MEASUREMENT, NOT ON DOCUMENTATION.** Three upstream matrices were probed at this session against the `ENVOY_TARGET.md`-pinned `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (digest `sha256:56da5afd…70c2`, verified by `docker image inspect` BEFORE any probe; all probe containers torn down afterwards). **(a) The HTTP→`grpc-status` mapping is a SPARSE EIGHT-ENTRY table over a DEFAULT of 2**: `400`→13, `401`→16, `403`→7, `404`→12, `429`→14, `502`→14, `503`→14, `504`→14, and EVERYTHING ELSE → 2 — including all 2xx/3xx and, counter-intuitively, `500`, `501`, `405`, `408`, `409`, `412`, `413` and `499`. **(b) The detection rule is SHARP**: matched iff `content-type` is EXACTLY `application/grpc` or begins with `application/grpc+`. `application/grpc+proto`/`+json` MATCH; `application/grpc; charset=utf-8` does NOT (a parameter defeats it), `APPLICATION/GRPC` does NOT (CASE-SENSITIVE), `application/grpc-web` and `application/grpcfoo` do NOT. Detection is METHOD-INSENSITIVE and INDEPENDENT of `te: trailers`. **(c) `grpc-message` is gRPC `Status-Message` percent-encoded**: SPACE PRESERVED, `\n`→`%0A`, `\t`→`%09`, UTF-8 PER BYTE (`é`→`%C3%A9`), UPPERCASE hex, and `%`→`%25` so the input `%25` doubles to `%2525`; the header is ABSENT ENTIRELY (not empty) when the original body is empty. **THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT — the one that made the pick viable and that RESOLVES A STANDING REJECTION: THIS SURFACE INVOLVES NO TRAILERS.** ADR-0048 rejected the gRPC family as blocked on HTTP/2 trailer propagation, a verdict re-affirmed ~15 times (most recently ADR-0171(b) and the ADR-0175 pick) and **still entirely correct for the gRPC DATA PATH**. It does NOT reach this slice: every gRPC-detected local reply arrives over HTTP/1.1 with **`content-length: 0`**, carrying `grpc-status`/`grpc-message` as ordinary response HEADERS — a bodiless response has no chunked framing and therefore NO TRAILER SECTION AT ALL. ADR-0177 records this as a NARROWING of ADR-0048's reach, established by measurement; it does NOT supersede it. **The tree's real trailer gap is left exactly as it is, and §5 non-goal 2 forbids adding a trailer API.** **WHAT THIS SESSION BANKS AND DOES NOT CLEAR** (§6.3; ADR-0165): the entire inherited ledger, untouched — the `109.2` REVIEW's EIGHT Minors (M-1…M-8) and ELEVEN Nits (N-1…N-11), the `109.1` M-5 + N-1…N-6 set, the `108.2` M-2 + N-1…N-6 set, **CF-109-1 (WIDENED)/2/3, CF-108-1/2/3, CF-76-1, CF-75-2/3/4/5/6**, CF-72-2/CF-75-1, M71-6, CF-74-1/2/3/4/6, CF-73-1 and the HTTP-filters-family (1)-(4). **STOP CONDITION RE-MEASURED FROM DISK — the FORTY-SIXTH consecutive evaluation and FALSE again, because it requires ALL THREE legs:** (i) TRUE at entry (113/113 `done`; 113 of 114 after this pick); (ii) **FALSE**, confirmed by DIRECT TREE PROBES rather than by the ledger's own assertion — **14** crates with no `envoy-http3`/`envoy-grpc`/`envoy-wasm`, `grep -rl '^quinn' crates/*/Cargo.toml` = **0**, `tonic-web` = **0**, `wasmtime` = **0**, `tests/conformance/` holding ONLY `h2spec/`, and `runtime_key_is_rtds_inert` still on disk (2 hits); (iii) **FALSE** — **TWO** family headings still carry ZERO rows. **NO `stop` FILE WAS CREATED; `ls stop` returns `No such file or directory`.**

The parent SPEC had this set as explicitly NOT MEASURED and assumed reuse. **(ii) `canonical_reason` IS MISSING 303/307/308.** `crates/envoy-http1/src/response.rs:188-215` has 301 and 302 but the other three fall through to `_ => "OK"`, so a 303 redirect would emit `HTTP/1.1 303 OK`. **The differential fixture CANNOT catch this** — the harness parses the status CODE only and the equivalence matrix does not compare the reason phrase — so it needs an in-process pin. Not in the parent SPEC at all. **(iii) THE `RedirectAction` ONEOFS ARE EXCLUSIVE ON FIELD PRESENCE, NOT ON VALUE.** MEASURED via `--mode validate`: `https_redirect: false` + `scheme_redirect: "ftp"` **REJECTS**, `https_redirect: false` **ALONE ACCEPTS**, `path_redirect: ""` + `prefix_rewrite: "/q"` **REJECTS**. So `https_redirect` MUST be `Option<bool>` and the path/scheme members `Option<String>`; a `#[serde(default)] bool` loses presence and would silently mint a NEW reject-direction divergence. **(iv) THE `prefix_rewrite` `:path` MUTATION NEEDS `&mut Request`.** The access-log record reads the path AFTER `build_response_in` returns (`build_access_log_record`, `hcm.rs:1601-1608`). MEASURED as contained — **8** call sites workspace-wide and every one already holds a `mut` binding (`hcm.rs:859`, `uring.rs:280`, `envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:459`) — versus **9** construction sites for the rejected `BuildOutcome::Synth` third-field alternative. **THE TWO PARENT-SPEC §7 CELLS THIS SESSION WAS REQUIRED TO MEASURE ARE MEASURED:** the wire reason phrases `FOUND` → `302 Found` and `PERMANENT_REDIRECT` → `308 Permanent Redirect` (301/303/307 re-confirmed in the same run), and the FULL redirect response-header set (above). **AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT MAKES FIXTURE `0086` VIABLE AT ALL:** with `Host: envoy-rust.test:1234` — a port deliberately DIFFERENT from the listen port — `https_redirect` yields `https://envoy-rust.test:1234/...` while `host_redirect` yields `http://example.com/...` with the port DROPPED. The authority is driven by the **`Host` header, not the socket**, which is why `location` is byte-comparable across two proxies listening on different ports. **TWO PARENT-SPEC CORRECTIONS are recorded in the sub-phase SPECs rather than edited into the parent** (ADR-0169 DECISION 5): its §4.1 item 5 is wrong that the `Route` action-cardinality check uses a `ConfigError` variant — it uses `serde::de::Error::custom` — and its `:2544`/`:2565` citation names one arm from each of **TWO SEPARATE** `Serialize` impls (`impl Serialize for Route` at `:2529-2552`, `impl Serialize for RouteAction` at `:2554-2570`), both of which need a new arm.

a `grep -rn` over `crates/` for `RedirectAction`/`host_redirect`/`path_redirect`/`port_redirect`/`https_redirect`/`scheme_redirect`/`strip_query` returns **ZERO** implementation hits. **WHY THIS SURFACE (four measured properties):** it is **backend-free** (the recon config exercising all eight sub-fields declared ZERO clusters and validated OK — so the fixture is FULLY VERIFIABLE LOCALLY on a host where backend-routing fixtures go RED and CI is otherwise the only authority); it needs **ZERO new harness machinery** (`location` is NOT on the THREE-entry `HEADER_ALLOW_LIST` at `tests/differential/src/lib.rs:1177-1181`, and `diff_headers` at `:1193` compares every non-allow-listed name **value-exact**, so the existing `Driver::Http1ProbeList` witnesses the `location` string byte-exact cross-proxy for free); it has **ONE clean runtime seam** (a single `match &route.action` at `crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:2110`, and H2 has NO resolver of its own — it calls H1's at `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:475`/`:518` — so a third arm serves BOTH codecs); and it is **rich but fully deterministic** (15 runtime cells + 7 reject-direction rules, no timing, no concurrency). **THE LOAD-BEARING MEASURED RULES** (full table in `SPEC.md` §3): **the AUTHORITY ASYMMETRY is the trap** — `host_redirect` DROPS the request's original port (`orig.test:18000` → `http://example.com/host`) while a scheme-only change PRESERVES it (`https_redirect` → `https://orig.test:18000/https/x`), and `port_redirect` overrides in both cases without normalising a redundant `:443`; the query is **PRESERVED by default even when `path_redirect` replaces the path wholesale** (`/path/x?k=v` → `/newpath?k=v`), `strip_query: true` drops it; **`%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` is `direct_response`** — the SAME string envoy-rust already emits at `hcm.rs:2112`, so NO new detail string / `Op` / `AccessLogRecord` field is needed; **`%RESPONSE_FLAGS%` is `-`**; **`prefix_rewrite` MUTATES the logged `:path`** (`/pfx/sub` logged as `PATH=/replaced/sub`) while `path_redirect` does NOT; and **`port_redirect` has NO PGV upper bound** (`70000` both validates AND renders verbatim), so envoy-rust must **NOT** add a `1..=65535` bound or it manufactures a reject-direction divergence. **SEVEN items are recorded as explicitly NOT MEASURED in `SPEC.md` §7** — most consequentially the wire reason phrases for 302/308, redirect on a TLS listener, redirect over HTTP/2, and the FULL redirect response-header set — and the state-2 PLAN-write must MEASURE the fixture-critical ones rather than assume them.

NO runtime behavior change — the value-matcher `absent+invert` divergence stays the correctly-scoped CF-72-1 boundary; the fix is to PIN and DOCUMENT it accurately. Docs-only review close. **status:** **PHASE 67 STATE-0/1 BRAINSTORM COMPLETE — the state-2 PLAN-write is next.** This session ran the §5 state-0/1 next-phase PICK via `superpowers:brainstorming`. Cold-started per `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §1; confirmed `git status --porcelain` clean, branch `main`, `HEAD` = `origin/main` = `4505016` (the phase-66 state-6 close-out, unmoved — `git fetch origin --prune` → `0 0` ahead/behind), no ROADMAP row `planned`/`in-progress`, no phase-67 directory, and **ADR-0128 free** (`grep -c '^## ADR-0128'` → 0). **NO code changed this session** (SPEC + ADR + ROADMAP + STATE only). **A real STATE-0 RECON ran before the pick** (the ADR-0037/0041/.../0123 cadence): a code-read at `4505016` plus a live drive of the pinned `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`. Every load-bearing claim is measured, quoted verbatim in `SPEC.md` §0, and cited `file:line`; none is recalled. **R-0.1 — the new parity gap.** `[rbac, echo]` validates (rbac is NON-TERMINAL); `[echo, rbac]` is rejected with phase 66's terminal error; **`[rbac]` alone is REJECTED**: `non-terminal filter named envoy.filters.network.rbac ... is the last filter in a network filter chain.` That is the **bilateral dual** of the rule phase 66 landed — *every chain must END in a terminal filter* — and envoy-rust does not enforce it. It was **structurally undiscoverable at phase 66**, which had no non-terminal filter to violate it with. **R-0.2 — the target is deterministic.** On DENY, Envoy writes **zero bytes** and closes with a **clean EOF, no RST**, discarding the client's already-sent bytes; on ALLOW the payload round-trips through the terminal `echo`. The decision is taken **once per connection at establishment, before any downstream byte is read** — which is why the iteration protocol needs only an `on_new_connection` hook and **not** `on_data` (deferred as **CF-67-3**, per §6.3's no-incomplete-stubs rule). **R-0.3/R-0.13 — stats and the INERT case.** Counters are `<stat_prefix>.rbac.{allowed,denied,shadow_allowed,shadow_denied}`; `stat_prefix` is REQUIRED (proto constraint), `rules` is OPTIONAL. **With `rules` omitted the filter is INERT: the connection is allowed and NEITHER counter increments** — it is *not* `default action ALLOW, counted`. A naive default-`Rules` implementation would produce a **stat divergence with no body divergence**. Error precedence was also probed: a chain violating both rules at once reports the **terminal-not-last** error. **These resolve PLAN-VERIFY V-3 and V-6 at state-1.** **R-0.9 — the vacuity trap, and why the harness must grow.** `expected_stats` exists on only three `Driver` variants, all HTTP; the four raw-TCP/TLS variants have none. Because `assert_body_rule`'s `ByteExact` is a bare inequality check, a DENY fixture asserting only *both returned zero bytes* would **pass vacuously even if envoy-rust never implemented RBAC**. Extending the raw-TCP driver family with `expected_stats` is therefore an **in-scope hard requirement**, not polish. (This is the same vacuity hazard the phase-66 `REVIEW.md` identified, which fixture `0071` escaped only by carrying a non-empty payload.) **R-0.5/R-0.6 — reuse is PARTIAL, and there is a naming hazard.** envoy-rust already models `RbacConfig`/`Rules`/`Policy`/`Permission`/`Principal` (landed by the **HTTP** RBAC filter), with the empty-set and `RBAC_TREE_MAX_DEPTH` validations reusable as-is — but its arms are HTTP-shaped (`header`, `url_path`, `metadata`) and there is **no `direct_remote_ip`/`remote_ip`/`source_ip`/`destination_port`/`destination_ip` arm and no `CidrRange`**. And `crates/envoy-filter/src/rbac.rs` (1270 lines) is `envoy.filters.http.rbac` — **a different feature sharing the name**, exactly the `direct_response` conflation hazard phase 66 hit. **CONSUMES CF-66-2** (the iteration protocol), **M66-3** (the `JoinSet` non-reaping + unbounded per-connection drain shared verbatim by `echo.rs:21-59` and `direct_response.rs:36-74` — this phase restructures **both** accept loops, which is exactly the joint repair unit the phase-66 review demanded) and **M66-4** (the doc-precision line in a file being restructured anyway). **CLOSES M66-5 on measured evidence, with NO code change.** The phase-66 review recorded envoy-rust's behavior on two config edges and **deliberately declined to assert Envoy's**, because neither was probed. Both were probed this session: an empty `filters: []` network chain is **ACCEPTED by upstream Envoy** — so envoy-rust's acceptance is **parity, not a divergence**, and *the reviewer's stated intuition that Envoy rejects it was WRONG* — and `direct_response` with `response: {}` is **REJECTED by both** (upstream: proto `specifier is required`; envoy-rust: serde `missing field inline_string` — same class, different text, which §7.4 permits). **This vindicates the D-3.3 discipline of asserting only what was measured.** **OPENS CF-67-1** (`shadow_rules` + the two shadow counters, emitted as constant `0`), **CF-67-2** (`Action::LOG`), **CF-67-3** (`on_data`-time iteration with buffering — required by the first payload-parsing network filter), **CF-67-4** (the L4 matcher-arm posture: envoy-rust rejects `header` in **parity** with Envoy, and also rejects `url_path`/`metadata` fail-loud where Envoy accepts a matcher that can never match at L4). **Chosen over `sni_cluster`** — the other candidate non-terminal filter — because `sni_cluster` needs the downstream SNI without terminating TLS, i.e. a `tls_inspector` **listener filter**, and envoy-rust has **no listener-filter concept at all** (`lib.rs:230` defers it by name). Same CF-66-2 payoff, strictly more work. Also chosen over `redis_proxy`/`thrift_proxy` (terminal, force nothing), `mongo_proxy`/`zookeeper_proxy`/`kafka_broker` (also force `on_data` buffering), xDS CDS/LDS hot-reload, the non-deterministic LB policies, `DC`, and the doc-only leaves. **NO new crate, dependency, or fuzz target** — §7.4 gate (d) is satisfied by the pre-existing `parse_bootstrap` target (network `rbac` **parses nothing**; a corpus seed is added instead), and the state-4 session must **record that explicitly rather than skip it silently**. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds (D-3.8). **The §6.1 split is PROJECTED TO FIRE at the state-2 PLAN-write** (~1740 net LoC vs the ~1500 threshold; ~16-20 tasks vs ~25 — §6.1 triggers on **either**). Projected shape: `67.1` = protocol + chain-termination rule + `rbac` with `any`-only matchers + fixtures `0072`/`0073` + the harness `expected_stats` extension + the M66-3/M66-4 consumption; `67.2` = the connection-level matcher arms + `CidrRange` + the CF-67-4 rejections. **The PLAN-write owns the split decision and must re-derive the estimate rather than inherit it.** **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0128**; **ADR-0129 RESERVED** for that split (lapses to the next new-phase pick if it does not fire). ADR-0123 remains in force (its CF-66-2 deferral is now consumed on exactly the trigger it named); ADR-0124 untouched; **ADR-0127's one-off §5.1 chaining override does NOT apply — this was a normal single-state session**; ADR-0014 in force; ADR-0028 open; ADR-0049 governs the fail-loud posture behind the CF-67-4 rejections.

A circuit-breaker overflow probe (`max_connections: 0`) showed `x-envoy-overloaded: true` ALSO survives IN ITS ORIGINAL POSITION — the pass-through rule is GENERAL, not a `location` special case. The generalized rule (pass-throughs in original relative order; then `content-type`, `grpc-status`, `[grpc-message]`; then `date`, `server`, `connection`; then `content-length: 0`) reproduces all THREE measured cases exactly. **Order remains a UNIT-TEST concern only — `diff_headers` never reads it.** **(5) A FEATURE-GATED MODULE IS INVISIBLE TO `cargo test --workspace`.** `crates/envoy-http1/src/uring.rs` is gated at `lib.rs:24-25` behind the `uring` feature (`Cargo.toml:27-28`) and contains **NO `#[cfg(test)]` and NO `#[test]` at all**. Its seam therefore gets its coverage STRUCTURALLY — the transform lives INSIDE `write_owned` (all four call sites are synth; the proxied path uses `write_head_body` at `:376`) — and the absence of a test is BANKED as **CF-110-5** rather than papered over. **(6) A NEW PRE-EXISTING DIVERGENCE, BANKED AS CF-110-4:** upstream's own NON-gRPC local-reply header order is `[pass-through,] content-length, content-type, date, server, connection`, whereas envoy-rust's `synth_with` emits `server, date, content-length, content-type, connection`. ORDER-ONLY, invisible to `diff_headers`, PRE-EXISTING and gRPC-ORTHOGONAL — **not a licence to touch `synth_with`.** Together with CF-110-3 (upstream's `location` on a `201`/`3xx` `direct_response`) these are the two divergences `110.2`'s fixture must route around. **[NEW AT THE PHASE-110 §5 STATE-2 SPLIT — six traps, every one MEASURED AT THIS COMMIT.]** **(1) A SPEC's "structural boundary" claim is a CENSUS, and this one was FALSE.** The parent `110/SPEC.md` §3 D6 asserted that H1 and H2 share only the route RESOLVER, so scoping to H1 was "a real boundary rather than a hopeful one". **MEASURED FALSE:** `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:518` calls **`envoy_http1::build_response`**, which reaches `synth_direct_response`/`synth_400`/`synth_404`/`synth_redirect` → `synth_with`, and `envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:2127-2128` documents it ("ONE arm serves BOTH codecs"). H2 owns its own synthesisers for UPSTREAM-FAILURE paths ONLY. **The general rule: when a SPEC says two subsystems are isolated, grep the CALL EDGE, not the type names.** **(2) A CODE-SHAPE claim can be right about the NAMES and wrong about the TIERS.** The inherited "`synth_with` has SEVEN callers" list conflated direct callers with the whole synth family: there are **FOUR** direct call sites, and `synth_400`/`synth_404`/`synth_501` are depth-2 wrappers over `synth_status`. `grep -rn 'synth_with' crates/` returns 7 hits of which only 4 are CALLS — the rest are the definition and two doc mentions. **Count call sites, not grep hits.** **(3) A DOC COMMENT'S JUSTIFICATION CAN BE STALE EVEN WHEN ITS ADVICE IS GOOD.** `synth_with`'s doc block says "Header ORDER is load-bearing — the differential harness byte-compares against upstream Envoy." **The harness does NOT byte-compare:** `diff_headers` builds a `BTreeSet` of LOWER-CASED header NAMES, compares the SETS, then compares VALUES for every name outside the 3-entry `HEADER_ALLOW_LIST`. **Order is never read.** Matching upstream's order is still correct practice (unit tests pin it), but a wrong order fails a UNIT test, not a fixture — do not price it as a differential risk. **(4) A MEASURED RULE CAN BE WRONG AT EXACTLY ONE BOUNDARY BYTE.** The parent SPEC's `grpc-message` rule ("`0x20` through `0x7E` pass through except `%`") is FALSE: **`~` (0x7E) IS ESCAPED to `%7E`**. The corrected rule is pass-through iff **`0x20..=0x7D` AND not `%`**. It is not: `BodyRule::JsonShape` parses both bodies through `serde_json`, and because `preserve_order` is enabled NOWHERE in the workspace, `serde_json::Map` is a `BTreeMap` that canonically key-sorts on re-serialization. **The fix was already in the harness; the temptation was to add an allow-list and weaken the assertion.** **(5) AN "ABSENCE" CAN BE PINNED BY A PASSING TEST, AND A PHASE THAT BUILDS THE ABSENT THING MUST SAY SO.** Four places assert "there is no runtime layer", one of them a test literally named `runtime_key_is_rtds_inert`. None becomes wrong when a `static_layer` store lands without RTDS or consumers — **but a reviewer meeting that test name inside a phase titled "runtime" will read a contradiction unless the SPEC pre-empts it.** **Grep for tests and docs that assert the ABSENCE of what you are about to build.** **(6) A REJECTED CANDIDATE'S RECORD IS WORTH IMPROVING EVEN WHEN YOU DO NOT PICK IT.** The `CF-76-1` re-census found a **SECOND matcher with the same bug** (`route_match_matches`, `crates/envoy-filter/src/jwt_authn.rs:173-186`), **THREE** unshared query-strip implementations already in-tree, that **`plan_redirect` is already query-strip-correct** (phase 76 pre-paid part of the fix), and that the record's "~4 probes" is an UNDER-COUNT (8-12, ≈900-1100 net LoC, because the two NON-REGRESSION witnesses need an access-log-observing driver). **The standing trap for whoever takes it: fix `route_matches`' ARGUMENT, never mutate `req.path`** — that field feeds the access log, the forwarded upstream target, `plan_redirect` and jwt_authn's `www-authenticate` realm, and NO current test would catch the damage. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-6 CLOSE-OUT — four findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A CLOSE-OUT THAT FLIPS A PARENT ROW MUST ASSERT EACH ROW'S OWN EXPECTED STATUS, NOT ONE SHARED VALUE.** This close-out flipped TWO rows from DIFFERENT starting statuses — `76.2` from `planned` and parent `76` from `in-progress`. A single shared `expect` would have silently skipped one row or aborted after mutating the other. **MEASURED result: `git diff --numstat` exactly `2 2`, a cell-by-cell compare showing f1/f2/f3/f5/f6 SAME on both rows, and the census moving `105 done / 1 in-progress / 1 planned` → `107 done`.** **Assert per-row, and compare cells rather than trusting the join.** **(2) THE LEDGER'S OWN WARNING ABOUT INHERITED LINE NUMBERS PAID OFF IMMEDIATELY.** The previous session's token sweep keyed on the inherited doctrine-bullet line number `128`, swept a BLANK line, and reported a false `109 → 0` total loss. This session located every sweep target BY TEXT (`awk '$0==H'` whole-line equality for the archive headers, an `.index()` on a distinctive substring for the traps-line boundary) and **verified all four top-section archive headers resolve to EXACTLY ONE line each BEFORE any write**, so a miss would abort before mutating. **A close-out RETIRES the active-phase Notes subsection entirely, so its downward shift is larger than a state advance's — never carry a line number across a session.** **(3) THE TRAPS LINE WAS REWRITTEN BY SPLITTING AT A TEXT BOUNDARY, WHICH MAKES THE ADR-0160 RETENTION CHECK STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN HOPEFUL.** Only the leading STATE-specific preamble (MEASURED **1604** of **62510** characters) was replaced; the enduring tail (**60906** characters, from the `[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2)` marker onward) was carried across BYTE-IDENTICALLY by construction. **A token sweep still ran and is still the gate — but a rewrite that preserves a measured byte-range cannot lose an enduring trap by accident.** **(4) A CLOSE-OUT ADDS NO ADR AND NO `### ` NOTES SUBSECTION, AND BOTH ARE MEASURED PRECEDENTS RATHER THAN OMISSIONS.** The 75.1 and 76.1 close-outs both landed ADR-less; the Notes subsection is RETIRED to the archive behind a `> Historical …` breadcrumb, not superseded in place. **Writing either one breaks the next session's checks** — an unexpected `### ` subsection makes the heading-structure check fail, and a gratuitous ADR moves the head the next session re-derives. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2) — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION.]** **(1) A FRESH REVIEWER RE-DERIVES THE PRIOR ROUND'S FINDINGS, AND THE ONLY GUARD IS READING THE PRIOR REVIEW.** THREE of five read-only dimensions surfaced round-1 items as if new — **M-7, M-9, N-4, N-5, N-8, N-9** — and TWO of them graded a banked Minor as an **ISSUE**. Nothing about a subagent's severity is trustworthy on this axis, because the subagent cannot know what was already banked. **Read the prior `REVIEW.md` before grading anything, and record every re-derived finding as STATUS rather than re-issuing it** (`REVIEW-2.md` §7 exists precisely for this). **(2) INDEPENDENT CONVERGENCE BY TWO DIMENSIONS ON AN UNPROMPTED FINDING IS WORTH MORE THAN EITHER REPORT.** M2-2 (`port_redirect` has no differential witness) was reached by one dimension censusing probes against routes and by another hand-executing a `strip_port` deletion against all 19 probes. Neither was asked for it. **Weight a finding by how many independent routes reached it, not by the confidence of the report.** **(3) A FIX THAT RE-ANCHORS AN ARTIFACT MUST RE-SWEEP THE PROSE THAT JUSTIFIED THE OLD ONE.** The M-2 fix re-anchored `q02` onto its own `/q2-hostport` route and carried forward the justification "q02 and r01 agree on the expected `location`" — TRUE of the original `/a-host` Q2, FALSE of the shipped one, and now wrong in THREE documents; `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` refutes itself nine lines apart (`:3018` vs `:3025`). The scheduled next widening (`regex_rewrite`, a declared non-goal at `SPEC.md:477`) adds a third `return Err` inside `validate_redirect_oneofs` in `bootstrap.rs`, whose doc carries no reciprocal warning — reproducing I-1 exactly. **Put the forcing-function warning on the file that will be EDITED, not on the file that will BREAK.** **(5) A LESSON PARAGRAPH CAN CONTRADICT ITSELF WITH ITS OWN NUMBERS.** `PROGRESS.md:2535` states the fixture carries "14×301, 2×302" — that is the **MUTATED** tree's census, captured while `q02`'s `expected_status` was flipped 301→302 for a negative control; the shipped fixture is **15×301, 1×302**. Pinned in a dedicated test instead — same coverage, guard intact, table's authority uncompromised, deviation RECORDED (`PROGRESS.md` §R3.7) rather than silently taken. **(5) WHEN A GUARD FIRES CORRECTLY ON A REAL DEFECT, EXTEND WHAT IT GUARDS — DO NOT REMOVE THE GUARD.** The tempting reading of I-1 is "`unreachable!()` was the bug, delete it". It was not: the bug was a WIDENED PRODUCER with an UNEXTENDED CONSUMER. The arm stays; its comment now says **six** and carries the cross-crate warning. **And the general rule that produced I-1 in the first place: when a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not tell you, because `unreachable!()` compiles clean.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-5 CODE REVIEW — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION, not quoted from a subagent.]** **(1) WIDENING A FUNCTION'S RETURNABLE ERROR SET IS A CROSS-CRATE CHANGE, AND `unreachable!()` IS WHERE IT LANDS.** Task 8 added a `validate_redirect_oneofs` call inside `reparse_and_select_route_config` (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs:159`), so that function can now return `RedirectPathRewriteConflict`/`RedirectSchemeRewriteConflict`. Its SOLE production caller (`crates/envoy-http1/src/rds_watcher.rs:184`) classifies exactly FOUR variants and ends `other => unreachable!(…)` (`:216-222`) — and the comment at `:211-215` states the invariant the phase broke VERBATIM. `Cargo.toml:42` is `panic = "abort"`, so the reload ABORTS THE PROCESS. **`unreachable!()` compiles clean, so gate (e) is structurally blind to it; only a `reload()`-LEVEL test could have caught it, and all four existing ones test other variants.** **When a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not.** **(2) A CONTRACT THAT DISCLAIMS A CELL AND THEN CLAIMS IT IS TESTED IS WORSE THAN SILENCE.** `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md:3122-3124` correctly labels §F items 7/8 as CHOICES rather than measurements, then says they are "pinned by in-process tests". **MEASURED FALSE for both**: all eight test call sites of `plan_redirect` pass `Some(...)`, and the 22-row table CANNOT express `None` because its `cell()` constructor hard-wires `prefix: Some(prefix)` (`hcm.rs:10484`) and all 22 rows go through it (0 direct `Cell {` literals). **A `Option` FIELD ON A TEST-TABLE STRUCT PROVES NOTHING IF THE CONSTRUCTOR CAN ONLY PRODUCE `Some` — check the constructor, not the type.** **(3) A PROBE PAIR NAMED AS A WITNESS IN A DOC COMMENT MUST BE RE-DERIVED, NOT READ.** `tests/differential/tests/route_redirect_action.rs:9-10` claims `q01` vs `r01` witnesses the `host_redirect` port-DROP. Re-deriving first-match-wins selection over the parsed config: **9** routes set `host_redirect`, **all 9** are probed with an UNPORTED Host, and the only two ported probes hit `https_redirect`/`{}` routes — so **0 of 18** probes can witness it, on the rule SPEC §2.4(b) itself calls the one most likely to be got wrong. **The cell IS pinned in-process (`hcm.rs:10671-10679`); it is UNCOMPARED, not unpinned — say which.** **(4) A SUBAGENT'S LINE NUMBERS DRIFT EVEN WHEN ITS REASONING IS RIGHT.** One dimension's `hcm.rs` citations were consistently **~12 lines high** (`:2331` for a line at `:2319`) while every one of its CONCLUSIONS held. **Re-read every citation; do not inherit a line number from a review either.** **(5) AN UNVERIFIED UPSTREAM HYPOTHESIS MUST NOT BE GRADED AS A FINDING.** A dimension proposed that upstream strips a DEFAULT port (`:80`/`:443`) on a scheme change, explicitly labelling it *"a hypothesis from upstream implementation shape, not from anything on disk"*. It is recorded in `REVIEW.md` §5 as an UNGRADED hypothesis with the two probes that would settle it — never as a defect. **D-3.3: the contract is the contract; you do not read upstream source to decide what equivalence means.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-4 VERIFICATION — five findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A DOCUMENTED HOST STALL DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND THAT ABSENCE IS ITSELF A MEASUREMENT.** The state-3 session recorded — and the handoff instructed state 4 to budget for — a hard stall on `xds_rds_hot_reload` that forced its `-p differential` sweep to be killed after ~11 minutes and left gate (b) unadjudicated. **THREE consecutive whole-workspace sweeps completed in ~5½ minutes each with all 163 binaries reporting, and `xds_rds_hot_reload` passes in isolation in 1.98 s.** An environmental stall is not a property of the TREE. **Re-measure an inherited time budget before spending it, and do not read a stall's absence as a different tree.** **(2) THE ONE RED SITTING ON THE PHASE'S OWN SURFACE IS THE ONE WORTH CHASING.** Seven of the eight REDs were trivially off-surface; `xds_rds_hot_reload_fixture` was NOT — Task 8 rewrote exactly that file's validation path (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs`, `if let` → exhaustive `match`). Disbelieve a zero.** **(5) A LANDED PLAN'S TEST-COUNT PREDICTION IS NOT A BASELINE — THE DIFF IS.** `76.2/PLAN.md` §6 predicted `passed≈2168` from "~30 new tests"; the measured `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` attribute delta is **+11 / −0**, and both identities close exactly on 11 (`162 + 1 = 163` binaries, `2137 + 11 = 2148` passed). The gap is the table-driven 22-cell design the plan itself chose. **Do NOT read `2148` against `2168` as "tests were lost".** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-3 IMPLEMENTATION — eight findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A PLAN'S LITERAL RUST CAN BE PRE-FLIGHTED AND STILL BROKEN — THREE DEFECTS IN ONE PLAN.** `PLAN.md` §2 claimed Tasks 1-5/8/9 passed `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` in a scratch worktree, and THREE literals still failed: T3-3's `Some("/é"[..2].into())` **panics in the test itself** (`"/é"` is 3 bytes, so byte index 2 is not a char boundary) and never reaches the function under test; T3-2's assert message `"a bare redirect{} rewrites nothing"` **does not compile** (`assert_eq!`'s third arg is a FORMAT STRING, so the bare `{}` is a positional placeholder); and T7-1's `HttpVersion::Http2` **does not exist** (the enum has exactly `Http10` and `Http11`). **THE ROOT CAUSE IS GENERAL: `fmt` and `clippy` DO NOT EXECUTE TESTS, and the pre-flight RAN only 2 of the new tests** — so a runtime panic in a third was invisible to it, and a block that never compiled cannot have passed the lint it was claimed to pass. **Treat a pre-flight's own claim as a CLAIM; transcribe verbatim, then COMPILE AND RUN.** **(2) A PER-TASK LINT GATE CAN BE UNACHIEVABLE UNDER THE PLAN'S OWN TASK SPLIT.** `PLAN.md`'s Global Constraint says `clippy -D warnings` must be clean at EVERY task boundary; measured, Tasks 2/3/4 each add a NON-TEST item whose only NON-TEST consumer is Task 5, so each boundary is `unused import` / `never constructed` / `never used` → **exit 101**. It does not — the call compiles, and the RED is the pure behavioural `left: 501, right: 301`, which is BETTER evidence. **Do not treat a plan's predicted failure MODE as a checkable fact.** **(4) `envoy-bin` HAS NO `--mode` FLAG.** `PLAN.md` Task 10's `--mode validate` exits **2** with `unknown argument: --mode`; `crates/envoy-bin/src/argv.rs:27-29` accepts EXACTLY `-c <path>` or `--config-path <path>` (clap is deliberately avoided per D-3.2). Validate instead by substituting `{{PORT}}` and booting under `timeout`: exit **124** (still running) with zero errors proves the config parses AND the listener binds — strictly stronger. **(5) THE STRONGEST SEAM EVIDENCE IS A CROSS-CRATE MUTATION.** Mutating `plan_redirect` in **`crates/envoy-http1`** turned an **`crates/envoy-http2`** test RED (`left: Some("http://envoy-rust.test/a-host")`). That does not merely assert H2 reaches the arm — it PROVES H2's answer is COMPUTED BY the H1 arm. **When a claim is "one implementation serves two consumers", mutate the implementation and watch the OTHER consumer fail.** **(6) A FULL LOCAL `-p differential` SWEEP STALLS ON `xds_rds_hot_reload` ON THIS HOST** (virtiofs, no inotify). ':(exclude)docs/'`, +1334/−69) against the plan's ≈1202 code-only projection — **+5%**, versus `76.1`'s **+50%**. The table-driven 22-cell design held (it was NOT expanded into 22 `#[test]` fns), §6.1's mid-execution trigger never fired, and **no split was needed**. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-2 PLAN-WRITE — six findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A SPLIT SIBLING'S LANDING STALE-DATES THE OTHER SPEC, AND THE DRIFT IS NOT UNIFORM.** `76.2/SPEC.md` was written at `f438cb9`, before `76.1`. A one-direction green proves nothing; the negative arm is what shows the file is invisible. **⚠ THE TEST-BINARY COUNT IS FORM-DEPENDENT WHILE `passed + failed` IS NOT.** `--all-targets` = 149 binaries, plain = 165, gap = 16 doc-test harnesses contributing `passed=0 failed=0`. Assert the IDENTITY, and state which form produced the binary count. **⚠ A `cargo fuzz run` CENSUS OVER `ci.yml` RETURNS A BELIEVABLE ZERO** — the workflow invokes `cargo +nightly fuzz run` because the workspace pins stable; grep `fuzz run`, not `cargo fuzz run`. **[NEW AT THE `110.1` §5 STATE-3 IMPLEMENTATION]** **⚠ A PLAN'S OWN CODE CAN FAIL A PLAN'S OWN TEST — RUN IT, DO NOT ASSUME IT.** `110.1/PLAN.md` specified `transform_is_idempotent` AND an `apply_grpc_local_reply` that fails it: the transform EMITS four headers it owns but DROPS only two on input, so a second application preserved `grpc-status`/`grpc-message` as pass-throughs and then appended a SECOND `grpc-status` carrying the default `2`, because the mapped code is recomputed from the already-rewritten `200`. **Dropping the other two is NOT the fix** — the code would still be recomputed from `200`. The fix is an EARLY RETURN on a sentinel the transform always emits. **⚠ A MUTATION `sed` WHOSE TARGET STRING APPEARS IN BOTH THE IMPLEMENTATION AND THE TEST MUTATES BOTH, AND RETURNS A GREEN THAT READS AS "VACUOUS TESTS".** MEASURED: the PLAN's Task-3 anchor `if (0x20..=0x7D).contains(&byte) && byte != b'%' {` occurs TWICE — the second occurrence is inside the test that RECOMPUTES the predicate to build its expectation, so `sed -i` moves the expectation in lockstep with the implementation and NOTHING is actually mutated. **ALWAYS assert the occurrence COUNT before mutating** (a `python` guard asserting `count == 1` is what caught it) and anchor on implementation-only context. **⚠ A SEAM'S PLACEMENT MUTATION IS THE ONLY THING THAT PROVES PLACEMENT.** Moving the transform from before the log locals to the wire write REDs **exactly the two access-log/stats witnesses and leaves the other 15 wire-shape tests GREEN** — they are structurally blind to it. **⚠ A LONG BACKGROUND `cargo test --workspace` HOLDS THE CARGO LOCK AND WILL SILENTLY REVERT A CONCURRENT `cargo update`.** MEASURED this session: a `Cargo.lock` h2 bump applied, `git diff` confirmed it, and the still-running sweep put it back — the re-run of `deny` then reported the OLD version and looked like the bump had failed. Serialize `cargo` mutations against any running sweep. **⚠ `cargo deny check` CAN RED ON A NEWLY-PUBLISHED ADVISORY THAT PREDATES YOUR WORK.** Prove it pre-existing BY EXPERIMENT — check the session BASE out in a scratch worktree and reproduce the red there — never by inferring it from "I didn't touch `Cargo.lock`". **⚠ A PLAN'S TEST-HELPER NAMES MAY BE ITS OWN INVENTIONS.** `110.1/PLAN.md` said so explicitly; five of its six Task-6 builders already existed under other names and one API it called (`log.records()`) does not exist at all. GREP FIRST, and report what you reused versus wrote. **[NEW AT THE SUB-PHASE-110.1 §5 STATE-2 PLAN-WRITE — six traps, every one MEASURED AT THIS COMMIT.]** **(1) A SEAM'S CORRECT PLACEMENT IS NOT ALWAYS THE WIRE WRITE — PROBE THE OBSERVABILITY SIDE TOO.** Both the landed `110.1/SPEC.md` (§1.5, D5) and the handoff located the gRPC local-reply seam at the H1 wire funnels (`hcm.rs:1457`/`:1468`). MEASURED, and that placement is byte-correct on the wire and SILENTLY WRONG everywhere else: upstream's access log records `%RESPONSE_CODE%` = **200** and `%BYTES_SENT%` = **0** for a transformed reply, and the per-class counter ticks `downstream_rq_2xx` — NOT the original status's class (probed with a `FileAccessLog` to `/dev/stdout` read back through `docker logs`, plus admin `/stats`: 4 requests → `2xx: 2`, `4xx: 1`, `5xx: 1`, `completed: 4`). envoy-rust derives BOTH from `response_status_for_log`/`response_body_len` at `hcm.rs:1447-1448`, so the transform must go BEFORE those, not at the write. `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` stays UNCHANGED. **A wire-shape test cannot see this class of bug — it needs its own witness, and ADR-0179 DECISION 2 records why.** **(2) A LANDED SPEC'S FAMILY LIST IS A CENSUS, AND THIS ONE WAS INCOMPLETE.** `110.1/SPEC.md` §1.5 enumerates the local-reply family and OMITS the two filter-generated arms in `serve_connection` (`SynthFromDecode` `hcm.rs:1391`, encode-side `StopAndSend` `:1423`). MEASURED with an `envoy.filters.http.rbac` deny-all chain: upstream DOES transform them (`200` + `grpc-status: 7` + `grpc-message: RBAC: access denied` vs a `403` + `text/plain` control). Shipping the SPEC's literal list would have instantiated the ADR-0049 partially-covered-family class the seam design exists to avoid. **Enumerate the family from the CODE, then check the SPEC against it — not the other way round.** **(3) PREFER A PREDICATE THAT FAILS SAFE OVER ONE THAT ENUMERATES.** The locality bit is `outgoing_local`, defaulting to **true** and cleared ONLY by `outgoing_local = !completing_upstream_response` at the proxy arm — reusing `AttemptResult.upstream_response`, a bit the tree ALREADY carries and documents (`hcm.rs:368-370`). A synth arm added later is covered BY OMISSION rather than skipped by omission. The `BuildOutcome::Synth`-only gate the SPEC contemplates would have missed the `run_attempt`/pool synths, the request-budget overflow, the chunked-501 and both filter arms. **(4) WHEN A RULE IS DERIVED FROM ONE INSTANCE, FIND A SECOND INSTANCE.** §1.4's order rule was banked from `location` alone. A circuit-breaker overflow probe (`max_connections: 0`) showed `x-envoy-overloaded: true` ALSO survives IN ITS ORIGINAL POSITION — the pass-through rule is GENERAL, not a `location` special case. The generalized rule (pass-throughs in original relative order; then `content-type`, `grpc-status`, `[grpc-message]`; then `date`, `server`, `connection`; then `content-length: 0`) reproduces all THREE measured cases exactly. **Order remains a UNIT-TEST concern only — `diff_headers` never reads it.** **(5) A FEATURE-GATED MODULE IS INVISIBLE TO `cargo test --workspace`.** `crates/envoy-http1/src/uring.rs` is gated at `lib.rs:24-25` behind the `uring` feature (`Cargo.toml:27-28`) and contains **NO `#[cfg(test)]` and NO `#[test]` at all**. Only `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` compiles it. Its seam therefore gets its coverage STRUCTURALLY — the transform lives INSIDE `write_owned` (all four call sites are synth; the proxied path uses `write_head_body` at `:376`) — and the absence of a test is BANKED as **CF-110-5** rather than papered over. **(6) A NEW PRE-EXISTING DIVERGENCE, BANKED AS CF-110-4:** upstream's own NON-gRPC local-reply header order is `[pass-through,] content-length, content-type, date, server, connection`, whereas envoy-rust's `synth_with` emits `server, date, content-length, content-type, connection`. ORDER-ONLY, invisible to `diff_headers`, PRE-EXISTING and gRPC-ORTHOGONAL — **not a licence to touch `synth_with`.** Together with CF-110-3 (upstream's `location` on a `201`/`3xx` `direct_response`) these are the two divergences `110.2`'s fixture must route around. **[NEW AT THE PHASE-110 §5 STATE-2 SPLIT — six traps, every one MEASURED AT THIS COMMIT.]** **(1) A SPEC's "structural boundary" claim is a CENSUS, and this one was FALSE.** The parent `110/SPEC.md` §3 D6 asserted that H1 and H2 share only the route RESOLVER, so scoping to H1 was "a real boundary rather than a hopeful one". **MEASURED FALSE:** `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:518` calls **`envoy_http1::build_response`**, which reaches `synth_direct_response`/`synth_400`/`synth_404`/`synth_redirect` → `synth_with`, and `envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:2127-2128` documents it ("ONE arm serves BOTH codecs"). H2 owns its own synthesisers for UPSTREAM-FAILURE paths ONLY. **The general rule: when a SPEC says two subsystems are isolated, grep the CALL EDGE, not the type names.** **(2) A CODE-SHAPE claim can be right about the NAMES and wrong about the TIERS.** The inherited "`synth_with` has SEVEN callers" list conflated direct callers with the whole synth family: there are **FOUR** direct call sites, and `synth_400`/`synth_404`/`synth_501` are depth-2 wrappers over `synth_status`. `grep -rn 'synth_with' crates/` returns 7 hits of which only 4 are CALLS — the rest are the definition and two doc mentions. **Count call sites, not grep hits.** **(3) A DOC COMMENT'S JUSTIFICATION CAN BE STALE EVEN WHEN ITS ADVICE IS GOOD.** `synth_with`'s doc block says "Header ORDER is load-bearing — the differential harness byte-compares against upstream Envoy." **The harness does NOT byte-compare:** `diff_headers` builds a `BTreeSet` of LOWER-CASED header NAMES, compares the SETS, then compares VALUES for every name outside the 3-entry `HEADER_ALLOW_LIST`. **Order is never read.** Matching upstream's order is still correct practice (unit tests pin it), but a wrong order fails a UNIT test, not a fixture — do not price it as a differential risk. **(4) A MEASURED RULE CAN BE WRONG AT EXACTLY ONE BOUNDARY BYTE.** The parent SPEC's `grpc-message` rule ("`0x20` through `0x7E` pass through except `%`") is FALSE: **`~` (0x7E) IS ESCAPED to `%7E`**. The corrected rule is pass-through iff **`0x20..=0x7D` AND not `%`**. The parent had measured the INTERIOR of the range and inferred the endpoints. **When a rule is stated as a RANGE, probe BOTH endpoints explicitly.** **(5) PAIRED CONTROLS FIND DIVERGENCES THAT ARE NOT YOUR SUBJECT.** Probing every mapping cell WITH and WITHOUT the gRPC content-type surfaced an unrelated, PRE-EXISTING divergence: upstream emits `location: <scheme>://<authority><path>` on a `direct_response` whose status is **`201` or `3xx`**, in BOTH directions; envoy-rust does not. Banked as the reassigned **CF-110-3**, and it forces `110.2`'s fixture to avoid those statuses — without the control column that fixture would have landed RED for a reason unrelated to its subject. **(6) A HEADER-DICT CLIENT DESTROYS THE EVIDENCE YOU CAME FOR.** V-2 (ORDER) and V-10 (CASE) are both unanswerable through `curl`-style or dict-based clients. Probe with a **RAW SOCKET**, one connection per probe, and parse the response head yourself — but remember your own parser is a hazard too: an `lstrip()` on field values silently ate the leading spaces of an encoding probe and briefly looked like an Envoy rule. **Also: an HCM with no `http_filters` block ACCEPTS the config and then HANGS every request** — a probe harness that times out with zero bytes is usually missing the router filter, not evidence about the surface under test. **[NEW AT THE PHASE-110 §5 STATE-0/1 PICK — five traps, every one MEASURED AT THIS COMMIT.]** **(1) A STANDING, REPEATEDLY-AFFIRMED REJECTION CAN BE SOUND IN ITS REASONING AND STILL NOT REACH YOUR SLICE — CHECK ITS PREMISE AGAINST THE WIRE, NOT AGAINST ITS RESTATEMENTS.** ADR-0048 rejected the gRPC family as blocked on HTTP/2 trailer propagation; that verdict was re-affirmed roughly FIFTEEN times, most recently ADR-0171(b) and the ADR-0175 pick, and it is **still entirely correct for the gRPC DATA PATH**. It is inapplicable to gRPC-aware LOCAL REPLIES, and one probe settled it: the reply is `content-length: 0` over HTTP/1.1 with `grpc-status`/`grpc-message` as ordinary response HEADERS, and a bodiless response has NO TRAILER SECTION AT ALL. It is not: `BodyRule::JsonShape` parses both bodies through `serde_json`, and because `preserve_order` is enabled NOWHERE in the workspace, `serde_json::Map` is a `BTreeMap` that canonically key-sorts on re-serialization. **The fix was already in the harness; the temptation was to add an allow-list and weaken the assertion.** **(5) AN "ABSENCE" CAN BE PINNED BY A PASSING TEST, AND A PHASE THAT BUILDS THE ABSENT THING MUST SAY SO.** Four places assert "there is no runtime layer", one of them a test literally named `runtime_key_is_rtds_inert`. None becomes wrong when a `static_layer` store lands without RTDS or consumers — **but a reviewer meeting that test name inside a phase titled "runtime" will read a contradiction unless the SPEC pre-empts it.** **Grep for tests and docs that assert the ABSENCE of what you are about to build.** **(6) A REJECTED CANDIDATE'S RECORD IS WORTH IMPROVING EVEN WHEN YOU DO NOT PICK IT.** The `CF-76-1` re-census found a **SECOND matcher with the same bug** (`route_match_matches`, `crates/envoy-filter/src/jwt_authn.rs:173-186`), **THREE** unshared query-strip implementations already in-tree, that **`plan_redirect` is already query-strip-correct** (phase 76 pre-paid part of the fix), and that the record's "~4 probes" is an UNDER-COUNT (8-12, ≈900-1100 net LoC, because the two NON-REGRESSION witnesses need an access-log-observing driver). **The standing trap for whoever takes it: fix `route_matches`' ARGUMENT, never mutate `req.path`** — that field feeds the access log, the forwarded upstream target, `plan_redirect` and jwt_authn's `www-authenticate` realm, and NO current test would catch the damage. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-6 CLOSE-OUT — four findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A CLOSE-OUT THAT FLIPS A PARENT ROW MUST ASSERT EACH ROW'S OWN EXPECTED STATUS, NOT ONE SHARED VALUE.** This close-out flipped TWO rows from DIFFERENT starting statuses — `76.2` from `planned` and parent `76` from `in-progress`. A single shared `expect` would have silently skipped one row or aborted after mutating the other. **MEASURED result: `git diff --numstat` exactly `2 2`, a cell-by-cell compare showing f1/f2/f3/f5/f6 SAME on both rows, and the census moving `105 done / 1 in-progress / 1 planned` → `107 done`.** **Assert per-row, and compare cells rather than trusting the join.** **(2) THE LEDGER'S OWN WARNING ABOUT INHERITED LINE NUMBERS PAID OFF IMMEDIATELY.** The previous session's token sweep keyed on the inherited doctrine-bullet line number `128`, swept a BLANK line, and reported a false `109 → 0` total loss. This session located every sweep target BY TEXT (`awk '$0==H'` whole-line equality for the archive headers, an `.index()` on a distinctive substring for the traps-line boundary) and **verified all four top-section archive headers resolve to EXACTLY ONE line each BEFORE any write**, so a miss would abort before mutating. **A close-out RETIRES the active-phase Notes subsection entirely, so its downward shift is larger than a state advance's — never carry a line number across a session.** **(3) THE TRAPS LINE WAS REWRITTEN BY SPLITTING AT A TEXT BOUNDARY, WHICH MAKES THE ADR-0160 RETENTION CHECK STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN HOPEFUL.** Only the leading STATE-specific preamble (MEASURED **1604** of **62510** characters) was replaced; the enduring tail (**60906** characters, from the `[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2)` marker onward) was carried across BYTE-IDENTICALLY by construction. **A token sweep still ran and is still the gate — but a rewrite that preserves a measured byte-range cannot lose an enduring trap by accident.** **(4) A CLOSE-OUT ADDS NO ADR AND NO `### ` NOTES SUBSECTION, AND BOTH ARE MEASURED PRECEDENTS RATHER THAN OMISSIONS.** The 75.1 and 76.1 close-outs both landed ADR-less; the Notes subsection is RETIRED to the archive behind a `> Historical …` breadcrumb, not superseded in place. **Writing either one breaks the next session's checks** — an unexpected `### ` subsection makes the heading-structure check fail, and a gratuitous ADR moves the head the next session re-derives. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2) — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION.]** **(1) A FRESH REVIEWER RE-DERIVES THE PRIOR ROUND'S FINDINGS, AND THE ONLY GUARD IS READING THE PRIOR REVIEW.** THREE of five read-only dimensions surfaced round-1 items as if new — **M-7, M-9, N-4, N-5, N-8, N-9** — and TWO of them graded a banked Minor as an **ISSUE**. Nothing about a subagent's severity is trustworthy on this axis, because the subagent cannot know what was already banked. **Read the prior `REVIEW.md` before grading anything, and record every re-derived finding as STATUS rather than re-issuing it** (`REVIEW-2.md` §7 exists precisely for this). **(2) INDEPENDENT CONVERGENCE BY TWO DIMENSIONS ON AN UNPROMPTED FINDING IS WORTH MORE THAN EITHER REPORT.** M2-2 (`port_redirect` has no differential witness) was reached by one dimension censusing probes against routes and by another hand-executing a `strip_port` deletion against all 19 probes. Neither was asked for it. **Weight a finding by how many independent routes reached it, not by the confidence of the report.** **(3) A FIX THAT RE-ANCHORS AN ARTIFACT MUST RE-SWEEP THE PROSE THAT JUSTIFIED THE OLD ONE.** The M-2 fix re-anchored `q02` onto its own `/q2-hostport` route and carried forward the justification "q02 and r01 agree on the expected `location`" — TRUE of the original `/a-host` Q2, FALSE of the shipped one, and now wrong in THREE documents; `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` refutes itself nine lines apart (`:3018` vs `:3025`). The scheduled next widening (`regex_rewrite`, a declared non-goal at `SPEC.md:477`) adds a third `return Err` inside `validate_redirect_oneofs` in `bootstrap.rs`, whose doc carries no reciprocal warning — reproducing I-1 exactly. **Put the forcing-function warning on the file that will be EDITED, not on the file that will BREAK.** **(5) A LESSON PARAGRAPH CAN CONTRADICT ITSELF WITH ITS OWN NUMBERS.** `PROGRESS.md:2535` states the fixture carries "14×301, 2×302" — that is the **MUTATED** tree's census, captured while `q02`'s `expected_status` was flipped 301→302 for a negative control; the shipped fixture is **15×301, 1×302**. Pinned in a dedicated test instead — same coverage, guard intact, table's authority uncompromised, deviation RECORDED (`PROGRESS.md` §R3.7) rather than silently taken. **(5) WHEN A GUARD FIRES CORRECTLY ON A REAL DEFECT, EXTEND WHAT IT GUARDS — DO NOT REMOVE THE GUARD.** The tempting reading of I-1 is "`unreachable!()` was the bug, delete it". It was not: the bug was a WIDENED PRODUCER with an UNEXTENDED CONSUMER. The arm stays; its comment now says **six** and carries the cross-crate warning. **And the general rule that produced I-1 in the first place: when a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not tell you, because `unreachable!()` compiles clean.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-5 CODE REVIEW — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION, not quoted from a subagent.]** **(1) WIDENING A FUNCTION'S RETURNABLE ERROR SET IS A CROSS-CRATE CHANGE, AND `unreachable!()` IS WHERE IT LANDS.** Task 8 added a `validate_redirect_oneofs` call inside `reparse_and_select_route_config` (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs:159`), so that function can now return `RedirectPathRewriteConflict`/`RedirectSchemeRewriteConflict`. Its SOLE production caller (`crates/envoy-http1/src/rds_watcher.rs:184`) classifies exactly FOUR variants and ends `other => unreachable!(…)` (`:216-222`) — and the comment at `:211-215` states the invariant the phase broke VERBATIM. `Cargo.toml:42` is `panic = "abort"`, so the reload ABORTS THE PROCESS. **`unreachable!()` compiles clean, so gate (e) is structurally blind to it; only a `reload()`-LEVEL test could have caught it, and all four existing ones test other variants.** **When a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not.** **(2) A CONTRACT THAT DISCLAIMS A CELL AND THEN CLAIMS IT IS TESTED IS WORSE THAN SILENCE.** `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md:3122-3124` correctly labels §F items 7/8 as CHOICES rather than measurements, then says they are "pinned by in-process tests". **MEASURED FALSE for both**: all eight test call sites of `plan_redirect` pass `Some(...)`, and the 22-row table CANNOT express `None` because its `cell()` constructor hard-wires `prefix: Some(prefix)` (`hcm.rs:10484`) and all 22 rows go through it (0 direct `Cell {` literals). **A `Option` FIELD ON A TEST-TABLE STRUCT PROVES NOTHING IF THE CONSTRUCTOR CAN ONLY PRODUCE `Some` — check the constructor, not the type.** **(3) A PROBE PAIR NAMED AS A WITNESS IN A DOC COMMENT MUST BE RE-DERIVED, NOT READ.** `tests/differential/tests/route_redirect_action.rs:9-10` claims `q01` vs `r01` witnesses the `host_redirect` port-DROP. Re-deriving first-match-wins selection over the parsed config: **9** routes set `host_redirect`, **all 9** are probed with an UNPORTED Host, and the only two ported probes hit `https_redirect`/`{}` routes — so **0 of 18** probes can witness it, on the rule SPEC §2.4(b) itself calls the one most likely to be got wrong. **The cell IS pinned in-process (`hcm.rs:10671-10679`); it is UNCOMPARED, not unpinned — say which.** **(4) A SUBAGENT'S LINE NUMBERS DRIFT EVEN WHEN ITS REASONING IS RIGHT.** One dimension's `hcm.rs` citations were consistently **~12 lines high** (`:2331` for a line at `:2319`) while every one of its CONCLUSIONS held. **Re-read every citation; do not inherit a line number from a review either.** **(5) AN UNVERIFIED UPSTREAM HYPOTHESIS MUST NOT BE GRADED AS A FINDING.** A dimension proposed that upstream strips a DEFAULT port (`:80`/`:443`) on a scheme change, explicitly labelling it *"a hypothesis from upstream implementation shape, not from anything on disk"*. It is recorded in `REVIEW.md` §5 as an UNGRADED hypothesis with the two probes that would settle it — never as a defect. **D-3.3: the contract is the contract; you do not read upstream source to decide what equivalence means.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-4 VERIFICATION — five findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A DOCUMENTED HOST STALL DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND THAT ABSENCE IS ITSELF A MEASUREMENT.** The state-3 session recorded — and the handoff instructed state 4 to budget for — a hard stall on `xds_rds_hot_reload` that forced its `-p differential` sweep to be killed after ~11 minutes and left gate (b) unadjudicated. **THREE consecutive whole-workspace sweeps completed in ~5½ minutes each with all 163 binaries reporting, and `xds_rds_hot_reload` passes in isolation in 1.98 s.** An environmental stall is not a property of the TREE. **Re-measure an inherited time budget before spending it, and do not read a stall's absence as a different tree.** **(2) THE ONE RED SITTING ON THE PHASE'S OWN SURFACE IS THE ONE WORTH CHASING.** Seven of the eight REDs were trivially off-surface; `xds_rds_hot_reload_fixture` was NOT — Task 8 rewrote exactly that file's validation path (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs`, `if let` → exhaustive `match`). Disbelieve a zero.** **(5) A LANDED PLAN'S TEST-COUNT PREDICTION IS NOT A BASELINE — THE DIFF IS.** `76.2/PLAN.md` §6 predicted `passed≈2168` from "~30 new tests"; the measured `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` attribute delta is **+11 / −0**, and both identities close exactly on 11 (`162 + 1 = 163` binaries, `2137 + 11 = 2148` passed). The gap is the table-driven 22-cell design the plan itself chose. **Do NOT read `2148` against `2168` as "tests were lost".** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-3 IMPLEMENTATION — eight findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A PLAN'S LITERAL RUST CAN BE PRE-FLIGHTED AND STILL BROKEN — THREE DEFECTS IN ONE PLAN.** `PLAN.md` §2 claimed Tasks 1-5/8/9 passed `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` in a scratch worktree, and THREE literals still failed: T3-3's `Some("/é"[..2].into())` **panics in the test itself** (`"/é"` is 3 bytes, so byte index 2 is not a char boundary) and never reaches the function under test; T3-2's assert message `"a bare redirect{} rewrites nothing"` **does not compile** (`assert_eq!`'s third arg is a FORMAT STRING, so the bare `{}` is a positional placeholder); and T7-1's `HttpVersion::Http2` **does not exist** (the enum has exactly `Http10` and `Http11`). **THE ROOT CAUSE IS GENERAL: `fmt` and `clippy` DO NOT EXECUTE TESTS, and the pre-flight RAN only 2 of the new tests** — so a runtime panic in a third was invisible to it, and a block that never compiled cannot have passed the lint it was claimed to pass. **Treat a pre-flight's own claim as a CLAIM; transcribe verbatim, then COMPILE AND RUN.** **(2) A PER-TASK LINT GATE CAN BE UNACHIEVABLE UNDER THE PLAN'S OWN TASK SPLIT.** `PLAN.md`'s Global Constraint says `clippy -D warnings` must be clean at EVERY task boundary; measured, Tasks 2/3/4 each add a NON-TEST item whose only NON-TEST consumer is Task 5, so each boundary is `unused import` / `never constructed` / `never used` → **exit 101**. It does not — the call compiles, and the RED is the pure behavioural `left: 501, right: 301`, which is BETTER evidence. **Do not treat a plan's predicted failure MODE as a checkable fact.** **(4) `envoy-bin` HAS NO `--mode` FLAG.** `PLAN.md` Task 10's `--mode validate` exits **2** with `unknown argument: --mode`; `crates/envoy-bin/src/argv.rs:27-29` accepts EXACTLY `-c <path>` or `--config-path <path>` (clap is deliberately avoided per D-3.2). Validate instead by substituting `{{PORT}}` and booting under `timeout`: exit **124** (still running) with zero errors proves the config parses AND the listener binds — strictly stronger. **(5) THE STRONGEST SEAM EVIDENCE IS A CROSS-CRATE MUTATION.** Mutating `plan_redirect` in **`crates/envoy-http1`** turned an **`crates/envoy-http2`** test RED (`left: Some("http://envoy-rust.test/a-host")`). That does not merely assert H2 reaches the arm — it PROVES H2's answer is COMPUTED BY the H1 arm. **When a claim is "one implementation serves two consumers", mutate the implementation and watch the OTHER consumer fail.** **(6) A FULL LOCAL `-p differential` SWEEP STALLS ON `xds_rds_hot_reload` ON THIS HOST** (virtiofs, no inotify). ':(exclude)docs/'`, +1334/−69) against the plan's ≈1202 code-only projection — **+5%**, versus `76.1`'s **+50%**. The table-driven 22-cell design held (it was NOT expanded into 22 `#[test]` fns), §6.1's mid-execution trigger never fired, and **no split was needed**. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-2 PLAN-WRITE — six findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A SPLIT SIBLING'S LANDING STALE-DATES THE OTHER SPEC, AND THE DRIFT IS NOT UNIFORM.** `76.2/SPEC.md` was written at `f438cb9`, before `76.1`. MEASURED with an `envoy.filters.http.rbac` deny-all chain: upstream DOES transform them (`200` + `grpc-status: 7` + `grpc-message: RBAC: access denied` vs a `403` + `text/plain` control). Shipping the SPEC's literal list would have instantiated the ADR-0049 partially-covered-family class the seam design exists to avoid. **Enumerate the family from the CODE, then check the SPEC against it — not the other way round.** **(3) PREFER A PREDICATE THAT FAILS SAFE OVER ONE THAT ENUMERATES.** The locality bit is `outgoing_local`, defaulting to **true** and cleared ONLY by `outgoing_local = !completing_upstream_response` at the proxy arm — reusing `AttemptResult.upstream_response`, a bit the tree ALREADY carries and documents (`hcm.rs:368-370`). A synth arm added later is covered BY OMISSION rather than skipped by omission. The `BuildOutcome::Synth`-only gate the SPEC contemplates would have missed the `run_attempt`/pool synths, the request-budget overflow, the chunked-501 and both filter arms. **(4) WHEN A RULE IS DERIVED FROM ONE INSTANCE, FIND A SECOND INSTANCE.** §1.4's order rule was banked from `location` alone. A circuit-breaker overflow probe (`max_connections: 0`) showed `x-envoy-overloaded: true` ALSO survives IN ITS ORIGINAL POSITION — the pass-through rule is GENERAL, not a `location` special case. The generalized rule (pass-throughs in original relative order; then `content-type`, `grpc-status`, `[grpc-message]`; then `date`, `server`, `connection`; then `content-length: 0`) reproduces all THREE measured cases exactly. **Order remains a UNIT-TEST concern only — `diff_headers` never reads it.** **(5) A FEATURE-GATED MODULE IS INVISIBLE TO `cargo test --workspace`.** `crates/envoy-http1/src/uring.rs` is gated at `lib.rs:24-25` behind the `uring` feature (`Cargo.toml:27-28`) and contains **NO `#[cfg(test)]` and NO `#[test]` at all**. Only `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` compiles it. Its seam therefore gets its coverage STRUCTURALLY — the transform lives INSIDE `write_owned` (all four call sites are synth; the proxied path uses `write_head_body` at `:376`) — and the absence of a test is BANKED as **CF-110-5** rather than papered over. **(6) A NEW PRE-EXISTING DIVERGENCE, BANKED AS CF-110-4:** upstream's own NON-gRPC local-reply header order is `[pass-through,] content-length, content-type, date, server, connection`, whereas envoy-rust's `synth_with` emits `server, date, content-length, content-type, connection`. ORDER-ONLY, invisible to `diff_headers`, PRE-EXISTING and gRPC-ORTHOGONAL — **not a licence to touch `synth_with`.** Together with CF-110-3 (upstream's `location` on a `201`/`3xx` `direct_response`) these are the two divergences `110.2`'s fixture must route around. **[NEW AT THE PHASE-110 §5 STATE-2 SPLIT — six traps, every one MEASURED AT THIS COMMIT.]** **(1) A SPEC's "structural boundary" claim is a CENSUS, and this one was FALSE.** The parent `110/SPEC.md` §3 D6 asserted that H1 and H2 share only the route RESOLVER, so scoping to H1 was "a real boundary rather than a hopeful one". **MEASURED FALSE:** `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:518` calls **`envoy_http1::build_response`**, which reaches `synth_direct_response`/`synth_400`/`synth_404`/`synth_redirect` → `synth_with`, and `envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:2127-2128` documents it ("ONE arm serves BOTH codecs"). H2 owns its own synthesisers for UPSTREAM-FAILURE paths ONLY. **The general rule: when a SPEC says two subsystems are isolated, grep the CALL EDGE, not the type names.** **(2) A CODE-SHAPE claim can be right about the NAMES and wrong about the TIERS.** The inherited "`synth_with` has SEVEN callers" list conflated direct callers with the whole synth family: there are **FOUR** direct call sites, and `synth_400`/`synth_404`/`synth_501` are depth-2 wrappers over `synth_status`. `grep -rn 'synth_with' crates/` returns 7 hits of which only 4 are CALLS — the rest are the definition and two doc mentions. **Count call sites, not grep hits.** **(3) A DOC COMMENT'S JUSTIFICATION CAN BE STALE EVEN WHEN ITS ADVICE IS GOOD.** `synth_with`'s doc block says "Header ORDER is load-bearing — the differential harness byte-compares against upstream Envoy." **The harness does NOT byte-compare:** `diff_headers` builds a `BTreeSet` of LOWER-CASED header NAMES, compares the SETS, then compares VALUES for every name outside the 3-entry `HEADER_ALLOW_LIST`. **Order is never read.** Matching upstream's order is still correct practice (unit tests pin it), but a wrong order fails a UNIT test, not a fixture — do not price it as a differential risk. **(4) A MEASURED RULE CAN BE WRONG AT EXACTLY ONE BOUNDARY BYTE.** The parent SPEC's `grpc-message` rule ("`0x20` through `0x7E` pass through except `%`") is FALSE: **`~` (0x7E) IS ESCAPED to `%7E`**. The corrected rule is pass-through iff **`0x20..=0x7D` AND not `%`**. The parent had measured the INTERIOR of the range and inferred the endpoints. **When a rule is stated as a RANGE, probe BOTH endpoints explicitly.** **(5) PAIRED CONTROLS FIND DIVERGENCES THAT ARE NOT YOUR SUBJECT.** Probing every mapping cell WITH and WITHOUT the gRPC content-type surfaced an unrelated, PRE-EXISTING divergence: upstream emits `location: <scheme>://<authority><path>` on a `direct_response` whose status is **`201` or `3xx`**, in BOTH directions; envoy-rust does not. Banked as the reassigned **CF-110-3**, and it forces `110.2`'s fixture to avoid those statuses — without the control column that fixture would have landed RED for a reason unrelated to its subject. **(6) A HEADER-DICT CLIENT DESTROYS THE EVIDENCE YOU CAME FOR.** V-2 (ORDER) and V-10 (CASE) are both unanswerable through `curl`-style or dict-based clients. Probe with a **RAW SOCKET**, one connection per probe, and parse the response head yourself — but remember your own parser is a hazard too: an `lstrip()` on field values silently ate the leading spaces of an encoding probe and briefly looked like an Envoy rule. **Also: an HCM with no `http_filters` block ACCEPTS the config and then HANGS every request** — a probe harness that times out with zero bytes is usually missing the router filter, not evidence about the surface under test. **[NEW AT THE PHASE-110 §5 STATE-0/1 PICK — five traps, every one MEASURED AT THIS COMMIT.]** **(1) A STANDING, REPEATEDLY-AFFIRMED REJECTION CAN BE SOUND IN ITS REASONING AND STILL NOT REACH YOUR SLICE — CHECK ITS PREMISE AGAINST THE WIRE, NOT AGAINST ITS RESTATEMENTS.** ADR-0048 rejected the gRPC family as blocked on HTTP/2 trailer propagation; that verdict was re-affirmed roughly FIFTEEN times, most recently ADR-0171(b) and the ADR-0175 pick, and it is **still entirely correct for the gRPC DATA PATH**. It is inapplicable to gRPC-aware LOCAL REPLIES, and one probe settled it: the reply is `content-length: 0` over HTTP/1.1 with `grpc-status`/`grpc-message` as ordinary response HEADERS, and a bodiless response has NO TRAILER SECTION AT ALL. The re-affirmations had propagated the CONCLUSION without re-testing the PREMISE against the specific slice. **A banked rejection is a claim too.** **(2) `deny_unknown_fields` MAKES CONFIG-SURFACE PHASES REAL BUT NOT NECESSARILY WITNESSABLE.** `bootstrap.rs` carries **207** `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` occurrences (`Node` the sole documented exception), so accepting a new config block IS a genuine behaviour change — but `0088/expectations.yaml` states outright that **a fixture cannot witness a config that refuses to boot**, and the `Driver` enum has NO boot-failure variant. Reject/accept parity is provable ONLY by in-process unit tests. **Price a config-surface-only slice accordingly: it may be cheap AND unwitnessable.** **(3) THE PIPE TRAP IS PART-RIGHT AND PART-WRONG, AND SO WAS THIS SESSION'S FIRST ATTEMPT TO CORRECT IT.** **MEASURED FOUR WAYS over all 114 rows at the phase-110 pick, superseding this line's own earlier correction:** **9** rows carry an in-cell pipe (raw `|` count ≠ 7 — rows `36`, `38`, `39`, `52`, `54`, `66`, `70`, `76`, `108`), so the inherited count of NINE is CORRECT; **5** of those escape at least one pipe as `\|` (`38`, `66`, `70`, `76`, `108`), so the word **UNESCAPED** overstates it and the parenthetical **"(incl. `76` and `108`)" MISLABELS those two — both are ESCAPED and split cleanly into 6 cells**; only **2** rows (`38`, `39`) actually mis-split on `' | '`; and **field 4 holds a VALID status on all 114 rows**, which is exactly why the operational rule works. ⚠ **A raw-pipe census and a `' | '`-split census answer DIFFERENT questions and neither alone is the trap** — an earlier attempt at this correction claimed "6 rows" by filtering on `'\\|' in line or mis-split`, which silently MISSES rows whose unescaped pipe is not surrounded by spaces (`36`, `52`, `54`). **ADR-0177's "THREE STANDING FIGURES CORRECTED" item (1) carries that understated 6 and is superseded by THIS measurement**; the ADR is append-only (D-3.5) and was not rewritten.  The OPERATIONAL rule is unchanged and still correct: split on `' | '` WITH surrounding spaces, status is FIELD 4; never "fix" the rows (`ROADMAP.md` is append-only history). **(4) CENSUS A FIXTURE-YAML CONSTRUCT BY ITS SERDE SPELLING, NOT ITS RUST TYPE NAME.** `grep -rl 'Http1ProbeList' tests/fixtures/*/expectations.yaml` returns a believable **1**; the YAML spelling is **`kind: http1_probe_list`** (`#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]`), and the true count is **14** — which also stale-dates `109/SPEC.md:119`'s "13". Another instance of the standing "a probe that fails to execute returns a believable zero". **(5) A HEADER-SET ASSERTION CAN BE A FULL VALUE WITNESS — READ THE COMPARATOR BEFORE ASSUMING YOU NEED A NEW ONE.** `Http1HeaderRule` has exactly ONE variant (`SetEqualModuloAllowList`), which reads like a names-only check. `diff_headers` actually asserts BOTH the lower-cased NAME SETS' equality AND, for every name outside the **3**-entry `HEADER_ALLOW_LIST`, exact string VALUE equality — so `grpc-status`, `grpc-message`, `content-type` and `content-length` are all value-compared, and the phase needs **ZERO harness changes**. Reading the comparator is what turned an assumed harness extension into no work at all. **[NEW AT THE SUB-PHASE 109.2 §5 STATE-6 CLOSE-OUT — four traps, every one MEASURED AT THIS COMMIT.]** **(1) A 113/113 `done` ROADMAP IS NOT A COMPLETE MISSION, AND THIS IS THE FIRST SESSION THAT CAN BE FOOLED BY IT.** Leg (i) of the stop condition went TRUE here for the first time in the project's history; legs (ii) and (iii) did NOT, and the condition requires ALL THREE. The census counts ROWS while the mission counts FEATURES, which is the entire reason legs (ii) and (iii) exist. **A human asking for a CONDITIONAL `stop` file is asking you to EVALUATE the condition, not to create the file — measure, report FALSE, move on.** **(2) A FULLY-`done` FAMILY HEADING IS NOT A COMPLETE FAMILY.** `### Runtime + hot restart family` reads 6/6 `done` as of this commit while RTDS, hot restart and the `RuntimeUInt32`/CSRF honoring consumers have never been built — `109.1`/`109.2` landed the ROUTE consumer and the REJECT sides only. A close-out RETIRES the subsection instead, so the heading AND every one of its bullets are ARCHIVED members and there is no extra at all. **Derive the expected multiset from what you actually move, then let the mechanical PER-FILE (old − new) check ADJUDICATE.** Here that was 15 standing lines (the four top-section blocks + their four `_Historical_` pointers + the superseded traps line + the superseded §5.1 doctrine bullet + the CONSUMED follow-up CI-record line under `## Last commit`) + 19 retired Notes lines (heading + EIGHTEEN bullets accumulated across the state-2..5 arc, where a handoff would have guessed five) = **34**, with ZERO unexpected members. **(4) THE RETIRED SUBSECTION'S BULLET COUNT IS ITSELF A CENSUS — COUNT IT, DO NOT INHERIT IT.** The `### Sub-phase 109.2 §5 state-5 code review` heading was renamed at each of four sessions while its bullets ACCUMULATED underneath, so the state-5 name sits above bullets written at state 2, 3, 4 AND 5. Reading the heading as a description of its contents undercounts by thirteen.]** **[NEW AT THE SUB-PHASE 109.2 §5 STATE-5 CODE REVIEW — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION AND RE-VERIFIED ON DISK BEFORE BEING WRITTEN.]** **(1) A BANKED FINDING'S *CONSEQUENCE* CLAUSE IS A CLAIM TOO, AND THIS ONE WAS FALSE.** V-1's stale-citation core was CONFIRMED, but the ratio it derived inverted which comparator supports which number — see the corrected +58%/+52%/−25% arithmetic above. **Re-derive the CONCLUSION a banked finding draws, not only the measurement it rests on.** **(2) A FINDING CAN BE REAL WHILE ITS *CHARGE* IS MISPLACED — CHECK WHETHER THE DEFECT WAS TRANSCRIBED OR INTRODUCED.** V-5, V-6 and V-10 object to sentences in the new `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` subsection that are near-VERBATIM copies of `109.1/SPEC.md` §1.3 — the source the SPEC's own X-5 item REQUIRED the executor to transcribe from. The argument it carries survives (both extra files are the STATE ledger, neither a test file), but one stale figure on a page is a reason to re-derive EVERY figure on that page, not just the one that was banked. **(4) A FIXTURE CAN PIN A MEASURED CELL AND STILL FAIL TO PIN THE *READING* THE CONTRACT CALLS LOAD-BEARING.** Fixture `0088`'s `p7` witnesses cell 10 (unparseable + default 100 → GATED) and cell **11** (unparseable + default **0** → FALLBACK) is absent — so p7 excludes "unparseable → 0" but CANNOT exclude "unparseable → always-pass, default ignored", because with a 100/HUNDRED default both readings answer the same body. The contract says so itself twelve lines away (`:3279-3281`: "a single-direction probe is equally consistent with 'unparseable → 0'"). **When a contract names a both-directions reading as load-bearing, count the directions the fixture actually ships.** Related: probe `p10` is DOMINATED by `p2` (no gated prefix is a prefix of `/p-catch`, and the driver `bail!`s at the FIRST failing probe), so it cannot report a failure independently — a probe that cannot fail is not a test. **(5) AN EXCLUSION IS ONLY AS GOOD AS THE PREMISE THAT JUSTIFIES IT, AND THIS ONE IS MEASURED FALSE.** `109.2/SPEC.md:46` excludes bool runtime values from the fixture because they "are boot-fatal after 109.1 (CF-109-1/2)". They are not: `RuntimeValue::Bool` stringifies to `"true"`/`"false"`, fails the `f64` parse and falls through to the default — the landed unit table pins B1/B2/B3 as `Ok` rows and the contract carries them as measured 40/40 cells.
