MEASURED with an `envoy.filters.http.rbac` deny-all chain: upstream DOES transform them (`200` + `grpc-status: 7` + `grpc-message: RBAC: access denied` vs a `403` + `text/plain` control). Shipping the SPEC's literal list would have instantiated the ADR-0049 partially-covered-family class the seam design exists to avoid. **Enumerate the family from the CODE, then check the SPEC against it — not the other way round.** **(3) PREFER A PREDICATE THAT FAILS SAFE OVER ONE THAT ENUMERATES.** The locality bit is `outgoing_local`, defaulting to **true** and cleared ONLY by `outgoing_local = !completing_upstream_response` at the proxy arm — reusing `AttemptResult.upstream_response`, a bit the tree ALREADY carries and documents (`hcm.rs:368-370`). A synth arm added later is covered BY OMISSION rather than skipped by omission. The `BuildOutcome::Synth`-only gate the SPEC contemplates would have missed the `run_attempt`/pool synths, the request-budget overflow, the chunked-501 and both filter arms. **(4) WHEN A RULE IS DERIVED FROM ONE INSTANCE, FIND A SECOND INSTANCE.** §1.4's order rule was banked from `location` alone. A circuit-breaker overflow probe (`max_connections: 0`) showed `x-envoy-overloaded: true` ALSO survives IN ITS ORIGINAL POSITION — the pass-through rule is GENERAL, not a `location` special case. The generalized rule (pass-throughs in original relative order; then `content-type`, `grpc-status`, `[grpc-message]`; then `date`, `server`, `connection`; then `content-length: 0`) reproduces all THREE measured cases exactly. **Order remains a UNIT-TEST concern only — `diff_headers` never reads it.** **(5) A FEATURE-GATED MODULE IS INVISIBLE TO `cargo test --workspace`.** `crates/envoy-http1/src/uring.rs` is gated at `lib.rs:24-25` behind the `uring` feature (`Cargo.toml:27-28`) and contains **NO `#[cfg(test)]` and NO `#[test]` at all**. Its seam therefore gets its coverage STRUCTURALLY — the transform lives INSIDE `write_owned` (all four call sites are synth; the proxied path uses `write_head_body` at `:376`) — and the absence of a test is BANKED as **CF-110-5** rather than papered over. **(6) A NEW PRE-EXISTING DIVERGENCE, BANKED AS CF-110-4:** upstream's own NON-gRPC local-reply header order is `[pass-through,] content-length, content-type, date, server, connection`, whereas envoy-rust's `synth_with` emits `server, date, content-length, content-type, connection`. ORDER-ONLY, invisible to `diff_headers`, PRE-EXISTING and gRPC-ORTHOGONAL — **not a licence to touch `synth_with`.** Together with CF-110-3 (upstream's `location` on a `201`/`3xx` `direct_response`) these are the two divergences `110.2`'s fixture must route around. **[NEW AT THE PHASE-110 §5 STATE-2 SPLIT — six traps, every one MEASURED AT THIS COMMIT.]** **(1) A SPEC's "structural boundary" claim is a CENSUS, and this one was FALSE.** The parent `110/SPEC.md` §3 D6 asserted that H1 and H2 share only the route RESOLVER, so scoping to H1 was "a real boundary rather than a hopeful one". **MEASURED FALSE:** `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:518` calls **`envoy_http1::build_response`**, which reaches `synth_direct_response`/`synth_400`/`synth_404`/`synth_redirect` → `synth_with`, and `envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:2127-2128` documents it ("ONE arm serves BOTH codecs"). H2 owns its own synthesisers for UPSTREAM-FAILURE paths ONLY. **The general rule: when a SPEC says two subsystems are isolated, grep the CALL EDGE, not the type names.** **(2) A CODE-SHAPE claim can be right about the NAMES and wrong about the TIERS.** The inherited "`synth_with` has SEVEN callers" list conflated direct callers with the whole synth family: there are **FOUR** direct call sites, and `synth_400`/`synth_404`/`synth_501` are depth-2 wrappers over `synth_status`. `grep -rn 'synth_with' crates/` returns 7 hits of which only 4 are CALLS — the rest are the definition and two doc mentions. **Count call sites, not grep hits.** **(3) A DOC COMMENT'S JUSTIFICATION CAN BE STALE EVEN WHEN ITS ADVICE IS GOOD.** `synth_with`'s doc block says "Header ORDER is load-bearing — the differential harness byte-compares against upstream Envoy." **The harness does NOT byte-compare:** `diff_headers` builds a `BTreeSet` of LOWER-CASED header NAMES, compares the SETS, then compares VALUES for every name outside the 3-entry `HEADER_ALLOW_LIST`. **Order is never read.** Matching upstream's order is still correct practice (unit tests pin it), but a wrong order fails a UNIT test, not a fixture — do not price it as a differential risk. **(4) A MEASURED RULE CAN BE WRONG AT EXACTLY ONE BOUNDARY BYTE.** The parent SPEC's `grpc-message` rule ("`0x20` through `0x7E` pass through except `%`") is FALSE: **`~` (0x7E) IS ESCAPED to `%7E`**. The corrected rule is pass-through iff **`0x20..=0x7D` AND not `%`**. The parent had measured the INTERIOR of the range and inferred the endpoints. **When a rule is stated as a RANGE, probe BOTH endpoints explicitly.** **(5) PAIRED CONTROLS FIND DIVERGENCES THAT ARE NOT YOUR SUBJECT.** Probing every mapping cell WITH and WITHOUT the gRPC content-type surfaced an unrelated, PRE-EXISTING divergence: upstream emits `location: <scheme>://<authority><path>` on a `direct_response` whose status is **`201` or `3xx`**, in BOTH directions; envoy-rust does not. Banked as the reassigned **CF-110-3**, and it forces `110.2`'s fixture to avoid those statuses — without the control column that fixture would have landed RED for a reason unrelated to its subject. **(6) A HEADER-DICT CLIENT DESTROYS THE EVIDENCE YOU CAME FOR.** V-2 (ORDER) and V-10 (CASE) are both unanswerable through `curl`-style or dict-based clients. Probe with a **RAW SOCKET**, one connection per probe, and parse the response head yourself — but remember your own parser is a hazard too: an `lstrip()` on field values silently ate the leading spaces of an encoding probe and briefly looked like an Envoy rule. **Also: an HCM with no `http_filters` block ACCEPTS the config and then HANGS every request** — a probe harness that times out with zero bytes is usually missing the router filter, not evidence about the surface under test. **[NEW AT THE PHASE-110 §5 STATE-0/1 PICK — five traps, every one MEASURED AT THIS COMMIT.]** **(1) A STANDING, REPEATEDLY-AFFIRMED REJECTION CAN BE SOUND IN ITS REASONING AND STILL NOT REACH YOUR SLICE — CHECK ITS PREMISE AGAINST THE WIRE, NOT AGAINST ITS RESTATEMENTS.** ADR-0048 rejected the gRPC family as blocked on HTTP/2 trailer propagation; that verdict was re-affirmed roughly FIFTEEN times, most recently ADR-0171(b) and the ADR-0175 pick, and it is **still entirely correct for the gRPC DATA PATH**. It is inapplicable to gRPC-aware LOCAL REPLIES, and one probe settled it: the reply is `content-length: 0` over HTTP/1.1 with `grpc-status`/`grpc-message` as ordinary response HEADERS, and a bodiless response has NO TRAILER SECTION AT ALL. It is not: `BodyRule::JsonShape` parses both bodies through `serde_json`, and because `preserve_order` is enabled NOWHERE in the workspace, `serde_json::Map` is a `BTreeMap` that canonically key-sorts on re-serialization. **The fix was already in the harness; the temptation was to add an allow-list and weaken the assertion.** **(5) AN "ABSENCE" CAN BE PINNED BY A PASSING TEST, AND A PHASE THAT BUILDS THE ABSENT THING MUST SAY SO.** Four places assert "there is no runtime layer", one of them a test literally named `runtime_key_is_rtds_inert`. None becomes wrong when a `static_layer` store lands without RTDS or consumers — **but a reviewer meeting that test name inside a phase titled "runtime" will read a contradiction unless the SPEC pre-empts it.** **Grep for tests and docs that assert the ABSENCE of what you are about to build.** **(6) A REJECTED CANDIDATE'S RECORD IS WORTH IMPROVING EVEN WHEN YOU DO NOT PICK IT.** The `CF-76-1` re-census found a **SECOND matcher with the same bug** (`route_match_matches`, `crates/envoy-filter/src/jwt_authn.rs:173-186`), **THREE** unshared query-strip implementations already in-tree, that **`plan_redirect` is already query-strip-correct** (phase 76 pre-paid part of the fix), and that the record's "~4 probes" is an UNDER-COUNT (8-12, ≈900-1100 net LoC, because the two NON-REGRESSION witnesses need an access-log-observing driver). **The standing trap for whoever takes it: fix `route_matches`' ARGUMENT, never mutate `req.path`** — that field feeds the access log, the forwarded upstream target, `plan_redirect` and jwt_authn's `www-authenticate` realm, and NO current test would catch the damage. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-6 CLOSE-OUT — four findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A CLOSE-OUT THAT FLIPS A PARENT ROW MUST ASSERT EACH ROW'S OWN EXPECTED STATUS, NOT ONE SHARED VALUE.** This close-out flipped TWO rows from DIFFERENT starting statuses — `76.2` from `planned` and parent `76` from `in-progress`. A single shared `expect` would have silently skipped one row or aborted after mutating the other. **MEASURED result: `git diff --numstat` exactly `2 2`, a cell-by-cell compare showing f1/f2/f3/f5/f6 SAME on both rows, and the census moving `105 done / 1 in-progress / 1 planned` → `107 done`.** **Assert per-row, and compare cells rather than trusting the join.** **(2) THE LEDGER'S OWN WARNING ABOUT INHERITED LINE NUMBERS PAID OFF IMMEDIATELY.** The previous session's token sweep keyed on the inherited doctrine-bullet line number `128`, swept a BLANK line, and reported a false `109 → 0` total loss. This session located every sweep target BY TEXT (`awk '$0==H'` whole-line equality for the archive headers, an `.index()` on a distinctive substring for the traps-line boundary) and **verified all four top-section archive headers resolve to EXACTLY ONE line each BEFORE any write**, so a miss would abort before mutating. **A close-out RETIRES the active-phase Notes subsection entirely, so its downward shift is larger than a state advance's — never carry a line number across a session.** **(3) THE TRAPS LINE WAS REWRITTEN BY SPLITTING AT A TEXT BOUNDARY, WHICH MAKES THE ADR-0160 RETENTION CHECK STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN HOPEFUL.** Only the leading STATE-specific preamble (MEASURED **1604** of **62510** characters) was replaced; the enduring tail (**60906** characters, from the `[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2)` marker onward) was carried across BYTE-IDENTICALLY by construction. **A token sweep still ran and is still the gate — but a rewrite that preserves a measured byte-range cannot lose an enduring trap by accident.** **(4) A CLOSE-OUT ADDS NO ADR AND NO `### ` NOTES SUBSECTION, AND BOTH ARE MEASURED PRECEDENTS RATHER THAN OMISSIONS.** The 75.1 and 76.1 close-outs both landed ADR-less; the Notes subsection is RETIRED to the archive behind a `> Historical …` breadcrumb, not superseded in place. **Writing either one breaks the next session's checks** — an unexpected `### ` subsection makes the heading-structure check fail, and a gratuitous ADR moves the head the next session re-derives. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2) — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION.]** **(1) A FRESH REVIEWER RE-DERIVES THE PRIOR ROUND'S FINDINGS, AND THE ONLY GUARD IS READING THE PRIOR REVIEW.** THREE of five read-only dimensions surfaced round-1 items as if new — **M-7, M-9, N-4, N-5, N-8, N-9** — and TWO of them graded a banked Minor as an **ISSUE**. Nothing about a subagent's severity is trustworthy on this axis, because the subagent cannot know what was already banked. **Read the prior `REVIEW.md` before grading anything, and record every re-derived finding as STATUS rather than re-issuing it** (`REVIEW-2.md` §7 exists precisely for this). **(2) INDEPENDENT CONVERGENCE BY TWO DIMENSIONS ON AN UNPROMPTED FINDING IS WORTH MORE THAN EITHER REPORT.** M2-2 (`port_redirect` has no differential witness) was reached by one dimension censusing probes against routes and by another hand-executing a `strip_port` deletion against all 19 probes. Neither was asked for it. **Weight a finding by how many independent routes reached it, not by the confidence of the report.** **(3) A FIX THAT RE-ANCHORS AN ARTIFACT MUST RE-SWEEP THE PROSE THAT JUSTIFIED THE OLD ONE.** The M-2 fix re-anchored `q02` onto its own `/q2-hostport` route and carried forward the justification "q02 and r01 agree on the expected `location`" — TRUE of the original `/a-host` Q2, FALSE of the shipped one, and now wrong in THREE documents; `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` refutes itself nine lines apart (`:3018` vs `:3025`). The scheduled next widening (`regex_rewrite`, a declared non-goal at `SPEC.md:477`) adds a third `return Err` inside `validate_redirect_oneofs` in `bootstrap.rs`, whose doc carries no reciprocal warning — reproducing I-1 exactly. **Put the forcing-function warning on the file that will be EDITED, not on the file that will BREAK.** **(5) A LESSON PARAGRAPH CAN CONTRADICT ITSELF WITH ITS OWN NUMBERS.** `PROGRESS.md:2535` states the fixture carries "14×301, 2×302" — that is the **MUTATED** tree's census, captured while `q02`'s `expected_status` was flipped 301→302 for a negative control; the shipped fixture is **15×301, 1×302**. Pinned in a dedicated test instead — same coverage, guard intact, table's authority uncompromised, deviation RECORDED (`PROGRESS.md` §R3.7) rather than silently taken. **(5) WHEN A GUARD FIRES CORRECTLY ON A REAL DEFECT, EXTEND WHAT IT GUARDS — DO NOT REMOVE THE GUARD.** The tempting reading of I-1 is "`unreachable!()` was the bug, delete it". It was not: the bug was a WIDENED PRODUCER with an UNEXTENDED CONSUMER. The arm stays; its comment now says **six** and carries the cross-crate warning. **And the general rule that produced I-1 in the first place: when a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not tell you, because `unreachable!()` compiles clean.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-5 CODE REVIEW — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION, not quoted from a subagent.]** **(1) WIDENING A FUNCTION'S RETURNABLE ERROR SET IS A CROSS-CRATE CHANGE, AND `unreachable!()` IS WHERE IT LANDS.** Task 8 added a `validate_redirect_oneofs` call inside `reparse_and_select_route_config` (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs:159`), so that function can now return `RedirectPathRewriteConflict`/`RedirectSchemeRewriteConflict`. Its SOLE production caller (`crates/envoy-http1/src/rds_watcher.rs:184`) classifies exactly FOUR variants and ends `other => unreachable!(…)` (`:216-222`) — and the comment at `:211-215` states the invariant the phase broke VERBATIM. `Cargo.toml:42` is `panic = "abort"`, so the reload ABORTS THE PROCESS. **`unreachable!()` compiles clean, so gate (e) is structurally blind to it; only a `reload()`-LEVEL test could have caught it, and all four existing ones test other variants.** **When a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not.** **(2) A CONTRACT THAT DISCLAIMS A CELL AND THEN CLAIMS IT IS TESTED IS WORSE THAN SILENCE.** `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md:3122-3124` correctly labels §F items 7/8 as CHOICES rather than measurements, then says they are "pinned by in-process tests". **MEASURED FALSE for both**: all eight test call sites of `plan_redirect` pass `Some(...)`, and the 22-row table CANNOT express `None` because its `cell()` constructor hard-wires `prefix: Some(prefix)` (`hcm.rs:10484`) and all 22 rows go through it (0 direct `Cell {` literals). **A `Option` FIELD ON A TEST-TABLE STRUCT PROVES NOTHING IF THE CONSTRUCTOR CAN ONLY PRODUCE `Some` — check the constructor, not the type.** **(3) A PROBE PAIR NAMED AS A WITNESS IN A DOC COMMENT MUST BE RE-DERIVED, NOT READ.** `tests/differential/tests/route_redirect_action.rs:9-10` claims `q01` vs `r01` witnesses the `host_redirect` port-DROP. Re-deriving first-match-wins selection over the parsed config: **9** routes set `host_redirect`, **all 9** are probed with an UNPORTED Host, and the only two ported probes hit `https_redirect`/`{}` routes — so **0 of 18** probes can witness it, on the rule SPEC §2.4(b) itself calls the one most likely to be got wrong. **The cell IS pinned in-process (`hcm.rs:10671-10679`); it is UNCOMPARED, not unpinned — say which.** **(4) A SUBAGENT'S LINE NUMBERS DRIFT EVEN WHEN ITS REASONING IS RIGHT.** One dimension's `hcm.rs` citations were consistently **~12 lines high** (`:2331` for a line at `:2319`) while every one of its CONCLUSIONS held. **Re-read every citation; do not inherit a line number from a review either.** **(5) AN UNVERIFIED UPSTREAM HYPOTHESIS MUST NOT BE GRADED AS A FINDING.** A dimension proposed that upstream strips a DEFAULT port (`:80`/`:443`) on a scheme change, explicitly labelling it *"a hypothesis from upstream implementation shape, not from anything on disk"*. It is recorded in `REVIEW.md` §5 as an UNGRADED hypothesis with the two probes that would settle it — never as a defect. **D-3.3: the contract is the contract; you do not read upstream source to decide what equivalence means.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-4 VERIFICATION — five findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A DOCUMENTED HOST STALL DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND THAT ABSENCE IS ITSELF A MEASUREMENT.** The state-3 session recorded — and the handoff instructed state 4 to budget for — a hard stall on `xds_rds_hot_reload` that forced its `-p differential` sweep to be killed after ~11 minutes and left gate (b) unadjudicated. **THREE consecutive whole-workspace sweeps completed in ~5½ minutes each with all 163 binaries reporting, and `xds_rds_hot_reload` passes in isolation in 1.98 s.** An environmental stall is not a property of the TREE. **Re-measure an inherited time budget before spending it, and do not read a stall's absence as a different tree.** **(2) THE ONE RED SITTING ON THE PHASE'S OWN SURFACE IS THE ONE WORTH CHASING.** Seven of the eight REDs were trivially off-surface; `xds_rds_hot_reload_fixture` was NOT — Task 8 rewrote exactly that file's validation path (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs`, `if let` → exhaustive `match`). Disbelieve a zero.** **(5) A LANDED PLAN'S TEST-COUNT PREDICTION IS NOT A BASELINE — THE DIFF IS.** `76.2/PLAN.md` §6 predicted `passed≈2168` from "~30 new tests"; the measured `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` attribute delta is **+11 / −0**, and both identities close exactly on 11 (`162 + 1 = 163` binaries, `2137 + 11 = 2148` passed). The gap is the table-driven 22-cell design the plan itself chose. **Do NOT read `2148` against `2168` as "tests were lost".** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-3 IMPLEMENTATION — eight findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A PLAN'S LITERAL RUST CAN BE PRE-FLIGHTED AND STILL BROKEN — THREE DEFECTS IN ONE PLAN.** `PLAN.md` §2 claimed Tasks 1-5/8/9 passed `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` in a scratch worktree, and THREE literals still failed: T3-3's `Some("/é"[..2].into())` **panics in the test itself** (`"/é"` is 3 bytes, so byte index 2 is not a char boundary) and never reaches the function under test; T3-2's assert message `"a bare redirect{} rewrites nothing"` **does not compile** (`assert_eq!`'s third arg is a FORMAT STRING, so the bare `{}` is a positional placeholder); and T7-1's `HttpVersion::Http2` **does not exist** (the enum has exactly `Http10` and `Http11`). **THE ROOT CAUSE IS GENERAL: `fmt` and `clippy` DO NOT EXECUTE TESTS, and the pre-flight RAN only 2 of the new tests** — so a runtime panic in a third was invisible to it, and a block that never compiled cannot have passed the lint it was claimed to pass. **Treat a pre-flight's own claim as a CLAIM; transcribe verbatim, then COMPILE AND RUN.** **(2) A PER-TASK LINT GATE CAN BE UNACHIEVABLE UNDER THE PLAN'S OWN TASK SPLIT.** `PLAN.md`'s Global Constraint says `clippy -D warnings` must be clean at EVERY task boundary; measured, Tasks 2/3/4 each add a NON-TEST item whose only NON-TEST consumer is Task 5, so each boundary is `unused import` / `never constructed` / `never used` → **exit 101**. It does not — the call compiles, and the RED is the pure behavioural `left: 501, right: 301`, which is BETTER evidence. **Do not treat a plan's predicted failure MODE as a checkable fact.** **(4) `envoy-bin` HAS NO `--mode` FLAG.** `PLAN.md` Task 10's `--mode validate` exits **2** with `unknown argument: --mode`; `crates/envoy-bin/src/argv.rs:27-29` accepts EXACTLY `-c <path>` or `--config-path <path>` (clap is deliberately avoided per D-3.2). Validate instead by substituting `{{PORT}}` and booting under `timeout`: exit **124** (still running) with zero errors proves the config parses AND the listener binds — strictly stronger. **(5) THE STRONGEST SEAM EVIDENCE IS A CROSS-CRATE MUTATION.** Mutating `plan_redirect` in **`crates/envoy-http1`** turned an **`crates/envoy-http2`** test RED (`left: Some("http://envoy-rust.test/a-host")`). That does not merely assert H2 reaches the arm — it PROVES H2's answer is COMPUTED BY the H1 arm. **When a claim is "one implementation serves two consumers", mutate the implementation and watch the OTHER consumer fail.** **(6) A FULL LOCAL `-p differential` SWEEP STALLS ON `xds_rds_hot_reload` ON THIS HOST** (virtiofs, no inotify). ':(exclude)docs/'`, +1334/−69) against the plan's ≈1202 code-only projection — **+5%**, versus `76.1`'s **+50%**. The table-driven 22-cell design held (it was NOT expanded into 22 `#[test]` fns), §6.1's mid-execution trigger never fired, and **no split was needed**. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-2 PLAN-WRITE — six findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A SPLIT SIBLING'S LANDING STALE-DATES THE OTHER SPEC, AND THE DRIFT IS NOT UNIFORM.** `76.2/SPEC.md` was written at `f438cb9`, before `76.1`. It is not: `BodyRule::JsonShape` parses both bodies through `serde_json`, and because `preserve_order` is enabled NOWHERE in the workspace, `serde_json::Map` is a `BTreeMap` that canonically key-sorts on re-serialization. **The fix was already in the harness; the temptation was to add an allow-list and weaken the assertion.** **(5) AN "ABSENCE" CAN BE PINNED BY A PASSING TEST, AND A PHASE THAT BUILDS THE ABSENT THING MUST SAY SO.** Four places assert "there is no runtime layer", one of them a test literally named `runtime_key_is_rtds_inert`. None becomes wrong when a `static_layer` store lands without RTDS or consumers — **but a reviewer meeting that test name inside a phase titled "runtime" will read a contradiction unless the SPEC pre-empts it.** **Grep for tests and docs that assert the ABSENCE of what you are about to build.** **(6) A REJECTED CANDIDATE'S RECORD IS WORTH IMPROVING EVEN WHEN YOU DO NOT PICK IT.** The `CF-76-1` re-census found a **SECOND matcher with the same bug** (`route_match_matches`, `crates/envoy-filter/src/jwt_authn.rs:173-186`), **THREE** unshared query-strip implementations already in-tree, that **`plan_redirect` is already query-strip-correct** (phase 76 pre-paid part of the fix), and that the record's "~4 probes" is an UNDER-COUNT (8-12, ≈900-1100 net LoC, because the two NON-REGRESSION witnesses need an access-log-observing driver). **The standing trap for whoever takes it: fix `route_matches`' ARGUMENT, never mutate `req.path`** — that field feeds the access log, the forwarded upstream target, `plan_redirect` and jwt_authn's `www-authenticate` realm, and NO current test would catch the damage. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-6 CLOSE-OUT — four findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A CLOSE-OUT THAT FLIPS A PARENT ROW MUST ASSERT EACH ROW'S OWN EXPECTED STATUS, NOT ONE SHARED VALUE.** This close-out flipped TWO rows from DIFFERENT starting statuses — `76.2` from `planned` and parent `76` from `in-progress`. A single shared `expect` would have silently skipped one row or aborted after mutating the other. **MEASURED result: `git diff --numstat` exactly `2 2`, a cell-by-cell compare showing f1/f2/f3/f5/f6 SAME on both rows, and the census moving `105 done / 1 in-progress / 1 planned` → `107 done`.** **Assert per-row, and compare cells rather than trusting the join.** **(2) THE LEDGER'S OWN WARNING ABOUT INHERITED LINE NUMBERS PAID OFF IMMEDIATELY.** The previous session's token sweep keyed on the inherited doctrine-bullet line number `128`, swept a BLANK line, and reported a false `109 → 0` total loss. This session located every sweep target BY TEXT (`awk '$0==H'` whole-line equality for the archive headers, an `.index()` on a distinctive substring for the traps-line boundary) and **verified all four top-section archive headers resolve to EXACTLY ONE line each BEFORE any write**, so a miss would abort before mutating. **A close-out RETIRES the active-phase Notes subsection entirely, so its downward shift is larger than a state advance's — never carry a line number across a session.** **(3) THE TRAPS LINE WAS REWRITTEN BY SPLITTING AT A TEXT BOUNDARY, WHICH MAKES THE ADR-0160 RETENTION CHECK STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN HOPEFUL.** Only the leading STATE-specific preamble (MEASURED **1604** of **62510** characters) was replaced; the enduring tail (**60906** characters, from the `[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2)` marker onward) was carried across BYTE-IDENTICALLY by construction. **A token sweep still ran and is still the gate — but a rewrite that preserves a measured byte-range cannot lose an enduring trap by accident.** **(4) A CLOSE-OUT ADDS NO ADR AND NO `### ` NOTES SUBSECTION, AND BOTH ARE MEASURED PRECEDENTS RATHER THAN OMISSIONS.** The 75.1 and 76.1 close-outs both landed ADR-less; the Notes subsection is RETIRED to the archive behind a `> Historical …` breadcrumb, not superseded in place. **Writing either one breaks the next session's checks** — an unexpected `### ` subsection makes the heading-structure check fail, and a gratuitous ADR moves the head the next session re-derives. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2) — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION.]** **(1) A FRESH REVIEWER RE-DERIVES THE PRIOR ROUND'S FINDINGS, AND THE ONLY GUARD IS READING THE PRIOR REVIEW.** THREE of five read-only dimensions surfaced round-1 items as if new — **M-7, M-9, N-4, N-5, N-8, N-9** — and TWO of them graded a banked Minor as an **ISSUE**. Nothing about a subagent's severity is trustworthy on this axis, because the subagent cannot know what was already banked. **Read the prior `REVIEW.md` before grading anything, and record every re-derived finding as STATUS rather than re-issuing it** (`REVIEW-2.md` §7 exists precisely for this). **(2) INDEPENDENT CONVERGENCE BY TWO DIMENSIONS ON AN UNPROMPTED FINDING IS WORTH MORE THAN EITHER REPORT.** M2-2 (`port_redirect` has no differential witness) was reached by one dimension censusing probes against routes and by another hand-executing a `strip_port` deletion against all 19 probes. Neither was asked for it. **Weight a finding by how many independent routes reached it, not by the confidence of the report.** **(3) A FIX THAT RE-ANCHORS AN ARTIFACT MUST RE-SWEEP THE PROSE THAT JUSTIFIED THE OLD ONE.** The M-2 fix re-anchored `q02` onto its own `/q2-hostport` route and carried forward the justification "q02 and r01 agree on the expected `location`" — TRUE of the original `/a-host` Q2, FALSE of the shipped one, and now wrong in THREE documents; `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` refutes itself nine lines apart (`:3018` vs `:3025`). The scheduled next widening (`regex_rewrite`, a declared non-goal at `SPEC.md:477`) adds a third `return Err` inside `validate_redirect_oneofs` in `bootstrap.rs`, whose doc carries no reciprocal warning — reproducing I-1 exactly. **Put the forcing-function warning on the file that will be EDITED, not on the file that will BREAK.** **(5) A LESSON PARAGRAPH CAN CONTRADICT ITSELF WITH ITS OWN NUMBERS.** `PROGRESS.md:2535` states the fixture carries "14×301, 2×302" — that is the **MUTATED** tree's census, captured while `q02`'s `expected_status` was flipped 301→302 for a negative control; the shipped fixture is **15×301, 1×302**. Pinned in a dedicated test instead — same coverage, guard intact, table's authority uncompromised, deviation RECORDED (`PROGRESS.md` §R3.7) rather than silently taken. **(5) WHEN A GUARD FIRES CORRECTLY ON A REAL DEFECT, EXTEND WHAT IT GUARDS — DO NOT REMOVE THE GUARD.** The tempting reading of I-1 is "`unreachable!()` was the bug, delete it". It was not: the bug was a WIDENED PRODUCER with an UNEXTENDED CONSUMER. The arm stays; its comment now says **six** and carries the cross-crate warning. **And the general rule that produced I-1 in the first place: when a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not tell you, because `unreachable!()` compiles clean.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-5 CODE REVIEW — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION, not quoted from a subagent.]** **(1) WIDENING A FUNCTION'S RETURNABLE ERROR SET IS A CROSS-CRATE CHANGE, AND `unreachable!()` IS WHERE IT LANDS.** Task 8 added a `validate_redirect_oneofs` call inside `reparse_and_select_route_config` (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs:159`), so that function can now return `RedirectPathRewriteConflict`/`RedirectSchemeRewriteConflict`. Its SOLE production caller (`crates/envoy-http1/src/rds_watcher.rs:184`) classifies exactly FOUR variants and ends `other => unreachable!(…)` (`:216-222`) — and the comment at `:211-215` states the invariant the phase broke VERBATIM. `Cargo.toml:42` is `panic = "abort"`, so the reload ABORTS THE PROCESS. **`unreachable!()` compiles clean, so gate (e) is structurally blind to it; only a `reload()`-LEVEL test could have caught it, and all four existing ones test other variants.** **When a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not.** **(2) A CONTRACT THAT DISCLAIMS A CELL AND THEN CLAIMS IT IS TESTED IS WORSE THAN SILENCE.** `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md:3122-3124` correctly labels §F items 7/8 as CHOICES rather than measurements, then says they are "pinned by in-process tests". **MEASURED FALSE for both**: all eight test call sites of `plan_redirect` pass `Some(...)`, and the 22-row table CANNOT express `None` because its `cell()` constructor hard-wires `prefix: Some(prefix)` (`hcm.rs:10484`) and all 22 rows go through it (0 direct `Cell {` literals). **A `Option` FIELD ON A TEST-TABLE STRUCT PROVES NOTHING IF THE CONSTRUCTOR CAN ONLY PRODUCE `Some` — check the constructor, not the type.** **(3) A PROBE PAIR NAMED AS A WITNESS IN A DOC COMMENT MUST BE RE-DERIVED, NOT READ.** `tests/differential/tests/route_redirect_action.rs:9-10` claims `q01` vs `r01` witnesses the `host_redirect` port-DROP. Re-deriving first-match-wins selection over the parsed config: **9** routes set `host_redirect`, **all 9** are probed with an UNPORTED Host, and the only two ported probes hit `https_redirect`/`{}` routes — so **0 of 18** probes can witness it, on the rule SPEC §2.4(b) itself calls the one most likely to be got wrong. **The cell IS pinned in-process (`hcm.rs:10671-10679`); it is UNCOMPARED, not unpinned — say which.** **(4) A SUBAGENT'S LINE NUMBERS DRIFT EVEN WHEN ITS REASONING IS RIGHT.** One dimension's `hcm.rs` citations were consistently **~12 lines high** (`:2331` for a line at `:2319`) while every one of its CONCLUSIONS held. **Re-read every citation; do not inherit a line number from a review either.** **(5) AN UNVERIFIED UPSTREAM HYPOTHESIS MUST NOT BE GRADED AS A FINDING.** A dimension proposed that upstream strips a DEFAULT port (`:80`/`:443`) on a scheme change, explicitly labelling it *"a hypothesis from upstream implementation shape, not from anything on disk"*. It is recorded in `REVIEW.md` §5 as an UNGRADED hypothesis with the two probes that would settle it — never as a defect. **D-3.3: the contract is the contract; you do not read upstream source to decide what equivalence means.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-4 VERIFICATION — five findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A DOCUMENTED HOST STALL DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND THAT ABSENCE IS ITSELF A MEASUREMENT.** The state-3 session recorded — and the handoff instructed state 4 to budget for — a hard stall on `xds_rds_hot_reload` that forced its `-p differential` sweep to be killed after ~11 minutes and left gate (b) unadjudicated. **THREE consecutive whole-workspace sweeps completed in ~5½ minutes each with all 163 binaries reporting, and `xds_rds_hot_reload` passes in isolation in 1.98 s.** An environmental stall is not a property of the TREE. **Re-measure an inherited time budget before spending it, and do not read a stall's absence as a different tree.** **(2) THE ONE RED SITTING ON THE PHASE'S OWN SURFACE IS THE ONE WORTH CHASING.** Seven of the eight REDs were trivially off-surface; `xds_rds_hot_reload_fixture` was NOT — Task 8 rewrote exactly that file's validation path (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs`, `if let` → exhaustive `match`). Disbelieve a zero.** **(5) A LANDED PLAN'S TEST-COUNT PREDICTION IS NOT A BASELINE — THE DIFF IS.** `76.2/PLAN.md` §6 predicted `passed≈2168` from "~30 new tests"; the measured `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` attribute delta is **+11 / −0**, and both identities close exactly on 11 (`162 + 1 = 163` binaries, `2137 + 11 = 2148` passed). The gap is the table-driven 22-cell design the plan itself chose. **Do NOT read `2148` against `2168` as "tests were lost".** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-3 IMPLEMENTATION — eight findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A PLAN'S LITERAL RUST CAN BE PRE-FLIGHTED AND STILL BROKEN — THREE DEFECTS IN ONE PLAN.** `PLAN.md` §2 claimed Tasks 1-5/8/9 passed `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` in a scratch worktree, and THREE literals still failed: T3-3's `Some("/é"[..2].into())` **panics in the test itself** (`"/é"` is 3 bytes, so byte index 2 is not a char boundary) and never reaches the function under test; T3-2's assert message `"a bare redirect{} rewrites nothing"` **does not compile** (`assert_eq!`'s third arg is a FORMAT STRING, so the bare `{}` is a positional placeholder); and T7-1's `HttpVersion::Http2` **does not exist** (the enum has exactly `Http10` and `Http11`). **THE ROOT CAUSE IS GENERAL: `fmt` and `clippy` DO NOT EXECUTE TESTS, and the pre-flight RAN only 2 of the new tests** — so a runtime panic in a third was invisible to it, and a block that never compiled cannot have passed the lint it was claimed to pass. **Treat a pre-flight's own claim as a CLAIM; transcribe verbatim, then COMPILE AND RUN.** **(2) A PER-TASK LINT GATE CAN BE UNACHIEVABLE UNDER THE PLAN'S OWN TASK SPLIT.** `PLAN.md`'s Global Constraint says `clippy -D warnings` must be clean at EVERY task boundary; measured, Tasks 2/3/4 each add a NON-TEST item whose only NON-TEST consumer is Task 5, so each boundary is `unused import` / `never constructed` / `never used` → **exit 101**. It does not — the call compiles, and the RED is the pure behavioural `left: 501, right: 301`, which is BETTER evidence. **Do not treat a plan's predicted failure MODE as a checkable fact.** **(4) `envoy-bin` HAS NO `--mode` FLAG.** `PLAN.md` Task 10's `--mode validate` exits **2** with `unknown argument: --mode`; `crates/envoy-bin/src/argv.rs:27-29` accepts EXACTLY `-c <path>` or `--config-path <path>` (clap is deliberately avoided per D-3.2). Validate instead by substituting `{{PORT}}` and booting under `timeout`: exit **124** (still running) with zero errors proves the config parses AND the listener binds — strictly stronger. **(5) THE STRONGEST SEAM EVIDENCE IS A CROSS-CRATE MUTATION.** Mutating `plan_redirect` in **`crates/envoy-http1`** turned an **`crates/envoy-http2`** test RED (`left: Some("http://envoy-rust.test/a-host")`). That does not merely assert H2 reaches the arm — it PROVES H2's answer is COMPUTED BY the H1 arm. **When a claim is "one implementation serves two consumers", mutate the implementation and watch the OTHER consumer fail.** **(6) A FULL LOCAL `-p differential` SWEEP STALLS ON `xds_rds_hot_reload` ON THIS HOST** (virtiofs, no inotify). ':(exclude)docs/'`, +1334/−69) against the plan's ≈1202 code-only projection — **+5%**, versus `76.1`'s **+50%**. The table-driven 22-cell design held (it was NOT expanded into 22 `#[test]` fns), §6.1's mid-execution trigger never fired, and **no split was needed**. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-2 PLAN-WRITE — six findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A SPLIT SIBLING'S LANDING STALE-DATES THE OTHER SPEC, AND THE DRIFT IS NOT UNIFORM.** `76.2/SPEC.md` was written at `f438cb9`, before `76.1`. It is not: `BodyRule::JsonShape` parses both bodies through `serde_json`, and because `preserve_order` is enabled NOWHERE in the workspace, `serde_json::Map` is a `BTreeMap` that canonically key-sorts on re-serialization. **The fix was already in the harness; the temptation was to add an allow-list and weaken the assertion.** **(5) AN "ABSENCE" CAN BE PINNED BY A PASSING TEST, AND A PHASE THAT BUILDS THE ABSENT THING MUST SAY SO.** Four places assert "there is no runtime layer", one of them a test literally named `runtime_key_is_rtds_inert`. None becomes wrong when a `static_layer` store lands without RTDS or consumers — **but a reviewer meeting that test name inside a phase titled "runtime" will read a contradiction unless the SPEC pre-empts it.** **Grep for tests and docs that assert the ABSENCE of what you are about to build.** **(6) A REJECTED CANDIDATE'S RECORD IS WORTH IMPROVING EVEN WHEN YOU DO NOT PICK IT.** The `CF-76-1` re-census found a **SECOND matcher with the same bug** (`route_match_matches`, `crates/envoy-filter/src/jwt_authn.rs:173-186`), **THREE** unshared query-strip implementations already in-tree, that **`plan_redirect` is already query-strip-correct** (phase 76 pre-paid part of the fix), and that the record's "~4 probes" is an UNDER-COUNT (8-12, ≈900-1100 net LoC, because the two NON-REGRESSION witnesses need an access-log-observing driver). **The standing trap for whoever takes it: fix `route_matches`' ARGUMENT, never mutate `req.path`** — that field feeds the access log, the forwarded upstream target, `plan_redirect` and jwt_authn's `www-authenticate` realm, and NO current test would catch the damage. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-6 CLOSE-OUT — four findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A CLOSE-OUT THAT FLIPS A PARENT ROW MUST ASSERT EACH ROW'S OWN EXPECTED STATUS, NOT ONE SHARED VALUE.** This close-out flipped TWO rows from DIFFERENT starting statuses — `76.2` from `planned` and parent `76` from `in-progress`. A single shared `expect` would have silently skipped one row or aborted after mutating the other. **MEASURED result: `git diff --numstat` exactly `2 2`, a cell-by-cell compare showing f1/f2/f3/f5/f6 SAME on both rows, and the census moving `105 done / 1 in-progress / 1 planned` → `107 done`.** **Assert per-row, and compare cells rather than trusting the join.** **(2) THE LEDGER'S OWN WARNING ABOUT INHERITED LINE NUMBERS PAID OFF IMMEDIATELY.** The previous session's token sweep keyed on the inherited doctrine-bullet line number `128`, swept a BLANK line, and reported a false `109 → 0` total loss. This session located every sweep target BY TEXT (`awk '$0==H'` whole-line equality for the archive headers, an `.index()` on a distinctive substring for the traps-line boundary) and **verified all four top-section archive headers resolve to EXACTLY ONE line each BEFORE any write**, so a miss would abort before mutating. **A close-out RETIRES the active-phase Notes subsection entirely, so its downward shift is larger than a state advance's — never carry a line number across a session.** **(3) THE TRAPS LINE WAS REWRITTEN BY SPLITTING AT A TEXT BOUNDARY, WHICH MAKES THE ADR-0160 RETENTION CHECK STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN HOPEFUL.** Only the leading STATE-specific preamble (MEASURED **1604** of **62510** characters) was replaced; the enduring tail (**60906** characters, from the `[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2)` marker onward) was carried across BYTE-IDENTICALLY by construction. **A token sweep still ran and is still the gate — but a rewrite that preserves a measured byte-range cannot lose an enduring trap by accident.** **(4) A CLOSE-OUT ADDS NO ADR AND NO `### ` NOTES SUBSECTION, AND BOTH ARE MEASURED PRECEDENTS RATHER THAN OMISSIONS.** The 75.1 and 76.1 close-outs both landed ADR-less; the Notes subsection is RETIRED to the archive behind a `> Historical …` breadcrumb, not superseded in place. **Writing either one breaks the next session's checks** — an unexpected `### ` subsection makes the heading-structure check fail, and a gratuitous ADR moves the head the next session re-derives. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2) — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION.]** **(1) A FRESH REVIEWER RE-DERIVES THE PRIOR ROUND'S FINDINGS, AND THE ONLY GUARD IS READING THE PRIOR REVIEW.** THREE of five read-only dimensions surfaced round-1 items as if new — **M-7, M-9, N-4, N-5, N-8, N-9** — and TWO of them graded a banked Minor as an **ISSUE**. Nothing about a subagent's severity is trustworthy on this axis, because the subagent cannot know what was already banked. **Read the prior `REVIEW.md` before grading anything, and record every re-derived finding as STATUS rather than re-issuing it** (`REVIEW-2.md` §7 exists precisely for this). **(2) INDEPENDENT CONVERGENCE BY TWO DIMENSIONS ON AN UNPROMPTED FINDING IS WORTH MORE THAN EITHER REPORT.** M2-2 (`port_redirect` has no differential witness) was reached by one dimension censusing probes against routes and by another hand-executing a `strip_port` deletion against all 19 probes. Neither was asked for it. **Weight a finding by how many independent routes reached it, not by the confidence of the report.** **(3) A FIX THAT RE-ANCHORS AN ARTIFACT MUST RE-SWEEP THE PROSE THAT JUSTIFIED THE OLD ONE.** The M-2 fix re-anchored `q02` onto its own `/q2-hostport` route and carried forward the justification "q02 and r01 agree on the expected `location`" — TRUE of the original `/a-host` Q2, FALSE of the shipped one, and now wrong in THREE documents; `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` refutes itself nine lines apart (`:3018` vs `:3025`). The scheduled next widening (`regex_rewrite`, a declared non-goal at `SPEC.md:477`) adds a third `return Err` inside `validate_redirect_oneofs` in `bootstrap.rs`, whose doc carries no reciprocal warning — reproducing I-1 exactly. **Put the forcing-function warning on the file that will be EDITED, not on the file that will BREAK.** **(5) A LESSON PARAGRAPH CAN CONTRADICT ITSELF WITH ITS OWN NUMBERS.** `PROGRESS.md:2535` states the fixture carries "14×301, 2×302" — that is the **MUTATED** tree's census, captured while `q02`'s `expected_status` was flipped 301→302 for a negative control; the shipped fixture is **15×301, 1×302**. Pinned in a dedicated test instead — same coverage, guard intact, table's authority uncompromised, deviation RECORDED (`PROGRESS.md` §R3.7) rather than silently taken. **(5) WHEN A GUARD FIRES CORRECTLY ON A REAL DEFECT, EXTEND WHAT IT GUARDS — DO NOT REMOVE THE GUARD.** The tempting reading of I-1 is "`unreachable!()` was the bug, delete it". It was not: the bug was a WIDENED PRODUCER with an UNEXTENDED CONSUMER. The arm stays; its comment now says **six** and carries the cross-crate warning. **And the general rule that produced I-1 in the first place: when a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not tell you, because `unreachable!()` compiles clean.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-5 CODE REVIEW — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION, not quoted from a subagent.]** **(1) WIDENING A FUNCTION'S RETURNABLE ERROR SET IS A CROSS-CRATE CHANGE, AND `unreachable!()` IS WHERE IT LANDS.** Task 8 added a `validate_redirect_oneofs` call inside `reparse_and_select_route_config` (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs:159`), so that function can now return `RedirectPathRewriteConflict`/`RedirectSchemeRewriteConflict`. Its SOLE production caller (`crates/envoy-http1/src/rds_watcher.rs:184`) classifies exactly FOUR variants and ends `other => unreachable!(…)` (`:216-222`) — and the comment at `:211-215` states the invariant the phase broke VERBATIM. `Cargo.toml:42` is `panic = "abort"`, so the reload ABORTS THE PROCESS. **`unreachable!()` compiles clean, so gate (e) is structurally blind to it; only a `reload()`-LEVEL test could have caught it, and all four existing ones test other variants.** **When a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not.** **(2) A CONTRACT THAT DISCLAIMS A CELL AND THEN CLAIMS IT IS TESTED IS WORSE THAN SILENCE.** `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md:3122-3124` correctly labels §F items 7/8 as CHOICES rather than measurements, then says they are "pinned by in-process tests". **MEASURED FALSE for both**: all eight test call sites of `plan_redirect` pass `Some(...)`, and the 22-row table CANNOT express `None` because its `cell()` constructor hard-wires `prefix: Some(prefix)` (`hcm.rs:10484`) and all 22 rows go through it (0 direct `Cell {` literals). **A `Option` FIELD ON A TEST-TABLE STRUCT PROVES NOTHING IF THE CONSTRUCTOR CAN ONLY PRODUCE `Some` — check the constructor, not the type.** **(3) A PROBE PAIR NAMED AS A WITNESS IN A DOC COMMENT MUST BE RE-DERIVED, NOT READ.** `tests/differential/tests/route_redirect_action.rs:9-10` claims `q01` vs `r01` witnesses the `host_redirect` port-DROP. Re-deriving first-match-wins selection over the parsed config: **9** routes set `host_redirect`, **all 9** are probed with an UNPORTED Host, and the only two ported probes hit `https_redirect`/`{}` routes — so **0 of 18** probes can witness it, on the rule SPEC §2.4(b) itself calls the one most likely to be got wrong. **The cell IS pinned in-process (`hcm.rs:10671-10679`); it is UNCOMPARED, not unpinned — say which.** **(4) A SUBAGENT'S LINE NUMBERS DRIFT EVEN WHEN ITS REASONING IS RIGHT.** One dimension's `hcm.rs` citations were consistently **~12 lines high** (`:2331` for a line at `:2319`) while every one of its CONCLUSIONS held. **Re-read every citation; do not inherit a line number from a review either.** **(5) AN UNVERIFIED UPSTREAM HYPOTHESIS MUST NOT BE GRADED AS A FINDING.** A dimension proposed that upstream strips a DEFAULT port (`:80`/`:443`) on a scheme change, explicitly labelling it *"a hypothesis from upstream implementation shape, not from anything on disk"*. It is recorded in `REVIEW.md` §5 as an UNGRADED hypothesis with the two probes that would settle it — never as a defect. **D-3.3: the contract is the contract; you do not read upstream source to decide what equivalence means.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-4 VERIFICATION — five findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A DOCUMENTED HOST STALL DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND THAT ABSENCE IS ITSELF A MEASUREMENT.** The state-3 session recorded — and the handoff instructed state 4 to budget for — a hard stall on `xds_rds_hot_reload` that forced its `-p differential` sweep to be killed after ~11 minutes and left gate (b) unadjudicated. **THREE consecutive whole-workspace sweeps completed in ~5½ minutes each with all 163 binaries reporting, and `xds_rds_hot_reload` passes in isolation in 1.98 s.** An environmental stall is not a property of the TREE. **Re-measure an inherited time budget before spending it, and do not read a stall's absence as a different tree.** **(2) THE ONE RED SITTING ON THE PHASE'S OWN SURFACE IS THE ONE WORTH CHASING.** Seven of the eight REDs were trivially off-surface; `xds_rds_hot_reload_fixture` was NOT — Task 8 rewrote exactly that file's validation path (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs`, `if let` → exhaustive `match`). Disbelieve a zero.** **(5) A LANDED PLAN'S TEST-COUNT PREDICTION IS NOT A BASELINE — THE DIFF IS.** `76.2/PLAN.md` §6 predicted `passed≈2168` from "~30 new tests"; the measured `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` attribute delta is **+11 / −0**, and both identities close exactly on 11 (`162 + 1 = 163` binaries, `2137 + 11 = 2148` passed). The gap is the table-driven 22-cell design the plan itself chose. **Do NOT read `2148` against `2168` as "tests were lost".** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-3 IMPLEMENTATION — eight findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A PLAN'S LITERAL RUST CAN BE PRE-FLIGHTED AND STILL BROKEN — THREE DEFECTS IN ONE PLAN.** `PLAN.md` §2 claimed Tasks 1-5/8/9 passed `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` in a scratch worktree, and THREE literals still failed: T3-3's `Some("/é"[..2].into())` **panics in the test itself** (`"/é"` is 3 bytes, so byte index 2 is not a char boundary) and never reaches the function under test; T3-2's assert message `"a bare redirect{} rewrites nothing"` **does not compile** (`assert_eq!`'s third arg is a FORMAT STRING, so the bare `{}` is a positional placeholder); and T7-1's `HttpVersion::Http2` **does not exist** (the enum has exactly `Http10` and `Http11`). **THE ROOT CAUSE IS GENERAL: `fmt` and `clippy` DO NOT EXECUTE TESTS, and the pre-flight RAN only 2 of the new tests** — so a runtime panic in a third was invisible to it, and a block that never compiled cannot have passed the lint it was claimed to pass. **Treat a pre-flight's own claim as a CLAIM; transcribe verbatim, then COMPILE AND RUN.** **(2) A PER-TASK LINT GATE CAN BE UNACHIEVABLE UNDER THE PLAN'S OWN TASK SPLIT.** `PLAN.md`'s Global Constraint says `clippy -D warnings` must be clean at EVERY task boundary; measured, Tasks 2/3/4 each add a NON-TEST item whose only NON-TEST consumer is Task 5, so each boundary is `unused import` / `never constructed` / `never used` → **exit 101**. It does not — the call compiles, and the RED is the pure behavioural `left: 501, right: 301`, which is BETTER evidence. **Do not treat a plan's predicted failure MODE as a checkable fact.** **(4) `envoy-bin` HAS NO `--mode` FLAG.** `PLAN.md` Task 10's `--mode validate` exits **2** with `unknown argument: --mode`; `crates/envoy-bin/src/argv.rs:27-29` accepts EXACTLY `-c <path>` or `--config-path <path>` (clap is deliberately avoided per D-3.2). Validate instead by substituting `{{PORT}}` and booting under `timeout`: exit **124** (still running) with zero errors proves the config parses AND the listener binds — strictly stronger. **(5) THE STRONGEST SEAM EVIDENCE IS A CROSS-CRATE MUTATION.** Mutating `plan_redirect` in **`crates/envoy-http1`** turned an **`crates/envoy-http2`** test RED (`left: Some("http://envoy-rust.test/a-host")`). That does not merely assert H2 reaches the arm — it PROVES H2's answer is COMPUTED BY the H1 arm. **When a claim is "one implementation serves two consumers", mutate the implementation and watch the OTHER consumer fail.** **(6) A FULL LOCAL `-p differential` SWEEP STALLS ON `xds_rds_hot_reload` ON THIS HOST** (virtiofs, no inotify). ':(exclude)docs/'`, +1334/−69) against the plan's ≈1202 code-only projection — **+5%**, versus `76.1`'s **+50%**. The table-driven 22-cell design held (it was NOT expanded into 22 `#[test]` fns), §6.1's mid-execution trigger never fired, and **no split was needed**. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-2 PLAN-WRITE — six findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A SPLIT SIBLING'S LANDING STALE-DATES THE OTHER SPEC, AND THE DRIFT IS NOT UNIFORM.** `76.2/SPEC.md` was written at `f438cb9`, before `76.1`. It is not: `BodyRule::JsonShape` parses both bodies through `serde_json`, and because `preserve_order` is enabled NOWHERE in the workspace, `serde_json::Map` is a `BTreeMap` that canonically key-sorts on re-serialization. **The fix was already in the harness; the temptation was to add an allow-list and weaken the assertion.** **(5) AN "ABSENCE" CAN BE PINNED BY A PASSING TEST, AND A PHASE THAT BUILDS THE ABSENT THING MUST SAY SO.** Four places assert "there is no runtime layer", one of them a test literally named `runtime_key_is_rtds_inert`. None becomes wrong when a `static_layer` store lands without RTDS or consumers — **but a reviewer meeting that test name inside a phase titled "runtime" will read a contradiction unless the SPEC pre-empts it.** **Grep for tests and docs that assert the ABSENCE of what you are about to build.** **(6) A REJECTED CANDIDATE'S RECORD IS WORTH IMPROVING EVEN WHEN YOU DO NOT PICK IT.** The `CF-76-1` re-census found a **SECOND matcher with the same bug** (`route_match_matches`, `crates/envoy-filter/src/jwt_authn.rs:173-186`), **THREE** unshared query-strip implementations already in-tree, that **`plan_redirect` is already query-strip-correct** (phase 76 pre-paid part of the fix), and that the record's "~4 probes" is an UNDER-COUNT (8-12, ≈900-1100 net LoC, because the two NON-REGRESSION witnesses need an access-log-observing driver). **The standing trap for whoever takes it: fix `route_matches`' ARGUMENT, never mutate `req.path`** — that field feeds the access log, the forwarded upstream target, `plan_redirect` and jwt_authn's `www-authenticate` realm, and NO current test would catch the damage. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-6 CLOSE-OUT — four findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A CLOSE-OUT THAT FLIPS A PARENT ROW MUST ASSERT EACH ROW'S OWN EXPECTED STATUS, NOT ONE SHARED VALUE.** This close-out flipped TWO rows from DIFFERENT starting statuses — `76.2` from `planned` and parent `76` from `in-progress`. A single shared `expect` would have silently skipped one row or aborted after mutating the other. **MEASURED result: `git diff --numstat` exactly `2 2`, a cell-by-cell compare showing f1/f2/f3/f5/f6 SAME on both rows, and the census moving `105 done / 1 in-progress / 1 planned` → `107 done`.** **Assert per-row, and compare cells rather than trusting the join.** **(2) THE LEDGER'S OWN WARNING ABOUT INHERITED LINE NUMBERS PAID OFF IMMEDIATELY.** The previous session's token sweep keyed on the inherited doctrine-bullet line number `128`, swept a BLANK line, and reported a false `109 → 0` total loss. This session located every sweep target BY TEXT (`awk '$0==H'` whole-line equality for the archive headers, an `.index()` on a distinctive substring for the traps-line boundary) and **verified all four top-section archive headers resolve to EXACTLY ONE line each BEFORE any write**, so a miss would abort before mutating. **A close-out RETIRES the active-phase Notes subsection entirely, so its downward shift is larger than a state advance's — never carry a line number across a session.** **(3) THE TRAPS LINE WAS REWRITTEN BY SPLITTING AT A TEXT BOUNDARY, WHICH MAKES THE ADR-0160 RETENTION CHECK STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN HOPEFUL.** Only the leading STATE-specific preamble (MEASURED **1604** of **62510** characters) was replaced; the enduring tail (**60906** characters, from the `[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2)` marker onward) was carried across BYTE-IDENTICALLY by construction. **A token sweep still ran and is still the gate — but a rewrite that preserves a measured byte-range cannot lose an enduring trap by accident.** **(4) A CLOSE-OUT ADDS NO ADR AND NO `### ` NOTES SUBSECTION, AND BOTH ARE MEASURED PRECEDENTS RATHER THAN OMISSIONS.** The 75.1 and 76.1 close-outs both landed ADR-less; the Notes subsection is RETIRED to the archive behind a `> Historical …` breadcrumb, not superseded in place. **Writing either one breaks the next session's checks** — an unexpected `### ` subsection makes the heading-structure check fail, and a gratuitous ADR moves the head the next session re-derives. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2) — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION.]** **(1) A FRESH REVIEWER RE-DERIVES THE PRIOR ROUND'S FINDINGS, AND THE ONLY GUARD IS READING THE PRIOR REVIEW.** THREE of five read-only dimensions surfaced round-1 items as if new — **M-7, M-9, N-4, N-5, N-8, N-9** — and TWO of them graded a banked Minor as an **ISSUE**. Nothing about a subagent's severity is trustworthy on this axis, because the subagent cannot know what was already banked. **Read the prior `REVIEW.md` before grading anything, and record every re-derived finding as STATUS rather than re-issuing it** (`REVIEW-2.md` §7 exists precisely for this). **(2) INDEPENDENT CONVERGENCE BY TWO DIMENSIONS ON AN UNPROMPTED FINDING IS WORTH MORE THAN EITHER REPORT.** M2-2 (`port_redirect` has no differential witness) was reached by one dimension censusing probes against routes and by another hand-executing a `strip_port` deletion against all 19 probes. Neither was asked for it. **Weight a finding by how many independent routes reached it, not by the confidence of the report.** **(3) A FIX THAT RE-ANCHORS AN ARTIFACT MUST RE-SWEEP THE PROSE THAT JUSTIFIED THE OLD ONE.** The M-2 fix re-anchored `q02` onto its own `/q2-hostport` route and carried forward the justification "q02 and r01 agree on the expected `location`" — TRUE of the original `/a-host` Q2, FALSE of the shipped one, and now wrong in THREE documents; `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` refutes itself nine lines apart (`:3018` vs `:3025`). The scheduled next widening (`regex_rewrite`, a declared non-goal at `SPEC.md:477`) adds a third `return Err` inside `validate_redirect_oneofs` in `bootstrap.rs`, whose doc carries no reciprocal warning — reproducing I-1 exactly. **Put the forcing-function warning on the file that will be EDITED, not on the file that will BREAK.** **(5) A LESSON PARAGRAPH CAN CONTRADICT ITSELF WITH ITS OWN NUMBERS.** `PROGRESS.md:2535` states the fixture carries "14×301, 2×302" — that is the **MUTATED** tree's census, captured while `q02`'s `expected_status` was flipped 301→302 for a negative control; the shipped fixture is **15×301, 1×302**. Pinned in a dedicated test instead — same coverage, guard intact, table's authority uncompromised, deviation RECORDED (`PROGRESS.md` §R3.7) rather than silently taken. **(5) WHEN A GUARD FIRES CORRECTLY ON A REAL DEFECT, EXTEND WHAT IT GUARDS — DO NOT REMOVE THE GUARD.** The tempting reading of I-1 is "`unreachable!()` was the bug, delete it". It was not: the bug was a WIDENED PRODUCER with an UNEXTENDED CONSUMER. The arm stays; its comment now says **six** and carries the cross-crate warning. **And the general rule that produced I-1 in the first place: when a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not tell you, because `unreachable!()` compiles clean.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-5 CODE REVIEW — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION, not quoted from a subagent.]** **(1) WIDENING A FUNCTION'S RETURNABLE ERROR SET IS A CROSS-CRATE CHANGE, AND `unreachable!()` IS WHERE IT LANDS.** Task 8 added a `validate_redirect_oneofs` call inside `reparse_and_select_route_config` (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs:159`), so that function can now return `RedirectPathRewriteConflict`/`RedirectSchemeRewriteConflict`. Its SOLE production caller (`crates/envoy-http1/src/rds_watcher.rs:184`) classifies exactly FOUR variants and ends `other => unreachable!(…)` (`:216-222`) — and the comment at `:211-215` states the invariant the phase broke VERBATIM. `Cargo.toml:42` is `panic = "abort"`, so the reload ABORTS THE PROCESS. **`unreachable!()` compiles clean, so gate (e) is structurally blind to it; only a `reload()`-LEVEL test could have caught it, and all four existing ones test other variants.** **When a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not.** **(2) A CONTRACT THAT DISCLAIMS A CELL AND THEN CLAIMS IT IS TESTED IS WORSE THAN SILENCE.** `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md:3122-3124` correctly labels §F items 7/8 as CHOICES rather than measurements, then says they are "pinned by in-process tests". **MEASURED FALSE for both**: all eight test call sites of `plan_redirect` pass `Some(...)`, and the 22-row table CANNOT express `None` because its `cell()` constructor hard-wires `prefix: Some(prefix)` (`hcm.rs:10484`) and all 22 rows go through it (0 direct `Cell {` literals). **A `Option` FIELD ON A TEST-TABLE STRUCT PROVES NOTHING IF THE CONSTRUCTOR CAN ONLY PRODUCE `Some` — check the constructor, not the type.** **(3) A PROBE PAIR NAMED AS A WITNESS IN A DOC COMMENT MUST BE RE-DERIVED, NOT READ.** `tests/differential/tests/route_redirect_action.rs:9-10` claims `q01` vs `r01` witnesses the `host_redirect` port-DROP. Re-deriving first-match-wins selection over the parsed config: **9** routes set `host_redirect`, **all 9** are probed with an UNPORTED Host, and the only two ported probes hit `https_redirect`/`{}` routes — so **0 of 18** probes can witness it, on the rule SPEC §2.4(b) itself calls the one most likely to be got wrong. **The cell IS pinned in-process (`hcm.rs:10671-10679`); it is UNCOMPARED, not unpinned — say which.** **(4) A SUBAGENT'S LINE NUMBERS DRIFT EVEN WHEN ITS REASONING IS RIGHT.** One dimension's `hcm.rs` citations were consistently **~12 lines high** (`:2331` for a line at `:2319`) while every one of its CONCLUSIONS held. **Re-read every citation; do not inherit a line number from a review either.** **(5) AN UNVERIFIED UPSTREAM HYPOTHESIS MUST NOT BE GRADED AS A FINDING.** A dimension proposed that upstream strips a DEFAULT port (`:80`/`:443`) on a scheme change, explicitly labelling it *"a hypothesis from upstream implementation shape, not from anything on disk"*. It is recorded in `REVIEW.md` §5 as an UNGRADED hypothesis with the two probes that would settle it — never as a defect. **D-3.3: the contract is the contract; you do not read upstream source to decide what equivalence means.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-4 VERIFICATION — five findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A DOCUMENTED HOST STALL DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND THAT ABSENCE IS ITSELF A MEASUREMENT.** The state-3 session recorded — and the handoff instructed state 4 to budget for — a hard stall on `xds_rds_hot_reload` that forced its `-p differential` sweep to be killed after ~11 minutes and left gate (b) unadjudicated. **THREE consecutive whole-workspace sweeps completed in ~5½ minutes each with all 163 binaries reporting, and `xds_rds_hot_reload` passes in isolation in 1.98 s.** An environmental stall is not a property of the TREE. **Re-measure an inherited time budget before spending it, and do not read a stall's absence as a different tree.** **(2) THE ONE RED SITTING ON THE PHASE'S OWN SURFACE IS THE ONE WORTH CHASING.** Seven of the eight REDs were trivially off-surface; `xds_rds_hot_reload_fixture` was NOT — Task 8 rewrote exactly that file's validation path (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs`, `if let` → exhaustive `match`). Disbelieve a zero.** **(5) A LANDED PLAN'S TEST-COUNT PREDICTION IS NOT A BASELINE — THE DIFF IS.** `76.2/PLAN.md` §6 predicted `passed≈2168` from "~30 new tests"; the measured `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` attribute delta is **+11 / −0**, and both identities close exactly on 11 (`162 + 1 = 163` binaries, `2137 + 11 = 2148` passed). The gap is the table-driven 22-cell design the plan itself chose. **Do NOT read `2148` against `2168` as "tests were lost".** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-3 IMPLEMENTATION — eight findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A PLAN'S LITERAL RUST CAN BE PRE-FLIGHTED AND STILL BROKEN — THREE DEFECTS IN ONE PLAN.** `PLAN.md` §2 claimed Tasks 1-5/8/9 passed `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` in a scratch worktree, and THREE literals still failed: T3-3's `Some("/é"[..2].into())` **panics in the test itself** (`"/é"` is 3 bytes, so byte index 2 is not a char boundary) and never reaches the function under test; T3-2's assert message `"a bare redirect{} rewrites nothing"` **does not compile** (`assert_eq!`'s third arg is a FORMAT STRING, so the bare `{}` is a positional placeholder); and T7-1's `HttpVersion::Http2` **does not exist** (the enum has exactly `Http10` and `Http11`). **THE ROOT CAUSE IS GENERAL: `fmt` and `clippy` DO NOT EXECUTE TESTS, and the pre-flight RAN only 2 of the new tests** — so a runtime panic in a third was invisible to it, and a block that never compiled cannot have passed the lint it was claimed to pass. **Treat a pre-flight's own claim as a CLAIM; transcribe verbatim, then COMPILE AND RUN.** **(2) A PER-TASK LINT GATE CAN BE UNACHIEVABLE UNDER THE PLAN'S OWN TASK SPLIT.** `PLAN.md`'s Global Constraint says `clippy -D warnings` must be clean at EVERY task boundary; measured, Tasks 2/3/4 each add a NON-TEST item whose only NON-TEST consumer is Task 5, so each boundary is `unused import` / `never constructed` / `never used` → **exit 101**. It does not — the call compiles, and the RED is the pure behavioural `left: 501, right: 301`, which is BETTER evidence. **Do not treat a plan's predicted failure MODE as a checkable fact.** **(4) `envoy-bin` HAS NO `--mode` FLAG.** `PLAN.md` Task 10's `--mode validate` exits **2** with `unknown argument: --mode`; `crates/envoy-bin/src/argv.rs:27-29` accepts EXACTLY `-c <path>` or `--config-path <path>` (clap is deliberately avoided per D-3.2). Validate instead by substituting `{{PORT}}` and booting under `timeout`: exit **124** (still running) with zero errors proves the config parses AND the listener binds — strictly stronger. **(5) THE STRONGEST SEAM EVIDENCE IS A CROSS-CRATE MUTATION.** Mutating `plan_redirect` in **`crates/envoy-http1`** turned an **`crates/envoy-http2`** test RED (`left: Some("http://envoy-rust.test/a-host")`). That does not merely assert H2 reaches the arm — it PROVES H2's answer is COMPUTED BY the H1 arm. **When a claim is "one implementation serves two consumers", mutate the implementation and watch the OTHER consumer fail.** **(6) A FULL LOCAL `-p differential` SWEEP STALLS ON `xds_rds_hot_reload` ON THIS HOST** (virtiofs, no inotify). ':(exclude)docs/'`, +1334/−69) against the plan's ≈1202 code-only projection — **+5%**, versus `76.1`'s **+50%**. The table-driven 22-cell design held (it was NOT expanded into 22 `#[test]` fns), §6.1's mid-execution trigger never fired, and **no split was needed**. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-2 PLAN-WRITE — six findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A SPLIT SIBLING'S LANDING STALE-DATES THE OTHER SPEC, AND THE DRIFT IS NOT UNIFORM.** `76.2/SPEC.md` was written at `f438cb9`, before `76.1`. It is not: `BodyRule::JsonShape` parses both bodies through `serde_json`, and because `preserve_order` is enabled NOWHERE in the workspace, `serde_json::Map` is a `BTreeMap` that canonically key-sorts on re-serialization. **The fix was already in the harness; the temptation was to add an allow-list and weaken the assertion.** **(5) AN "ABSENCE" CAN BE PINNED BY A PASSING TEST, AND A PHASE THAT BUILDS THE ABSENT THING MUST SAY SO.** Four places assert "there is no runtime layer", one of them a test literally named `runtime_key_is_rtds_inert`. None becomes wrong when a `static_layer` store lands without RTDS or consumers — **but a reviewer meeting that test name inside a phase titled "runtime" will read a contradiction unless the SPEC pre-empts it.** **Grep for tests and docs that assert the ABSENCE of what you are about to build.** **(6) A REJECTED CANDIDATE'S RECORD IS WORTH IMPROVING EVEN WHEN YOU DO NOT PICK IT.** The `CF-76-1` re-census found a **SECOND matcher with the same bug** (`route_match_matches`, `crates/envoy-filter/src/jwt_authn.rs:173-186`), **THREE** unshared query-strip implementations already in-tree, that **`plan_redirect` is already query-strip-correct** (phase 76 pre-paid part of the fix), and that the record's "~4 probes" is an UNDER-COUNT (8-12, ≈900-1100 net LoC, because the two NON-REGRESSION witnesses need an access-log-observing driver). **The standing trap for whoever takes it: fix `route_matches`' ARGUMENT, never mutate `req.path`** — that field feeds the access log, the forwarded upstream target, `plan_redirect` and jwt_authn's `www-authenticate` realm, and NO current test would catch the damage. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-6 CLOSE-OUT — four findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A CLOSE-OUT THAT FLIPS A PARENT ROW MUST ASSERT EACH ROW'S OWN EXPECTED STATUS, NOT ONE SHARED VALUE.** This close-out flipped TWO rows from DIFFERENT starting statuses — `76.2` from `planned` and parent `76` from `in-progress`. A single shared `expect` would have silently skipped one row or aborted after mutating the other. **MEASURED result: `git diff --numstat` exactly `2 2`, a cell-by-cell compare showing f1/f2/f3/f5/f6 SAME on both rows, and the census moving `105 done / 1 in-progress / 1 planned` → `107 done`.** **Assert per-row, and compare cells rather than trusting the join.** **(2) THE LEDGER'S OWN WARNING ABOUT INHERITED LINE NUMBERS PAID OFF IMMEDIATELY.** The previous session's token sweep keyed on the inherited doctrine-bullet line number `128`, swept a BLANK line, and reported a false `109 → 0` total loss. This session located every sweep target BY TEXT (`awk '$0==H'` whole-line equality for the archive headers, an `.index()` on a distinctive substring for the traps-line boundary) and **verified all four top-section archive headers resolve to EXACTLY ONE line each BEFORE any write**, so a miss would abort before mutating. **A close-out RETIRES the active-phase Notes subsection entirely, so its downward shift is larger than a state advance's — never carry a line number across a session.** **(3) THE TRAPS LINE WAS REWRITTEN BY SPLITTING AT A TEXT BOUNDARY, WHICH MAKES THE ADR-0160 RETENTION CHECK STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN HOPEFUL.** Only the leading STATE-specific preamble (MEASURED **1604** of **62510** characters) was replaced; the enduring tail (**60906** characters, from the `[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2)` marker onward) was carried across BYTE-IDENTICALLY by construction. **A token sweep still ran and is still the gate — but a rewrite that preserves a measured byte-range cannot lose an enduring trap by accident.** **(4) A CLOSE-OUT ADDS NO ADR AND NO `### ` NOTES SUBSECTION, AND BOTH ARE MEASURED PRECEDENTS RATHER THAN OMISSIONS.** The 75.1 and 76.1 close-outs both landed ADR-less; the Notes subsection is RETIRED to the archive behind a `> Historical …` breadcrumb, not superseded in place. **Writing either one breaks the next session's checks** — an unexpected `### ` subsection makes the heading-structure check fail, and a gratuitous ADR moves the head the next session re-derives. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2) — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION.]** **(1) A FRESH REVIEWER RE-DERIVES THE PRIOR ROUND'S FINDINGS, AND THE ONLY GUARD IS READING THE PRIOR REVIEW.** THREE of five read-only dimensions surfaced round-1 items as if new — **M-7, M-9, N-4, N-5, N-8, N-9** — and TWO of them graded a banked Minor as an **ISSUE**. Nothing about a subagent's severity is trustworthy on this axis, because the subagent cannot know what was already banked. **Read the prior `REVIEW.md` before grading anything, and record every re-derived finding as STATUS rather than re-issuing it** (`REVIEW-2.md` §7 exists precisely for this). **(2) INDEPENDENT CONVERGENCE BY TWO DIMENSIONS ON AN UNPROMPTED FINDING IS WORTH MORE THAN EITHER REPORT.** M2-2 (`port_redirect` has no differential witness) was reached by one dimension censusing probes against routes and by another hand-executing a `strip_port` deletion against all 19 probes. Neither was asked for it. **Weight a finding by how many independent routes reached it, not by the confidence of the report.** **(3) A FIX THAT RE-ANCHORS AN ARTIFACT MUST RE-SWEEP THE PROSE THAT JUSTIFIED THE OLD ONE.** The M-2 fix re-anchored `q02` onto its own `/q2-hostport` route and carried forward the justification "q02 and r01 agree on the expected `location`" — TRUE of the original `/a-host` Q2, FALSE of the shipped one, and now wrong in THREE documents; `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` refutes itself nine lines apart (`:3018` vs `:3025`). The scheduled next widening (`regex_rewrite`, a declared non-goal at `SPEC.md:477`) adds a third `return Err` inside `validate_redirect_oneofs` in `bootstrap.rs`, whose doc carries no reciprocal warning — reproducing I-1 exactly. **Put the forcing-function warning on the file that will be EDITED, not on the file that will BREAK.** **(5) A LESSON PARAGRAPH CAN CONTRADICT ITSELF WITH ITS OWN NUMBERS.** `PROGRESS.md:2535` states the fixture carries "14×301, 2×302" — that is the **MUTATED** tree's census, captured while `q02`'s `expected_status` was flipped 301→302 for a negative control; the shipped fixture is **15×301, 1×302**. Pinned in a dedicated test instead — same coverage, guard intact, table's authority uncompromised, deviation RECORDED (`PROGRESS.md` §R3.7) rather than silently taken. **(5) WHEN A GUARD FIRES CORRECTLY ON A REAL DEFECT, EXTEND WHAT IT GUARDS — DO NOT REMOVE THE GUARD.** The tempting reading of I-1 is "`unreachable!()` was the bug, delete it". It was not: the bug was a WIDENED PRODUCER with an UNEXTENDED CONSUMER. The arm stays; its comment now says **six** and carries the cross-crate warning. **And the general rule that produced I-1 in the first place: when a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not tell you, because `unreachable!()` compiles clean.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-5 CODE REVIEW — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION, not quoted from a subagent.]** **(1) WIDENING A FUNCTION'S RETURNABLE ERROR SET IS A CROSS-CRATE CHANGE, AND `unreachable!()` IS WHERE IT LANDS.** Task 8 added a `validate_redirect_oneofs` call inside `reparse_and_select_route_config` (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs:159`), so that function can now return `RedirectPathRewriteConflict`/`RedirectSchemeRewriteConflict`. Its SOLE production caller (`crates/envoy-http1/src/rds_watcher.rs:184`) classifies exactly FOUR variants and ends `other => unreachable!(…)` (`:216-222`) — and the comment at `:211-215` states the invariant the phase broke VERBATIM. `Cargo.toml:42` is `panic = "abort"`, so the reload ABORTS THE PROCESS. **`unreachable!()` compiles clean, so gate (e) is structurally blind to it; only a `reload()`-LEVEL test could have caught it, and all four existing ones test other variants.** **When a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not.** **(2) A CONTRACT THAT DISCLAIMS A CELL AND THEN CLAIMS IT IS TESTED IS WORSE THAN SILENCE.** `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md:3122-3124` correctly labels §F items 7/8 as CHOICES rather than measurements, then says they are "pinned by in-process tests". **MEASURED FALSE for both**: all eight test call sites of `plan_redirect` pass `Some(...)`, and the 22-row table CANNOT express `None` because its `cell()` constructor hard-wires `prefix: Some(prefix)` (`hcm.rs:10484`) and all 22 rows go through it (0 direct `Cell {` literals). **A `Option` FIELD ON A TEST-TABLE STRUCT PROVES NOTHING IF THE CONSTRUCTOR CAN ONLY PRODUCE `Some` — check the constructor, not the type.** **(3) A PROBE PAIR NAMED AS A WITNESS IN A DOC COMMENT MUST BE RE-DERIVED, NOT READ.** `tests/differential/tests/route_redirect_action.rs:9-10` claims `q01` vs `r01` witnesses the `host_redirect` port-DROP. Re-deriving first-match-wins selection over the parsed config: **9** routes set `host_redirect`, **all 9** are probed with an UNPORTED Host, and the only two ported probes hit `https_redirect`/`{}` routes — so **0 of 18** probes can witness it, on the rule SPEC §2.4(b) itself calls the one most likely to be got wrong. **The cell IS pinned in-process (`hcm.rs:10671-10679`); it is UNCOMPARED, not unpinned — say which.** **(4) A SUBAGENT'S LINE NUMBERS DRIFT EVEN WHEN ITS REASONING IS RIGHT.** One dimension's `hcm.rs` citations were consistently **~12 lines high** (`:2331` for a line at `:2319`) while every one of its CONCLUSIONS held. **Re-read every citation; do not inherit a line number from a review either.** **(5) AN UNVERIFIED UPSTREAM HYPOTHESIS MUST NOT BE GRADED AS A FINDING.** A dimension proposed that upstream strips a DEFAULT port (`:80`/`:443`) on a scheme change, explicitly labelling it *"a hypothesis from upstream implementation shape, not from anything on disk"*. It is recorded in `REVIEW.md` §5 as an UNGRADED hypothesis with the two probes that would settle it — never as a defect. **D-3.3: the contract is the contract; you do not read upstream source to decide what equivalence means.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-4 VERIFICATION — five findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A DOCUMENTED HOST STALL DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND THAT ABSENCE IS ITSELF A MEASUREMENT.** The state-3 session recorded — and the handoff instructed state 4 to budget for — a hard stall on `xds_rds_hot_reload` that forced its `-p differential` sweep to be killed after ~11 minutes and left gate (b) unadjudicated. **THREE consecutive whole-workspace sweeps completed in ~5½ minutes each with all 163 binaries reporting, and `xds_rds_hot_reload` passes in isolation in 1.98 s.** An environmental stall is not a property of the TREE. **Re-measure an inherited time budget before spending it, and do not read a stall's absence as a different tree.** **(2) THE ONE RED SITTING ON THE PHASE'S OWN SURFACE IS THE ONE WORTH CHASING.** Seven of the eight REDs were trivially off-surface; `xds_rds_hot_reload_fixture` was NOT — Task 8 rewrote exactly that file's validation path (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs`, `if let` → exhaustive `match`). Disbelieve a zero.** **(5) A LANDED PLAN'S TEST-COUNT PREDICTION IS NOT A BASELINE — THE DIFF IS.** `76.2/PLAN.md` §6 predicted `passed≈2168` from "~30 new tests"; the measured `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` attribute delta is **+11 / −0**, and both identities close exactly on 11 (`162 + 1 = 163` binaries, `2137 + 11 = 2148` passed). The gap is the table-driven 22-cell design the plan itself chose. **Do NOT read `2148` against `2168` as "tests were lost".** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-3 IMPLEMENTATION — eight findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A PLAN'S LITERAL RUST CAN BE PRE-FLIGHTED AND STILL BROKEN — THREE DEFECTS IN ONE PLAN.** `PLAN.md` §2 claimed Tasks 1-5/8/9 passed `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` in a scratch worktree, and THREE literals still failed: T3-3's `Some("/é"[..2].into())` **panics in the test itself** (`"/é"` is 3 bytes, so byte index 2 is not a char boundary) and never reaches the function under test; T3-2's assert message `"a bare redirect{} rewrites nothing"` **does not compile** (`assert_eq!`'s third arg is a FORMAT STRING, so the bare `{}` is a positional placeholder); and T7-1's `HttpVersion::Http2` **does not exist** (the enum has exactly `Http10` and `Http11`). **THE ROOT CAUSE IS GENERAL: `fmt` and `clippy` DO NOT EXECUTE TESTS, and the pre-flight RAN only 2 of the new tests** — so a runtime panic in a third was invisible to it, and a block that never compiled cannot have passed the lint it was claimed to pass. **Treat a pre-flight's own claim as a CLAIM; transcribe verbatim, then COMPILE AND RUN.** **(2) A PER-TASK LINT GATE CAN BE UNACHIEVABLE UNDER THE PLAN'S OWN TASK SPLIT.** `PLAN.md`'s Global Constraint says `clippy -D warnings` must be clean at EVERY task boundary; measured, Tasks 2/3/4 each add a NON-TEST item whose only NON-TEST consumer is Task 5, so each boundary is `unused import` / `never constructed` / `never used` → **exit 101**. It does not — the call compiles, and the RED is the pure behavioural `left: 501, right: 301`, which is BETTER evidence. **Do not treat a plan's predicted failure MODE as a checkable fact.** **(4) `envoy-bin` HAS NO `--mode` FLAG.** `PLAN.md` Task 10's `--mode validate` exits **2** with `unknown argument: --mode`; `crates/envoy-bin/src/argv.rs:27-29` accepts EXACTLY `-c <path>` or `--config-path <path>` (clap is deliberately avoided per D-3.2). Validate instead by substituting `{{PORT}}` and booting under `timeout`: exit **124** (still running) with zero errors proves the config parses AND the listener binds — strictly stronger. **(5) THE STRONGEST SEAM EVIDENCE IS A CROSS-CRATE MUTATION.** Mutating `plan_redirect` in **`crates/envoy-http1`** turned an **`crates/envoy-http2`** test RED (`left: Some("http://envoy-rust.test/a-host")`). That does not merely assert H2 reaches the arm — it PROVES H2's answer is COMPUTED BY the H1 arm. **When a claim is "one implementation serves two consumers", mutate the implementation and watch the OTHER consumer fail.** **(6) A FULL LOCAL `-p differential` SWEEP STALLS ON `xds_rds_hot_reload` ON THIS HOST** (virtiofs, no inotify).
