':(exclude)docs/'`, +1334/−69) against the plan's ≈1202 code-only projection — **+5%**, versus `76.1`'s **+50%**. The table-driven 22-cell design held (it was NOT expanded into 22 `#[test]` fns), §6.1's mid-execution trigger never fired, and **no split was needed**. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-2 PLAN-WRITE — six findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A SPLIT SIBLING'S LANDING STALE-DATES THE OTHER SPEC, AND THE DRIFT IS NOT UNIFORM.** `76.2/SPEC.md` was written at `f438cb9`, before `76.1`. This session located every sweep target BY TEXT (`awk '$0==H'` whole-line equality for the archive headers, an `.index()` on a distinctive substring for the traps-line boundary) and **verified all four top-section archive headers resolve to EXACTLY ONE line each BEFORE any write**, so a miss would abort before mutating. **A close-out RETIRES the active-phase Notes subsection entirely, so its downward shift is larger than a state advance's — never carry a line number across a session.** **(3) THE TRAPS LINE WAS REWRITTEN BY SPLITTING AT A TEXT BOUNDARY, WHICH MAKES THE ADR-0160 RETENTION CHECK STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN HOPEFUL.** Only the leading STATE-specific preamble (MEASURED **1604** of **62510** characters) was replaced; the enduring tail (**60906** characters, from the `[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2)` marker onward) was carried across BYTE-IDENTICALLY by construction. **A token sweep still ran and is still the gate — but a rewrite that preserves a measured byte-range cannot lose an enduring trap by accident.** **(4) A CLOSE-OUT ADDS NO ADR AND NO `### ` NOTES SUBSECTION, AND BOTH ARE MEASURED PRECEDENTS RATHER THAN OMISSIONS.** The 75.1 and 76.1 close-outs both landed ADR-less; the Notes subsection is RETIRED to the archive behind a `> Historical …` breadcrumb, not superseded in place. **Writing either one breaks the next session's checks** — an unexpected `### ` subsection makes the heading-structure check fail, and a gratuitous ADR moves the head the next session re-derives. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2) — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION.]** **(1) A FRESH REVIEWER RE-DERIVES THE PRIOR ROUND'S FINDINGS, AND THE ONLY GUARD IS READING THE PRIOR REVIEW.** THREE of five read-only dimensions surfaced round-1 items as if new — **M-7, M-9, N-4, N-5, N-8, N-9** — and TWO of them graded a banked Minor as an **ISSUE**. Nothing about a subagent's severity is trustworthy on this axis, because the subagent cannot know what was already banked. **Read the prior `REVIEW.md` before grading anything, and record every re-derived finding as STATUS rather than re-issuing it** (`REVIEW-2.md` §7 exists precisely for this). **(2) INDEPENDENT CONVERGENCE BY TWO DIMENSIONS ON AN UNPROMPTED FINDING IS WORTH MORE THAN EITHER REPORT.** M2-2 (`port_redirect` has no differential witness) was reached by one dimension censusing probes against routes and by another hand-executing a `strip_port` deletion against all 19 probes. Neither was asked for it. **Weight a finding by how many independent routes reached it, not by the confidence of the report.** **(3) A FIX THAT RE-ANCHORS AN ARTIFACT MUST RE-SWEEP THE PROSE THAT JUSTIFIED THE OLD ONE.** The M-2 fix re-anchored `q02` onto its own `/q2-hostport` route and carried forward the justification "q02 and r01 agree on the expected `location`" — TRUE of the original `/a-host` Q2, FALSE of the shipped one, and now wrong in THREE documents; `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` refutes itself nine lines apart (`:3018` vs `:3025`). The arm stays; its comment now says **six** and carries the cross-crate warning. **And the general rule that produced I-1 in the first place: when a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not tell you, because `unreachable!()` compiles clean.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-5 CODE REVIEW — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION, not quoted from a subagent.]** **(1) WIDENING A FUNCTION'S RETURNABLE ERROR SET IS A CROSS-CRATE CHANGE, AND `unreachable!()` IS WHERE IT LANDS.** Task 8 added a `validate_redirect_oneofs` call inside `reparse_and_select_route_config` (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs:159`), so that function can now return `RedirectPathRewriteConflict`/`RedirectSchemeRewriteConflict`. It is recorded in `REVIEW.md` §5 as an UNGRADED hypothesis with the two probes that would settle it — never as a defect. **D-3.3: the contract is the contract; you do not read upstream source to decide what equivalence means.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-4 VERIFICATION — five findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A DOCUMENTED HOST STALL DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND THAT ABSENCE IS ITSELF A MEASUREMENT.** The state-3 session recorded — and the handoff instructed state 4 to budget for — a hard stall on `xds_rds_hot_reload` that forced its `-p differential` sweep to be killed after ~11 minutes and left gate (b) unadjudicated. **THREE consecutive whole-workspace sweeps completed in ~5½ minutes each with all 163 binaries reporting, and `xds_rds_hot_reload` passes in isolation in 1.98 s.** An environmental stall is not a property of the TREE. **Re-measure an inherited time budget before spending it, and do not read a stall's absence as a different tree.** **(2) THE ONE RED SITTING ON THE PHASE'S OWN SURFACE IS THE ONE WORTH CHASING.** Seven of the eight REDs were trivially off-surface; `xds_rds_hot_reload_fixture` was NOT — Task 8 rewrote exactly that file's validation path (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs`, `if let` → exhaustive `match`). The gap is the table-driven 22-cell design the plan itself chose. **Do NOT read `2148` against `2168` as "tests were lost".** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-3 IMPLEMENTATION — eight findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A PLAN'S LITERAL RUST CAN BE PRE-FLIGHTED AND STILL BROKEN — THREE DEFECTS IN ONE PLAN.** `PLAN.md` §2 claimed Tasks 1-5/8/9 passed `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` in a scratch worktree, and THREE literals still failed: T3-3's `Some("/é"[..2].into())` **panics in the test itself** (`"/é"` is 3 bytes, so byte index 2 is not a char boundary) and never reaches the function under test; T3-2's assert message `"a bare redirect{} rewrites nothing"` **does not compile** (`assert_eq!`'s third arg is a FORMAT STRING, so the bare `{}` is a positional placeholder); and T7-1's `HttpVersion::Http2` **does not exist** (the enum has exactly `Http10` and `Http11`). **THE ROOT CAUSE IS GENERAL: `fmt` and `clippy` DO NOT EXECUTE TESTS, and the pre-flight RAN only 2 of the new tests** — so a runtime panic in a third was invisible to it, and a block that never compiled cannot have passed the lint it was claimed to pass. **Treat a pre-flight's own claim as a CLAIM; transcribe verbatim, then COMPILE AND RUN.** **(2) A PER-TASK LINT GATE CAN BE UNACHIEVABLE UNDER THE PLAN'S OWN TASK SPLIT.** `PLAN.md`'s Global Constraint says `clippy -D warnings` must be clean at EVERY task boundary; measured, Tasks 2/3/4 each add a NON-TEST item whose only NON-TEST consumer is Task 5, so each boundary is `unused import` / `never constructed` / `never used` → **exit 101**. ':(exclude)docs/'`, +1334/−69) against the plan's ≈1202 code-only projection — **+5%**, versus `76.1`'s **+50%**. The table-driven 22-cell design held (it was NOT expanded into 22 `#[test]` fns), §6.1's mid-execution trigger never fired, and **no split was needed**. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-2 PLAN-WRITE — six findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A SPLIT SIBLING'S LANDING STALE-DATES THE OTHER SPEC, AND THE DRIFT IS NOT UNIFORM.** `76.2/SPEC.md` was written at `f438cb9`, before `76.1`. None becomes wrong when a `static_layer` store lands without RTDS or consumers — **but a reviewer meeting that test name inside a phase titled "runtime" will read a contradiction unless the SPEC pre-empts it.** **Grep for tests and docs that assert the ABSENCE of what you are about to build.** **(6) A REJECTED CANDIDATE'S RECORD IS WORTH IMPROVING EVEN WHEN YOU DO NOT PICK IT.** The `CF-76-1` re-census found a **SECOND matcher with the same bug** (`route_match_matches`, `crates/envoy-filter/src/jwt_authn.rs:173-186`), **THREE** unshared query-strip implementations already in-tree, that **`plan_redirect` is already query-strip-correct** (phase 76 pre-paid part of the fix), and that the record's "~4 probes" is an UNDER-COUNT (8-12, ≈900-1100 net LoC, because the two NON-REGRESSION witnesses need an access-log-observing driver). **The standing trap for whoever takes it: fix `route_matches`' ARGUMENT, never mutate `req.path`** — that field feeds the access log, the forwarded upstream target, `plan_redirect` and jwt_authn's `www-authenticate` realm, and NO current test would catch the damage. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-6 CLOSE-OUT — four findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A CLOSE-OUT THAT FLIPS A PARENT ROW MUST ASSERT EACH ROW'S OWN EXPECTED STATUS, NOT ONE SHARED VALUE.** This close-out flipped TWO rows from DIFFERENT starting statuses — `76.2` from `planned` and parent `76` from `in-progress`. A single shared `expect` would have silently skipped one row or aborted after mutating the other. **MEASURED result: `git diff --numstat` exactly `2 2`, a cell-by-cell compare showing f1/f2/f3/f5/f6 SAME on both rows, and the census moving `105 done / 1 in-progress / 1 planned` → `107 done`.** **Assert per-row, and compare cells rather than trusting the join.** **(2) THE LEDGER'S OWN WARNING ABOUT INHERITED LINE NUMBERS PAID OFF IMMEDIATELY.** The previous session's token sweep keyed on the inherited doctrine-bullet line number `128`, swept a BLANK line, and reported a false `109 → 0` total loss. This session located every sweep target BY TEXT (`awk '$0==H'` whole-line equality for the archive headers, an `.index()` on a distinctive substring for the traps-line boundary) and **verified all four top-section archive headers resolve to EXACTLY ONE line each BEFORE any write**, so a miss would abort before mutating. **A close-out RETIRES the active-phase Notes subsection entirely, so its downward shift is larger than a state advance's — never carry a line number across a session.** **(3) THE TRAPS LINE WAS REWRITTEN BY SPLITTING AT A TEXT BOUNDARY, WHICH MAKES THE ADR-0160 RETENTION CHECK STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN HOPEFUL.** Only the leading STATE-specific preamble (MEASURED **1604** of **62510** characters) was replaced; the enduring tail (**60906** characters, from the `[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2)` marker onward) was carried across BYTE-IDENTICALLY by construction. **A token sweep still ran and is still the gate — but a rewrite that preserves a measured byte-range cannot lose an enduring trap by accident.** **(4) A CLOSE-OUT ADDS NO ADR AND NO `### ` NOTES SUBSECTION, AND BOTH ARE MEASURED PRECEDENTS RATHER THAN OMISSIONS.** The 75.1 and 76.1 close-outs both landed ADR-less; the Notes subsection is RETIRED to the archive behind a `> Historical …` breadcrumb, not superseded in place. **Writing either one breaks the next session's checks** — an unexpected `### ` subsection makes the heading-structure check fail, and a gratuitous ADR moves the head the next session re-derives. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2) — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION.]** **(1) A FRESH REVIEWER RE-DERIVES THE PRIOR ROUND'S FINDINGS, AND THE ONLY GUARD IS READING THE PRIOR REVIEW.** THREE of five read-only dimensions surfaced round-1 items as if new — **M-7, M-9, N-4, N-5, N-8, N-9** — and TWO of them graded a banked Minor as an **ISSUE**. Nothing about a subagent's severity is trustworthy on this axis, because the subagent cannot know what was already banked. **Read the prior `REVIEW.md` before grading anything, and record every re-derived finding as STATUS rather than re-issuing it** (`REVIEW-2.md` §7 exists precisely for this). **(2) INDEPENDENT CONVERGENCE BY TWO DIMENSIONS ON AN UNPROMPTED FINDING IS WORTH MORE THAN EITHER REPORT.** M2-2 (`port_redirect` has no differential witness) was reached by one dimension censusing probes against routes and by another hand-executing a `strip_port` deletion against all 19 probes. Neither was asked for it. **Weight a finding by how many independent routes reached it, not by the confidence of the report.** **(3) A FIX THAT RE-ANCHORS AN ARTIFACT MUST RE-SWEEP THE PROSE THAT JUSTIFIED THE OLD ONE.** The M-2 fix re-anchored `q02` onto its own `/q2-hostport` route and carried forward the justification "q02 and r01 agree on the expected `location`" — TRUE of the original `/a-host` Q2, FALSE of the shipped one, and now wrong in THREE documents; `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` refutes itself nine lines apart (`:3018` vs `:3025`). The scheduled next widening (`regex_rewrite`, a declared non-goal at `SPEC.md:477`) adds a third `return Err` inside `validate_redirect_oneofs` in `bootstrap.rs`, whose doc carries no reciprocal warning — reproducing I-1 exactly. **Put the forcing-function warning on the file that will be EDITED, not on the file that will BREAK.** **(5) A LESSON PARAGRAPH CAN CONTRADICT ITSELF WITH ITS OWN NUMBERS.** `PROGRESS.md:2535` states the fixture carries "14×301, 2×302" — that is the **MUTATED** tree's census, captured while `q02`'s `expected_status` was flipped 301→302 for a negative control; the shipped fixture is **15×301, 1×302**. It sits inside the paragraph whose lesson is "re-derive it from the artifact". **A census measured under a mutation is not the artifact's census — re-derive it after reverting.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-4 RE-VERIFICATION — five findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) `touch` CREATES FILES, AND A "HARMLESS" MTIME BUMP MUTATED THE TREE AND MANUFACTURED FOUR PHANTOM CLIPPY ERRORS.** Forcing a full clippy re-check by `touch`ing a hand-written list of `crates/*/src/{lib,main}.rs` created **22 EMPTY FILES** at paths that did not exist (e.g. `crates/envoy-config/src/main.rs`, `tests/helpers/helper-common/src/main.rs`); clippy then exited **101** with 4 `error` lines that looked exactly like a real gate-(e) failure and were entirely artifacts of the probe. READ THE FAILURE TEXT, and gate on the `test result` line's existence, not the exit code.** **(2) AN ABORT-AT-FIRST-FAILURE DRIVER CAN BE TURNED INTO A MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT.** `Http1ProbeList` stopping at the first red probe is normally a limitation (one run names one probe). Under MUT-D it was the PROOF: it named `q02`, the **18th** probe in list order, so every earlier probe necessarily PASSED under the mutation — which is exactly the claim ("this mutation survives all 18 original probes") that needed establishing. **Reason about probe ORDER and a limitation becomes evidence.** **(3) "MAKE THE CLAIM TRUE" BEAT "DELETE THE CLAIM" ON BOTH DOC FINDINGS, AND CHEAPLY.** M-1 and M-2 each offered a soften-the-doc option. Taken literally that forces the `cells.len() == 22` guard to 23 and mixes an INVENTED cell into a table whose entire meaning is "MEASURED against v1.33.0". Pinned in a dedicated test instead — same coverage, guard intact, table's authority uncompromised, deviation RECORDED (`PROGRESS.md` §R3.7) rather than silently taken. **(5) WHEN A GUARD FIRES CORRECTLY ON A REAL DEFECT, EXTEND WHAT IT GUARDS — DO NOT REMOVE THE GUARD.** The tempting reading of I-1 is "`unreachable!()` was the bug, delete it". It was not: the bug was a WIDENED PRODUCER with an UNEXTENDED CONSUMER. The arm stays; its comment now says **six** and carries the cross-crate warning. **And the general rule that produced I-1 in the first place: when a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not tell you, because `unreachable!()` compiles clean.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-5 CODE REVIEW — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION, not quoted from a subagent.]** **(1) WIDENING A FUNCTION'S RETURNABLE ERROR SET IS A CROSS-CRATE CHANGE, AND `unreachable!()` IS WHERE IT LANDS.** Task 8 added a `validate_redirect_oneofs` call inside `reparse_and_select_route_config` (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs:159`), so that function can now return `RedirectPathRewriteConflict`/`RedirectSchemeRewriteConflict`. Its SOLE production caller (`crates/envoy-http1/src/rds_watcher.rs:184`) classifies exactly FOUR variants and ends `other => unreachable!(…)` (`:216-222`) — and the comment at `:211-215` states the invariant the phase broke VERBATIM. `Cargo.toml:42` is `panic = "abort"`, so the reload ABORTS THE PROCESS. **`unreachable!()` compiles clean, so gate (e) is structurally blind to it; only a `reload()`-LEVEL test could have caught it, and all four existing ones test other variants.** **When a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not.** **(2) A CONTRACT THAT DISCLAIMS A CELL AND THEN CLAIMS IT IS TESTED IS WORSE THAN SILENCE.** `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md:3122-3124` correctly labels §F items 7/8 as CHOICES rather than measurements, then says they are "pinned by in-process tests". **MEASURED FALSE for both**: all eight test call sites of `plan_redirect` pass `Some(...)`, and the 22-row table CANNOT express `None` because its `cell()` constructor hard-wires `prefix: Some(prefix)` (`hcm.rs:10484`) and all 22 rows go through it (0 direct `Cell {` literals). **A `Option` FIELD ON A TEST-TABLE STRUCT PROVES NOTHING IF THE CONSTRUCTOR CAN ONLY PRODUCE `Some` — check the constructor, not the type.** **(3) A PROBE PAIR NAMED AS A WITNESS IN A DOC COMMENT MUST BE RE-DERIVED, NOT READ.** `tests/differential/tests/route_redirect_action.rs:9-10` claims `q01` vs `r01` witnesses the `host_redirect` port-DROP. Re-deriving first-match-wins selection over the parsed config: **9** routes set `host_redirect`, **all 9** are probed with an UNPORTED Host, and the only two ported probes hit `https_redirect`/`{}` routes — so **0 of 18** probes can witness it, on the rule SPEC §2.4(b) itself calls the one most likely to be got wrong. **The cell IS pinned in-process (`hcm.rs:10671-10679`); it is UNCOMPARED, not unpinned — say which.** **(4) A SUBAGENT'S LINE NUMBERS DRIFT EVEN WHEN ITS REASONING IS RIGHT.** One dimension's `hcm.rs` citations were consistently **~12 lines high** (`:2331` for a line at `:2319`) while every one of its CONCLUSIONS held. **Re-read every citation; do not inherit a line number from a review either.** **(5) AN UNVERIFIED UPSTREAM HYPOTHESIS MUST NOT BE GRADED AS A FINDING.** A dimension proposed that upstream strips a DEFAULT port (`:80`/`:443`) on a scheme change, explicitly labelling it *"a hypothesis from upstream implementation shape, not from anything on disk"*. It is recorded in `REVIEW.md` §5 as an UNGRADED hypothesis with the two probes that would settle it — never as a defect. **D-3.3: the contract is the contract; you do not read upstream source to decide what equivalence means.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-4 VERIFICATION — five findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A DOCUMENTED HOST STALL DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND THAT ABSENCE IS ITSELF A MEASUREMENT.** The state-3 session recorded — and the handoff instructed state 4 to budget for — a hard stall on `xds_rds_hot_reload` that forced its `-p differential` sweep to be killed after ~11 minutes and left gate (b) unadjudicated. **THREE consecutive whole-workspace sweeps completed in ~5½ minutes each with all 163 binaries reporting, and `xds_rds_hot_reload` passes in isolation in 1.98 s.** An environmental stall is not a property of the TREE. **Re-measure an inherited time budget before spending it, and do not read a stall's absence as a different tree.** **(2) THE ONE RED SITTING ON THE PHASE'S OWN SURFACE IS THE ONE WORTH CHASING.** Seven of the eight REDs were trivially off-surface; `xds_rds_hot_reload_fixture` was NOT — Task 8 rewrote exactly that file's validation path (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs`, `if let` → exhaustive `match`). Disbelieve a zero.** **(5) A LANDED PLAN'S TEST-COUNT PREDICTION IS NOT A BASELINE — THE DIFF IS.** `76.2/PLAN.md` §6 predicted `passed≈2168` from "~30 new tests"; the measured `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` attribute delta is **+11 / −0**, and both identities close exactly on 11 (`162 + 1 = 163` binaries, `2137 + 11 = 2148` passed). The gap is the table-driven 22-cell design the plan itself chose. **Do NOT read `2148` against `2168` as "tests were lost".** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-3 IMPLEMENTATION — eight findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A PLAN'S LITERAL RUST CAN BE PRE-FLIGHTED AND STILL BROKEN — THREE DEFECTS IN ONE PLAN.** `PLAN.md` §2 claimed Tasks 1-5/8/9 passed `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` in a scratch worktree, and THREE literals still failed: T3-3's `Some("/é"[..2].into())` **panics in the test itself** (`"/é"` is 3 bytes, so byte index 2 is not a char boundary) and never reaches the function under test; T3-2's assert message `"a bare redirect{} rewrites nothing"` **does not compile** (`assert_eq!`'s third arg is a FORMAT STRING, so the bare `{}` is a positional placeholder); and T7-1's `HttpVersion::Http2` **does not exist** (the enum has exactly `Http10` and `Http11`). **THE ROOT CAUSE IS GENERAL: `fmt` and `clippy` DO NOT EXECUTE TESTS, and the pre-flight RAN only 2 of the new tests** — so a runtime panic in a third was invisible to it, and a block that never compiled cannot have passed the lint it was claimed to pass. **Treat a pre-flight's own claim as a CLAIM; transcribe verbatim, then COMPILE AND RUN.** **(2) A PER-TASK LINT GATE CAN BE UNACHIEVABLE UNDER THE PLAN'S OWN TASK SPLIT.** `PLAN.md`'s Global Constraint says `clippy -D warnings` must be clean at EVERY task boundary; measured, Tasks 2/3/4 each add a NON-TEST item whose only NON-TEST consumer is Task 5, so each boundary is `unused import` / `never constructed` / `never used` → **exit 101**. It does not — the call compiles, and the RED is the pure behavioural `left: 501, right: 301`, which is BETTER evidence. **Do not treat a plan's predicted failure MODE as a checkable fact.** **(4) `envoy-bin` HAS NO `--mode` FLAG.** `PLAN.md` Task 10's `--mode validate` exits **2** with `unknown argument: --mode`; `crates/envoy-bin/src/argv.rs:27-29` accepts EXACTLY `-c <path>` or `--config-path <path>` (clap is deliberately avoided per D-3.2). Validate instead by substituting `{{PORT}}` and booting under `timeout`: exit **124** (still running) with zero errors proves the config parses AND the listener binds — strictly stronger. **(5) THE STRONGEST SEAM EVIDENCE IS A CROSS-CRATE MUTATION.** Mutating `plan_redirect` in **`crates/envoy-http1`** turned an **`crates/envoy-http2`** test RED (`left: Some("http://envoy-rust.test/a-host")`). That does not merely assert H2 reaches the arm — it PROVES H2's answer is COMPUTED BY the H1 arm. **When a claim is "one implementation serves two consumers", mutate the implementation and watch the OTHER consumer fail.** **(6) A FULL LOCAL `-p differential` SWEEP STALLS ON `xds_rds_hot_reload` ON THIS HOST** (virtiofs, no inotify). ':(exclude)docs/'`, +1334/−69) against the plan's ≈1202 code-only projection — **+5%**, versus `76.1`'s **+50%**. The table-driven 22-cell design held (it was NOT expanded into 22 `#[test]` fns), §6.1's mid-execution trigger never fired, and **no split was needed**. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-2 PLAN-WRITE — six findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A SPLIT SIBLING'S LANDING STALE-DATES THE OTHER SPEC, AND THE DRIFT IS NOT UNIFORM.** `76.2/SPEC.md` was written at `f438cb9`, before `76.1`. This session located every sweep target BY TEXT (`awk '$0==H'` whole-line equality for the archive headers, an `.index()` on a distinctive substring for the traps-line boundary) and **verified all four top-section archive headers resolve to EXACTLY ONE line each BEFORE any write**, so a miss would abort before mutating. **A close-out RETIRES the active-phase Notes subsection entirely, so its downward shift is larger than a state advance's — never carry a line number across a session.** **(3) THE TRAPS LINE WAS REWRITTEN BY SPLITTING AT A TEXT BOUNDARY, WHICH MAKES THE ADR-0160 RETENTION CHECK STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN HOPEFUL.** Only the leading STATE-specific preamble (MEASURED **1604** of **62510** characters) was replaced; the enduring tail (**60906** characters, from the `[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2)` marker onward) was carried across BYTE-IDENTICALLY by construction. **A token sweep still ran and is still the gate — but a rewrite that preserves a measured byte-range cannot lose an enduring trap by accident.** **(4) A CLOSE-OUT ADDS NO ADR AND NO `### ` NOTES SUBSECTION, AND BOTH ARE MEASURED PRECEDENTS RATHER THAN OMISSIONS.** The 75.1 and 76.1 close-outs both landed ADR-less; the Notes subsection is RETIRED to the archive behind a `> Historical …` breadcrumb, not superseded in place. **Writing either one breaks the next session's checks** — an unexpected `### ` subsection makes the heading-structure check fail, and a gratuitous ADR moves the head the next session re-derives. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 §5 STATE-5 RE-REVIEW (round 2) — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION.]** **(1) A FRESH REVIEWER RE-DERIVES THE PRIOR ROUND'S FINDINGS, AND THE ONLY GUARD IS READING THE PRIOR REVIEW.** THREE of five read-only dimensions surfaced round-1 items as if new — **M-7, M-9, N-4, N-5, N-8, N-9** — and TWO of them graded a banked Minor as an **ISSUE**. Nothing about a subagent's severity is trustworthy on this axis, because the subagent cannot know what was already banked. **Read the prior `REVIEW.md` before grading anything, and record every re-derived finding as STATUS rather than re-issuing it** (`REVIEW-2.md` §7 exists precisely for this). **(2) INDEPENDENT CONVERGENCE BY TWO DIMENSIONS ON AN UNPROMPTED FINDING IS WORTH MORE THAN EITHER REPORT.** M2-2 (`port_redirect` has no differential witness) was reached by one dimension censusing probes against routes and by another hand-executing a `strip_port` deletion against all 19 probes. Neither was asked for it. **Weight a finding by how many independent routes reached it, not by the confidence of the report.** **(3) A FIX THAT RE-ANCHORS AN ARTIFACT MUST RE-SWEEP THE PROSE THAT JUSTIFIED THE OLD ONE.** The M-2 fix re-anchored `q02` onto its own `/q2-hostport` route and carried forward the justification "q02 and r01 agree on the expected `location`" — TRUE of the original `/a-host` Q2, FALSE of the shipped one, and now wrong in THREE documents; `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` refutes itself nine lines apart (`:3018` vs `:3025`). The arm stays; its comment now says **six** and carries the cross-crate warning. **And the general rule that produced I-1 in the first place: when a phase adds an `Err` arm, GREP THE CALLERS OF THE FUNCTION IT SITS IN — the compiler will not tell you, because `unreachable!()` compiles clean.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-5 CODE REVIEW — five findings, every one MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION, not quoted from a subagent.]** **(1) WIDENING A FUNCTION'S RETURNABLE ERROR SET IS A CROSS-CRATE CHANGE, AND `unreachable!()` IS WHERE IT LANDS.** Task 8 added a `validate_redirect_oneofs` call inside `reparse_and_select_route_config` (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs:159`), so that function can now return `RedirectPathRewriteConflict`/`RedirectSchemeRewriteConflict`. It is recorded in `REVIEW.md` §5 as an UNGRADED hypothesis with the two probes that would settle it — never as a defect. **D-3.3: the contract is the contract; you do not read upstream source to decide what equivalence means.** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-4 VERIFICATION — five findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A DOCUMENTED HOST STALL DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND THAT ABSENCE IS ITSELF A MEASUREMENT.** The state-3 session recorded — and the handoff instructed state 4 to budget for — a hard stall on `xds_rds_hot_reload` that forced its `-p differential` sweep to be killed after ~11 minutes and left gate (b) unadjudicated. **THREE consecutive whole-workspace sweeps completed in ~5½ minutes each with all 163 binaries reporting, and `xds_rds_hot_reload` passes in isolation in 1.98 s.** An environmental stall is not a property of the TREE. **Re-measure an inherited time budget before spending it, and do not read a stall's absence as a different tree.** **(2) THE ONE RED SITTING ON THE PHASE'S OWN SURFACE IS THE ONE WORTH CHASING.** Seven of the eight REDs were trivially off-surface; `xds_rds_hot_reload_fixture` was NOT — Task 8 rewrote exactly that file's validation path (`crates/envoy-config/src/rds.rs`, `if let` → exhaustive `match`). The gap is the table-driven 22-cell design the plan itself chose. **Do NOT read `2148` against `2168` as "tests were lost".** **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-3 IMPLEMENTATION — eight findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A PLAN'S LITERAL RUST CAN BE PRE-FLIGHTED AND STILL BROKEN — THREE DEFECTS IN ONE PLAN.** `PLAN.md` §2 claimed Tasks 1-5/8/9 passed `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` in a scratch worktree, and THREE literals still failed: T3-3's `Some("/é"[..2].into())` **panics in the test itself** (`"/é"` is 3 bytes, so byte index 2 is not a char boundary) and never reaches the function under test; T3-2's assert message `"a bare redirect{} rewrites nothing"` **does not compile** (`assert_eq!`'s third arg is a FORMAT STRING, so the bare `{}` is a positional placeholder); and T7-1's `HttpVersion::Http2` **does not exist** (the enum has exactly `Http10` and `Http11`). **THE ROOT CAUSE IS GENERAL: `fmt` and `clippy` DO NOT EXECUTE TESTS, and the pre-flight RAN only 2 of the new tests** — so a runtime panic in a third was invisible to it, and a block that never compiled cannot have passed the lint it was claimed to pass. **Treat a pre-flight's own claim as a CLAIM; transcribe verbatim, then COMPILE AND RUN.** **(2) A PER-TASK LINT GATE CAN BE UNACHIEVABLE UNDER THE PLAN'S OWN TASK SPLIT.** `PLAN.md`'s Global Constraint says `clippy -D warnings` must be clean at EVERY task boundary; measured, Tasks 2/3/4 each add a NON-TEST item whose only NON-TEST consumer is Task 5, so each boundary is `unused import` / `never constructed` / `never used` → **exit 101**. ':(exclude)docs/'`, +1334/−69) against the plan's ≈1202 code-only projection — **+5%**, versus `76.1`'s **+50%**. The table-driven 22-cell design held (it was NOT expanded into 22 `#[test]` fns), §6.1's mid-execution trigger never fired, and **no split was needed**. **[NEW AT THE 76.2 STATE-2 PLAN-WRITE — six findings, every one MEASURED.]** **(1) A SPLIT SIBLING'S LANDING STALE-DATES THE OTHER SPEC, AND THE DRIFT IS NOT UNIFORM.** `76.2/SPEC.md` was written at `f438cb9`, before `76.1`. Cold-start reads `STATE.md` FIRST (disk-authoritative). **One state per session; do not chain** (§5.1), and the state-6 close-out and the next-phase state-0/1 PICK are ALWAYS separate sessions. **A REVIEWER MUST NOT FIX WHAT IT GRADES, and the context that wrote an artifact must not grade it** (§5.1; **ADR-0127**, which also records the ONE human-authorized 5→6 chaining exception at phase 66 and why 0→1, 1→2, 2→3, 3→4 and 4→5 must NEVER be chained) — **do not read the git history as licence to chain.** Parallelism is permitted strictly INSIDE one state (READ-ONLY review dimensions; the main session is the SOLE writer of the state ledger and makes every decisive measurement itself), never ACROSS states, and a state-6 close-out is ONE INDIVISIBLE UNIT, SOLO.

A job `cancelled` with `runner_name:""` + `steps:0` never got a runner → rerun the SAME SHA; `cancelled` with FULL step counts is your own follow-up push cancelling the older run and is benign. **Do not push twice in quick succession.** CI has no `paths-ignore`, so docs-only pushes DO build. **THREE `gh`-LOG TRAPS:** `gh` NEEDS ITS CWD INSIDE THE REPO (after a `cd` to a scratch dir it fails with `failed to determine base repo` and writes a ~120-byte file, and the CI-total census over that returns a clean-looking `passed= failed=` — assert `wc -c` is in the hundreds of KB first); **`gh run view --log` RETURNS ONLY ONE JOB**, so a fuzz-only failure is INVISIBLE (enumerate via `gh api repos/pgdad/envoy-rust/actions/runs/<run>/jobs`); and **a loose `warning|error` grep over a CI log is ALL FALSE POSITIVES** (17 hits, 11 of them test NAMES under `error::tests::…`). **A GitHub outage can persist >1h on this host** (`No route to host`) — NOT an auth error. **A NAIVE `awk` FAMILY-HEADING CENSUS UNDER-REPORTS — it returned 1 where the truth is 4.** An `awk` whose first rule matches `/^### .* family/` then calls `next` never reaches a later `/^### /` rule. MEASURED TRUE ANSWER: **four** family headings carry ZERO rows — `### HTTP/3 + QUIC family` (`ROADMAP.md:122`), `### gRPC family` (`:126`), `### Runtime + hot restart family` (`:183`), `### WASM host family` (`:185`). **CONCURRENCY — A PARALLEL WORKSTREAM IS ACTIVE.** FOUR `.claude/worktrees/agent-*` git worktrees plus a long-running container on `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` and a sibling's testcontainers reaper. **LEAVE THEM ALONE**, and **EXCLUDE those worktrees from any repo-wide `find`/census/grep** — they duplicate every `fuzz_targets` dir and will inflate counts; prefer `git ls-files`, or enumerate workspace members from the root `Cargo.toml`. **Re-check `git fetch origin --prune` at session start AND again immediately before your commit** — a clean cold-start `git status` can go dirty mid-session from a sibling; defer to the further-along session and remove only your own artifacts (memory `concurrent-loop-sessions-race-on-phase-pick`). **A SESSION WITHOUT A COMMIT ADVANCES NOTHING** — scratch outputs are session-scoped and unrecoverable; if cut short, label numbers PREDICTIONS, not results. Cold-start reads `STATE.md` FIRST (disk-authoritative). **One state per session; do not chain** (§5.1), and the state-6 close-out and the next-phase state-0/1 PICK are ALWAYS separate sessions. **A REVIEWER MUST NOT FIX WHAT IT GRADES, and the context that wrote an artifact must not grade it** (§5.1; **ADR-0127**, which also records the ONE human-authorized 5→6 chaining exception at phase 66 and why 0→1, 1→2, 2→3, 3→4 and 4→5 must NEVER be chained) — **do not read the git history as licence to chain.** Parallelism is permitted strictly INSIDE one state (READ-ONLY review dimensions; the main session is the SOLE writer of the state ledger and makes every decisive measurement itself), never ACROSS states, and a state-6 close-out is ONE INDIVISIBLE UNIT, SOLO.

The projected shape is in `SPEC.md` §8: `67.1` = the iteration protocol + the chain-termination rule + `rbac` with `any`-only matchers + fixtures `0072`/`0073` + the raw-TCP `expected_stats` harness extension + the M66-3/M66-4 consumption (fully exercised — **no stubs**, §6.3); `67.2` = the connection-level matcher arms (`CidrRange`, `direct_remote_ip`/`remote_ip`/`source_ip`, `destination_port`/`destination_ip`) + the CF-67-4 rejections + the V-1 fallout.

**Re-confirm SPEC §3's PLAN-VERIFY items V-1 … V-9 FRESH against the live tree** (line drift is routine). **V-3 and V-6 were already RESOLVED empirically at state-1** (SPEC R-0.13) and need only re-confirmation. The two that matter most:
- **V-1 (biggest unknown).** `Principal` / `Permission` are **shared** with the HTTP RBAC filter (`crates/envoy-filter/src/rbac.rs`, 1270 lines). Adding L4-only arms to those enums **may be a breaking change** if the HTTP filter matches exhaustively. Decide where the HTTP filter should reject the new L4-only arms (mirroring Envoy's own HTTP-vs-L4 split).
- **V-2 (biggest architectural risk).** `echo::serve` (`echo.rs:20`) and `direct_response::serve` (`direct_response.rs:31`) each **own an accept loop**, while `tcp_proxy`/HCM go through `envoy_listener::ConnectionHandler` (`envoy-listener/src/lib.rs:38`). Inserting a per-connection pre-hook spans two different shapes. **SPEC's recommendation: hoist the accept loop out once**, making `echo`/`direct_response` per-connection handlers — which is also what turns **M66-3** (the `JoinSet` non-reaping shared by both loops) into a single fix rather than two.
- **V-4.** Fixtures `0072`/`0073` use **`any: true` only**. `direct_remote_ip` would see the Docker bridge address (`192.168.65.2` on this host — a documented fragility) and `destination_port` would see a `{{PORT}}` that **differs between the two proxies**. Every IP/port matcher is covered **in-process** instead, bound to `127.0.0.1`.
- **V-5.** The `expected_stats` extension for raw-TCP drivers: reuse `KeepAliveExpectedStat` and the admin-scrape settle machinery, or add a new struct? Fixture `0072`'s Envoy side will need an `admin:` block to expose `/stats`.

**Do NOT add `rbac` to `is_terminal_network_filter`** (`bootstrap.rs:825`) — its **absence** is what makes it non-terminal, and that predicate's doc comment names `rbac` as the intended drop-in. **Do NOT add an `on_data` hook** with no filter to exercise it (§6.3; deferred as CF-67-3). **Do NOT materialise a default `Rules { action: ALLOW }` when `rules` is omitted** — the filter is INERT and must tick **neither** counter (SPEC R-0.13). **Do NOT let the DENY fixture assert bodies only** — empty-vs-empty passes vacuously; the `rbac.denied == 1` stats assertion is what makes it a witness (SPEC R-0.9).

**THE key §6.2 risks to nail at the PLAN-write (de-risk the byte-exact JSON differential):**
- **JSON key ordering (THE load-bearing fact):** configure `json_format` keys in a deliberately NON-alphabetical order and observe whether Envoy preserves config insertion order (projected → a `Vec<(String,String)>` model) or sorts alphabetically (would force a sort). Decides the config representation; a `BTreeMap` would silently re-sort and break byte-exactness.
- **string-vs-typed value emission:** does plain `json_format` quote EVERY value incl. numeric operators (`%RESPONSE_CODE%` → `"200"`, projected) or type-infer (which would blur the `typed_json_format` deferral and could fire the split)?
- the separators (compact `{"k":"v","k2":"v2"}` — projected), the per-object trailing `\n` (projected), the absent-value rendering inside a JSON value (the `-` string — projected, vs `null`/empty/omitted), and the JSON string-escaping rules (lock the fixture to the unambiguous-ASCII subset).
- the config-validity dispositions (empty `json_format` map, both `{text_format_source, json_format}` arms set at once, malformed value-operator) — boot-fatal on both (ADR-0049); projected NO new `ConfigError` variant (reuse `InvalidAccessLogFormat`).

- **gRPC family** — gRPC bridge, gRPC-Web, gRPC-JSON transcoding, interop conformance.
- **xDS / dynamic config family** — ADS, delta xDS, LDS, CDS, RDS, EDS, SDS, RTDS, reconnection, initial-fetch timeout.
- **Observability family** — gRPC ALS, OTLP access log, OTel/Zipkin/Jaeger/Datadog/XRay tracing, stats sinks, tap filter.
- **Runtime + hot restart family.**
- **WASM host family** — own multi-phase sub-project; ABI, engine binding, proxy-wasm conformance.
- **Deprecated / edge features** — explicit out-of-scope ADRs unless later re-opened.

The load-bearing ones: **`[rbac]` alone is REJECTED by upstream** (`non-terminal filter ... is the last filter in a network filter chain`) — the **bilateral dual** of phase 66's terminal rule, structurally undiscoverable then; **DENY writes zero bytes and closes with a clean EOF, no RST**, deciding once per connection **before any downstream byte is read** (so the protocol needs only `on_new_connection`, not `on_data`); **`rules` omitted ⇒ the filter is INERT and ticks NEITHER counter** (not `default ALLOW, counted`) — a naive default would be a **stat divergence with no body divergence**; and the harness has **`expected_stats` on no raw-TCP driver**, so a DENY fixture asserting bodies alone would **pass vacuously even with RBAC unimplemented** — extending the driver family is therefore a hard requirement, not polish. **CONSUMES CF-66-2** (the chain iteration protocol, on exactly the trigger ADR-0123 named), **M66-3** (the `JoinSet` non-reaping shared verbatim by `echo.rs` and `direct_response.rs` — this phase restructures both accept loops, the joint repair unit the phase-66 review demanded) and **M66-4**. **CLOSES M66-5 on measured evidence with no code change:** an empty `filters: []` chain is **ACCEPTED by upstream** (so envoy-rust is at parity, and the reviewer's intuition was wrong), and `response: {}` is **rejected by both**. **OPENS CF-67-1 … CF-67-4.** **Chosen over `sni_cluster`**, which needs a `tls_inspector` listener filter — a subsystem envoy-rust wholly lacks — for the same CF-66-2 payoff. **THIS commit = `SPEC.md` (new) + `ADR-0128` + ROADMAP row `67` + STATE + STATE_HISTORY.** (`next-prompt.txt` refreshed on disk but **gitignored** at `.gitignore:9`, so NOT in this commit.) Envoy v1.33's tightened `socket_address.address` parse semantics expect either a literal IP (under `STATIC`) or DNS resolution opt-in (under `STRICT_DNS` / `LOGICAL_DNS`):

```
[critical][main] [source/server/server.cc:416] error initializing config '/etc/envoy/envoy.yaml':
malformed IP address: host.docker.internal. Consider setting resolver_name or setting cluster type
to 'STRICT_DNS' or 'LOGICAL_DNS'
```

1. Items carrying forward to phase 05.3 (recommended closure-targets):

- **I1 (Important; CI h2spec tarball lacks integrity verification).** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:43-49` provisions h2spec via `curl -fsSL ... | sudo tar xz -C /usr/local/bin` with no SHA-256, no GPG, no tag-pinning beyond version string. Blast radius is contained (CI runner ephemeral; envoy-rust source checked out before install) but a release-pipeline takeover or DNS hijack could inject arbitrary code. **Fix sketch**: capture published SHA-256 from the GitHub release page, hardcode, verify after download. **Disposition: carry forward to 05.3 (or as a standalone 05.x security-pass).**
- **I2 (Important; `Http2Error` variant overload at the response-emission edge).** `crates/envoy-http2/src/response.rs:60-69` openly admits two misnomers: `send_response()` failures map to `H2StreamAccept` (line 77; "accept" implies inbound), `send_data()` failures map to `H2BodyRead` (line 81; "read" implies inbound). The variant names imply inbound/accept paths but are used for outbound/send paths. Source `h2::Error` retains diagnostic fidelity, but the typed wrapper is misleading on stack traces and log lines. **Fix sketch**: add `H2ResponseSend { source: h2::Error }` + `H2BodyWrite { source: h2::Error }` variants (or rename `H2StreamAccept` → `H2StreamIo` if a single duplex variant is preferred). Public API change but no external consumers yet — additive variants are cheap. **Disposition: carry forward to 05.3, BEFORE the upstream H2 client introduces additional H2 error sites that would amplify the misnaming.**
- **I3 (Important; `MalformedH2HeaderBlock` is a coarse catch-all hiding three distinct failure modes).** `crates/envoy-http2/src/error.rs:40-50` documents the variant as covering structural pseudo-header issues, non-token byte names, and non-UTF-8 byte values; in practice it's also raised for `HeaderName::from_bytes` failure on the response side, `HeaderValue::from_str` failure, and `HttpResponse::builder().body(())` failure (`crates/envoy-http2/src/response.rs:49-57`). When a request-side translation failure hits this variant, an operator looking at logs cannot tell whether it was a non-UTF-8 header-value byte (request-side, defensible 400), an unrepresentable response status, or a stale state-machine bug elsewhere. **Fix sketch**: split into `InvalidHeaderName { name: String }`, `InvalidHeaderValue { name: String }`, `InvalidResponseHead`. Public API impact bounded since callers currently only `match` exhaustively in tests. **Disposition: carry forward to 05.3.**
- **M2 (per-stream `tokio::spawn` task carries no per-test or per-fixture timeout).** `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:78-82` spawns each H2 stream task without a wall-clock budget. Latent in 05.2 because the only `BuildOutcome::Proxy` arm is the 502-stub which returns synchronously. **Fix sketch**: add a per-stream `tokio::time::timeout` budget when 05.3 wires the upstream H2 dispatch (the budget fits naturally there since the upstream call is the long-tail). **Disposition: carry forward to 05.3 or 08.**
- **M8 (502 Bad Gateway stub body literal mentions phase 05.3).** `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:132` emits body `b"upstream H2 not yet wired (sub-phase 05.3)\n"`. SPEC §6 local signpost 21 explicitly accepts "doctrine-line is sufficient." When 05.3 replaces the stub, this literal disappears. **Disposition: trivial 05.3 entry-point check; closes at 05.3.**
- **M10 (`differential::Driver::Http2` variant lacks `extra_headers`).** `tests/differential/src/lib.rs:86-96` carries `method/path/host/expected_status/expected_body/expected_headers` but no `extra_headers: Vec<(String, String)>` field (compare `Http1Probe` at lines 175-191). 05.2's only fixture (0009) does not need it; 05.3 may. The `drive_http2` helper already accepts an `extra_headers` parameter (`tests/differential/src/lib.rs:806`); only the enum variant lacks the field. **Fix sketch**: at 05.3 when fixture 0010 lands, add the field with `#[serde(default)]` and thread it through the dispatch arm. **Disposition: carry forward to 05.3.**
- **M11 (`Http2Error::MissingAuthority` recovery path is RFC-soft).** `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:78-82` (the spawn site) logs the per-stream error via `tracing::error!` and lets the task end without sending any response. RFC 9113 §8.3.1 requires a request without `:authority` (and without a `Host:` header) to either be rejected by the codec layer or generate a 400 from the server. envoy-rust currently produces no response. **Fix sketch**: raise a 400 Bad Request from the stream task on `MissingAuthority` (and other request-translation failures) instead of dropping silently. Maps to envoy-rust's H1 `synth_400` posture. **Disposition: carry forward to 05.3 or 06+.**

Items carrying forward to phase 06+ (recommended closure-targets):

- **I1 (Important; ADR-0028's option-(B) deferral leaves an H1-listener × H2-cluster silent runtime protocol-misnegotiation).** ADR-0028 deliberately defers the H1-listener H2-arm dispatch (the H1 listener cannot dispatch to a cluster whose `upstream_protocol = Http2` because adding `envoy-http2` as a dep on `envoy-http1` would cycle). The deferral is correct doctrine — but the deferred path is not gated at parse time, so a configuration with `codec_type: AUTO` (or `HTTP1`) on the listener and a cluster with `typed_extension_protocol_options.HttpProtocolOptions.http2_protocol_options` set does NOT fail validation; it silently runs H1-on-the-wire to an H2-only upstream backend, which would either get rejected by the backend or produce a confusing 502. **Fix sketch**: add `ConfigError::Http2ClusterFromHttp1Listener { listener: String, cluster: String }` parse-time gate at the envoy-config validator (cross-validate listener `codec_type` against each cluster's `upstream_protocol` per route), or add a runtime defense at the H1 router-arm `BuildOutcome::Proxy` site that catches the misconfiguration with an explicit log + 502. **Disposition: carry forward to phase 06+.** Phase 06's brainstorm should consider folding I1 as a Task-1 preamble (the parse-time gate is a small validator extension).
- **I2 (Important; typed-error chain dissolved at the dispatch site).** `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs`'s symmetric H1-or-H2 router-arm dispatch (Task 7, `52b3635`) collapses `Http2Error` variants to a 502 string at the wire via `to_string()`-shaping. The reviewer's specific finding: when the upstream H2 client returns `Http2Error::UpstreamConnect` (TCP refused) vs `H2ClientHandshake` (h2 handshake failed) vs `H2RecvBody` (body drain mid-stream), the on-the-wire response is identical (`502 Bad Gateway` with body `upstream connect error`-ish text); operators looking at logs see the typed variant in `tracing::error!`, but the response gives no signal. **Fix sketch**: structured `x-envoy-upstream-rq-failure-reason` response header reflecting the typed variant (envoy parity), or per-variant body text. Public API change but additive. **Disposition: carry forward to phase 06+.**
- **05.2 REVIEW I1+I2+I3** (CI tarball SHA-256 / Http2Error write-path variant rename / MalformedH2HeaderBlock overload split): **NOT CLOSED in 05.3.** Per 05.3 PROGRESS preamble paragraph 3, the SPEC §3 D1 explicitly preserved the 05.2 codec-side variants unchanged ("the 05.2 codec-side variants ... stay unchanged"). All three carryforwards continue to phase 06+.
- **05.2 REVIEW M11** (RFC-soft `MissingAuthority` recovery path): **NOT CLOSED in 05.3.** The per-stream task error handling at `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs` was unedited at the upstream-direction work; M11 continues to carry forward awareness-only.

Items carrying forward to 06.2 / 06.3 (recommended closure-targets):

- **I1 (Important; admin handler lacks idle read timeout — slow-loris-style resource hold).** `crates/envoy-admin/src/handler.rs:44-67` `read_request` loops on `stream.read(...).await` until either `MAX_REQUEST_HEAD = 8 KiB` is exceeded, `find_crlf_crlf` succeeds, or the peer closes (n == 0). A connected-but-silent client holds the connection open indefinitely, blocked on the kernel's read; the connection task in `JoinSet` stays parked. Compare the data-plane HCM at `crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:24` which sets `IDLE_READ_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5)` and wraps each per-request read in `tokio::time::timeout(IDLE_READ_TIMEOUT, ...)`. The shutdown path's `DRAIN_BUDGET = 5s` bounds the worst-case shutdown delay, but the steady-state hold is unbounded. **Fix sketch**: wrap the `stream.read(...)` call in `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), ...)` and map the `Elapsed` to a 408 Request Timeout (or just close — both proxies' admin scrape clients should retry on close). Mechanical, scoped to one site, ~10 LoC. **Disposition: carry forward to 06.2 or 06.3.** Whichever sub-phase first touches the admin handler is the natural close site. The 06.2 SPEC has admin-side access logging OUT OF SCOPE per cross-sub-phase rule 6, so 06.2 likely does not touch the admin handler by default — but the 06.2 PLAN-writer may opportunistically close I1 with a small no-scope-creep PR if the LoC budget allows. The 06.3 SPEC's comprehensive stats-wiring scope may touch the admin handler indirectly; if so, I1 closes at the same task.

Items carrying forward to phase 08 (recommended closure-targets):

- **I2 (Important; `serialize_response` unconditionally injects 5 standard headers — duplicate-header hazard).** `crates/envoy-admin/src/handler.rs:96-120` walks `resp.headers` writing them out, then *unconditionally* writes `cache-control: no-cache, max-age=0`, `x-content-type-options: nosniff`, `server: envoy-rust`, `date: <RFC 7231>`, `connection: close`. The current 06.1 endpoints (`render_ready`, `render_stats`, `render_stats_prometheus`, `render_404`, `render_405`) only set `content-type` / `content-length` / `allow` (where applicable) — so today the assumption holds and there are no duplicates. But the abstraction is fragile: a future endpoint that sets `cache-control: max-age=300` (e.g., a `/server_info` endpoint that's safe to cache briefly) would emit *both* headers on the wire. **Fix sketch**: in `serialize_response`, dedupe by case-insensitive header name before writing the standard headers — write only the ones not already present in `resp.headers`. ~10 LoC. **The current behavior is not a bug** for the 06.1 endpoint set; it's a latent maintenance hazard that will surface in phase 08 when the full admin endpoint surface (config_dump, clusters, listeners, runtime, server_info, /quitquitquit) lands. **Disposition: carry forward to phase 08.**
- **M1 (admin handler `resp.reason.unwrap_or("OK")` wrong for non-200 statuses).** `handler.rs:98` uses `unwrap_or("OK")` — if a future endpoint constructs a `Response { status: 404, reason: None, ... }`, the wire output is `HTTP/1.1 404 OK\r\n` which is wrong. All current 06.1 endpoints set `reason: Some(...)`, so the path is unreachable today. **Fix sketch**: map `unwrap_or` to the standard reason for the status code, or change `Response.reason` to non-Optional `String` and require renderer to populate. **Disposition: carry forward to phase 08 alongside I2** — same site (`serialize_response`); whichever phase first lands a `reason: None` arm. May fold into 06.2/06.3 if the access-log emitter happens to need a reason-from-status-code helper.
- **M4 (`DRAIN_BUDGET` constant duplicated between `envoy-admin` and `envoy-listener`).** `crates/envoy-admin/src/handler.rs:22` defines `DRAIN_BUDGET: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5)` and `crates/envoy-listener/src/lib.rs:135` defines the identical const inline. Two sources of truth for the same drain budget. Today the values agree; future drift would be silent. **Fix sketch**: hoist to `envoy-listener` and re-export, or add a `// keep in lockstep` comment at one or both sites. **Disposition: carry forward to phase 08** (graceful-drain consolidation).

- **R-1** — The dot-tree contract (`http.<stat_prefix>.downstream_rq_total = value-exact`; `cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_total = name-required, value-may-differ`; `listener.<name>.downstream_cx_total = value-exact`) is in BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md `Stat-name mapping` rows 1-3 as authoritative. 06.3's comprehensive stats wiring extends — each new stat lands a row with the `value-exact` or `name-required, value-may-differ` disposition + rationale. **Do NOT silently widen the allow-list in fixture 0011's expectations.yaml** when new counters are wired; widen the table first, allow-list second.
- **R-2** — The Prometheus exposition emitter's name-vs-label shape divergence (2 envoy-rust-only allow-list entries paired with their bare-name upstream-Envoy counterparts) is documented in BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md "06.1 Prometheus exposition shape divergence" subsection. When a later phase introduces a `StatsTagExtractor`-equivalent that projects dynamic name segments back into Prometheus labels, the 2 envoy-rust-only entries and their paired upstream-Envoy counterparts on the envoy-only side **must drop together as a single commit**. Half-dropping introduces a real divergence.
- **R-3** — `Driver::AdminScrape` and `BodyRule::PrometheusExposition` are reusable. 06.3 extends fixture 0011's `expectations.yaml` to assert the comprehensive stat set; the harness shape needs no change.
- **R-4** — The `connection: close` discipline on the admin response is a phase-08 generalization point. 06.1's admin handler closes the connection after each response (no keep-alive). Phase 08 may want HTTP/1.1 keep-alive for repeated scrapes from a Prometheus poller.
- **R-5** — The I2 `serialize_response` 5-header dedupe and the I1 idle-read-timeout should land before phase 08 expands the admin endpoint surface. 06.2 or 06.3 SPEC §6 should signpost both. Mechanical, ~20 LoC total.
- **R-6** — `Admin.access_log_path` is parsed-and-ignored at 06.1; admin-side access logging is OUT OF SCOPE in 06.2 too. The field stays parse-and-ignored indefinitely from 06.1; if 06.3 or a later phase wires admin-side access logging, the field already exists in the schema and `AdminConfig` already carries it through — no migration needed.
- **R-7** — The HCM stat-prefix-namespacing pattern (`format!("http.{stat_prefix}.<name>", ...)`) is the convention. 06.3 extends with `..._2xx`, `..._3xx`, `..._4xx`, `..._5xx`, and (per Rule 4) `..._access_logs_total`. Use the same `format!` pattern; register at `HCMStats::register` time; expose via `HCMStats` field accessors. The `register` method is idempotent for same-kind so re-registration of the same stat under the same `stat_prefix` is safe.
- **R-8** — The `Counter::add(n)` API exists but is unused by 06.1's three counters. When 06.3 wires bulk-increment paths (e.g., `bytes_received`/`bytes_sent` counters that increment per-N-bytes rather than per-event), `add(n)` is the right primitive; `inc()` would be wrong. The API is in place; usage starts in 06.3 if the bytes-side counters land then.
- **R-9** — Pre-state-4 fmt discipline. The 06.1 Task 14 fmt-drift catch (13 files of accumulated drift across Tasks 2-13) is the precedent: per-task PROGRESS sections logged "clippy clean" but not "fmt clean," and the drift accumulated quietly. 06.2 / 06.3 / future phases should consider running `cargo fmt --all -- --check` at every PROGRESS-task close, not just at state-4. Or land a pre-commit hook (out of scope for in-phase work; signposts for a future infra-only phase if anyone scopes it).

Per `tests/differential/src/lib.rs::assert_body_rule`, `BodyRule::ByteExact` only enforces byte-equality between upstream Envoy and envoy-rust — it does NOT assert either body actually equals `"ok\n"`. The 04.1 / 04.3 / 05.2 / 05.3 fixtures all use the same shape, so this is pre-existing — but the access-log fixture's `BYTES_SENT` token IS asserted as `exact: "3"` which catches that regression via the token rule. **Fix sketch**: introduce `BodyRule::ByteExactValue { value: String }` (mirrors `Http1BodyRule::ByteExact { body: String }` that already exists for the legacy 04.x driver). **Disposition: carry forward indefinitely** — phase-wide pre-existing pattern, not 06.2-specific.
- **M4 (Minor; `/tmp/0012-envoy-mount/` is a process-shared host path; parallel test jobs could collide).** `tests/differential/src/lib.rs:1388-1431` extracts the parent dir from the fixture's `expected_access_log_paths` and creates+chmods it host-side under `/tmp/0012-envoy-mount`. Today the testcontainers harness implicitly serializes Docker-gated tests (each fixture acquires the container's exposed port and tears down at drop), so the collision is mostly hypothetical — but the path being hardcoded means a future parallelism push (e.g., `cargo nextest`'s test sharding) would surface this. **Fix sketch**: prefix the access-log directory with a process-PID or per-fixture tempdir (`/tmp/0012-envoy-mount-{pid}/`), template-substitute into the YAML at fixture-render time. ~15 LoC. **Disposition: carry forward indefinitely** — activates only under future parallelism push (likely a CI-infra phase post-08).

Acceptable for a unit test today but adds CI runtime + potential flakiness on a loaded runner. **Fix sketch**: use `h2::server::SendResponse::stream_id()` / a `Notify` shared between the test and the server task to deterministically signal emission completion. ~30 LoC. **Disposition: carry forward indefinitely** — pattern-equivalent to the 06.1 backstop's `thread::sleep(100ms)` posture (M5 from 06.1 REVIEW chain) and inherits the standing 02.2 REVIEW M1 chain.

Pass-through unchanged for explicit Content-Length AND for non-empty bodies; suppression triggers only when the body is `None` or empty `&[]`. - **ADR-0028** (resolution of the `envoy-http1` ↔ `envoy-http2` cycle introduced by 05.3 SPEC §3 D4 router dispatch) — landed at 05.3 Task 6 commit `366af8b`. **Documented D-3.5 in-execution deviation from 05.3 SPEC §7's "no new ADRs projected" projection.** The cycle was discovered when the controller attempted to add `envoy-http2` as a `[dependencies]` entry on `crates/envoy-http1/Cargo.toml` to wire the H1 router-arm dispatch — `envoy-http2` already depends on `envoy-http1` for the listener-side `HCMConfig` type alias landed in 05.2, so adding the reverse edge would create a Cargo cycle. The ADR adopts option (B) — deferral: the H1 router-arm at `crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs`'s `BuildOutcome::Proxy` does not dispatch to H2 clusters in 05.3; the cluster's `upstream_protocol` field is queried but the H1 path returns a 502 with a doctrine-line body when the cluster is `Http2`-flagged. The H2 router-arm dispatch lives at `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs` and dispatches symmetrically to either H1 or H2 clusters via the new `envoy-http2::Client`. Future-extension trigger: option (A) — extract a third crate `envoy-http-router` carrying the protocol-agnostic router-walk + `BuildOutcome` + dispatch — is the natural close site if a future phase needs cross-protocol cluster sharing on the H1 listener. **Bounds future extension explicitly**: "Whichever later phase first needs the H1-listener × H2-cluster path lands the `envoy-http-router` extraction; this ADR's option-(B) deferral is then superseded by reference."

The plumbing exists end-to-end except the last two hops. **Not a correctness bug** — the `envoy-config` validator carries the real entry index in `UnsupportedHeaderMutationAppendAction`; `map_entry`'s construction is defense-in-depth that only fires if a caller bypasses the validator. **Fix sketch (preferred):** drop the dead `_position` parameter from `build` (option b — consistent with the 07.1 REVIEW I1 "delete dead plumbing" posture). **Disposition: close opportunistically** — fold into whichever future HTTP-filter-family phase next adds a non-HeaderMutation `HttpFilterInstance` variant (which re-opens `instance.rs::build`). No hard-gated owner.
- **M2 (Minor; `apply_mutations` Overwrite is O(n²) in the unlikely many-entries case).** Each `RuntimeAppendAction::Overwrite` runs a full `headers.retain(...)` with a per-element `to_ascii_lowercase()` allocation. For 07.2's 2-4-entry fixtures this is correct and trivially cheap. 07.2 SPEC §6 signpost 3 explicitly defers the optimization per YAGNI. **Fix sketch (if ever needed):** `eq_ignore_ascii_case` without allocating, or a removal set built once per call, alongside the `Arc<Vec<...>>` refactor. **Disposition: carry forward indefinitely** — acknowledged-and-accepted YAGNI; no named owner; activates only if a future deployment surfaces large mutation lists.
- **M3 (Minor; fixture 0013's `expected_body` byte-exact assertion coupled to upstream Envoy's request-header injection set).** `tests/fixtures/0013-http-filter-header-mutation/expectations.yaml` hardcodes the exact echoed header set; this relies on `envoy.yaml`'s `request_headers_to_remove` block enumerating every header Envoy v1.33 injects (the same posture as fixture 0008). Correct today (CI run `25887571566` green) but a future Envoy version-pin bump that adds a new default request header would silently break the body-exact assertion. The coupling is documented in the fixture `README.md` but not at the assertion site. **Fix sketch:** add a cross-reference comment in `expectations.yaml`. **Disposition: close opportunistically** — natural forced-close site is the future `ENVOY_TARGET.md` version-bump phase (its own phase per D-3.7) that re-baselines the differential suite.

Standing inventory carryforwards inherited but not closed in 07.2 (carry forward unchanged):

- **06.3 REVIEW I1** (verification-discipline gap — workspace-tests-clean does not include Docker-gated bilateral fixture runs) — **structurally closed at 07.1**; the 07.2 arc continued the two-layer attestation pattern (per-task PROGRESS test-bucket attestation + the comprehensive Task 10 state-4 CI anchor). Carries no further.
- **06.3 REVIEW I2** (synthetic 5xx backend + 4-class `pre_requests` deferred from 06.3 Task 11) — the upstream-robustness family is still the natural close site; 07.2 introduces no synthetic-backend infrastructure.
- **06.2 REVIEW M1 / M2 / M4 / M5** — not engaged by 07.2; carry forward unchanged.
- **06.1 REVIEW I2 / M1 / M4** — **carry forward to phase 08** (full admin endpoint surface; graceful-drain consolidation). 07.2 does not touch the admin handler. **06.1 REVIEW M2 / M3 / M5 / M6** — carry forward indefinitely.
- **05.3 REVIEW I2** (typed-error chain dissolution at the H2 dispatch site via `format!("{e}")`) — the 07.2 Task 5 `finalize_h2_stream` cleanup is structurally separate from the upstream-dispatch error path; carries forward.
- **05.2 REVIEW I1 / I2 / I3** (CI h2spec tarball SHA-256 / `Http2Error` write-path variant rename / `MalformedH2HeaderBlock` overload split) — not engaged by 07.2 (no `.github/workflows/ci.yml` edit; no h2 codec-edge surface touched); carry forward unchanged.

- **M3 (Minor; `command_line_options: BTreeMap<String, serde_yaml::Value>` cloned per-request inside `/server_info` rendering).** `crates/envoy-admin/src/handler.rs` clones the `BTreeMap` from `&self` into the borrowed `ServerInfoBody<'a>` on every `/server_info` GET. At 08.1's scope the map has a single entry (`config_path`) so the clone cost is negligible — the construction-site comment explicitly notes "small in 08.1 — single `config_path` entry". **Why it matters:** purely forward-looking — if a later phase widens the CLI surface (more flags, more options, runtime-RTDS-fed entries) the per-request clone scales linearly with the map size. **Fix sketch (if ever needed):** wrap the map in `Arc<BTreeMap<...>>` at construction time and clone the `Arc` instead. ~5 LoC; mechanical. **Disposition: carry forward indefinitely** — activates only if a future deployment surfaces a wide CLI option set. Named owner: whichever future phase first widens `envoy-bin`'s CLI surface beyond the current single-flag (`-c <config>`) shape.
- **M4 (Minor; `walk_pointer` produces opaque error on dotted path with an empty segment).** `tests/differential/src/lib.rs:379-394` walks a dotted-segment path like `"node..id"` (double dot) by `dotted_path.split('.')` — the empty segment between the two dots becomes the literal empty string `""`, which `parse::<usize>()` then fails on, then `cur.get("")` fails on the object, and the error message becomes `"key not found: "` (trailing blank). Unreachable in normal use (every dotted-path subtree assertion in fixture 0014's `expectations.yaml` is well-formed). **Fix sketch:** add a one-line guard at the top of `walk_pointer` body: `if dotted_path.split('.').any(|s| s.is_empty()) { anyhow::bail!("dotted path contains empty segment: {dotted_path:?}"); }`. **Disposition: close opportunistically at 08.2 D16 or whichever later phase first extends `walk_pointer` / `JsonShape`.** ~3-line guard. Named owner: 08.2 or later harness-touch phase.

Items carrying forward (the 8 Minor M1-M8 + 3 test/audit-trail T1-T3 findings — all awareness-only / close-opportunistically; **none has a hard-gated owner phase; none gated the 08.2 state-6 close-out**):

- **M1 (Minor; `let drain = async { … };` local shadows `drain: Arc<DrainState>` parameter in `Listener::serve`).** `crates/envoy-listener/src/lib.rs:323` declares a local `drain` future for the post-loop drain-wait block, shadowing the `drain: Arc<DrainState>` parameter at line 241. **Why it matters:** D-3.4 stranger-readability — a future maintainer adding code between the select and the post-loop block would see `drain` resolve unexpectedly. **Fix sketch:** rename the local to `drain_join` or `drain_fut` (~1-line edit). **Disposition: close opportunistically** at the next phase that touches `Listener::serve`. Named owner: future hardening or filter-family phase that extends the select. Non-blocking.
- **M2 (Minor; `Err(0)` sentinel in `drain()`'s second-CAS-skip branch collides semantically with `DrainStage::Live as u8` discriminant).** `crates/envoy-listener/src/drain.rs:204` reads `Err(0) // Sentinel — we already succeeded via from_live.`. The `0` value happens to be the `DrainStage::Live` discriminant; functionally fine because only `.is_ok()` is checked at line 206, but a reader could mis-read the encoding. **Fix sketch:** either (a) use `Err(u8::MAX)` as a sentinel that cannot collide + extend the comment, OR (b) refactor to a single boolean expression collapsing the conditional (~2-5 LoC). **Disposition: close opportunistically** at the next phase that touches `drain.rs`. Named owner: future drain-time-config phase or feature-family extension. Non-blocking.
- **M3 (Minor; BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md "Admin-action effect equivalence" rows for `/healthcheck/fail` + `/healthcheck/ok` claim "100ms" wire-flip budget unenforced).** `docs/envoy-rust/BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md:163-164` carries `"Both proxies MUST flip /ready to 503 within 100ms"`. The 100ms budget is doctrinal — `fail_healthcheck()` / `ok_healthcheck()` are synchronous `compare_exchange` + gauge updates + nothing else (sub-microsecond on a non-loaded host), but no test or fixture measures the latency or enforces the bound. **Fix sketch:** either (a) downgrade the row prose to `"synchronously observable after the POST response completes"` (~2 LoC contract edit), OR (b) add a `MaxLatencyMs` assertion type to the harness + a fixture or test that bounds the flip latency (sizable; defer indefinitely). Recommendation: option (a). **Disposition: close opportunistically** at the next phase that touches BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT's "Admin-action effect equivalence" subsection. Named owner: future healthcheck-filter phase or operations-hardening phase. Non-blocking; doc-tightening only.
- **M4 (Minor; `empty_200_ok()` helper omits `content-type` entirely).** `crates/envoy-admin/src/endpoint.rs:570-577` constructs `Response { status: 200, reason: Some("OK"), headers: [("content-length", "0")], body: Bytes::new() }` — no `content-type` header. RFC 7231 §3.1.1.5 permits this for empty bodies; upstream Envoy v1.33's `/drain_listeners` empirically carries `content-type: text/plain`. Fixture 0015 does NOT assert on `/drain_listeners`'s `content-type` (the scrape is `/server_info`). **Fix sketch:** add `("content-type", "text/plain")` to the headers vec at `endpoint.rs:572` (~1 LoC). **Disposition: close opportunistically** at whichever future phase first adds a POST-endpoint response-header assertion fixture. Named owner: future POST-endpoint header-assertion phase. Non-blocking; upstream-parity polish only.
- **M5 (Minor; `drain_signal()` always heap-allocates via `Box::pin`).** `crates/envoy-listener/src/drain.rs:246, 248` returns `Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = ()> + Send + '_>>` — the dynamic-dispatch return shape is forced by the two-arm return type asymmetry (`std::future::ready(())` vs `Notified<'_>`). The `Box::pin` allocates on every `drain_signal()` call (once per listener-accept-loop iteration). Under MVP-scale fixture load the cost is trivial; under high QPS this would become a per-connection allocation. **Fix sketch:** convert to `pub async fn drain_signal(&self)` + an internal `enum DrainSignalFuture<'a> { Ready, Pending(Notified<'a>) }` implementing `Future` (~20-30 LoC; mechanical). **Disposition: carry forward indefinitely** — activates only if a future high-throughput deployment surfaces allocator pressure on the accept loop's drain-signal path. Named owner: whichever future phase first benchmarks the accept loop's allocator footprint. Non-blocking; forward-looking performance note only.
- **M6 (Minor; `admin_handler_new_6arg_tests::admin_handler_new_accepts_six_args_and_constructs` test name + module name now describe a 7-arg shape post-Task-4 widening).** `crates/envoy-admin/src/handler.rs:953-985` retains the 06.1-era test name + module name despite Task 4's 7-arg widening. **Why it matters:** D-3.4 stranger-readability — a future maintainer searching for "6arg" tests would find this misnamed surface. **Fix sketch:** rename module to `admin_handler_new_constructor_tests` + test to `admin_handler_new_accepts_arg_count_and_constructs` + trim the 70-line block comment to a 3-line note pointing at the sibling Task-4 coverage (~75-line edit). **Disposition: close opportunistically** at the next phase that touches `crates/envoy-admin/src/handler.rs::tests`. Named owner: future admin-endpoint extension or test-organization cleanup pass. Non-blocking.
- **M7 (Minor; `drain_signal()` doc-comment "tens of microseconds" claim is unmeasured).** `crates/envoy-admin/src/endpoint.rs:531-535` (and a similar phrasing in `drain.rs` doc-comments) carries the claim that `notify_waiters → listener-serve-drop-listener` latency is "tens of microseconds" on Linux/macOS loopback. Structurally plausible but no benchmark or measurement is cited. **Fix sketch:** either (a) drop the quantification (`"sub-millisecond on a non-loaded host"`) OR (b) back with a `tokio::time::Instant` measurement in `serve_returns_when_drain_signal_fires`. Recommendation: option (a) (~1-line edit). **Disposition: close opportunistically** at the next phase that touches `endpoint.rs::render_drain_listeners`. Named owner: future admin-action-surface extension phase. Non-blocking; doc-tightening only.
- **M8 (Minor; `AdminEndpoint::render`'s `Ready` arm at `endpoint.rs:163-168` is `unreachable!()`).** The registry-only `render` path 08.1 D6 introduced cannot serve handler-scoped endpoints; the `Ready` arm reads `unreachable!("Ready requires handler-scoped DrainState; dispatch via AdminEndpoint::render_with")`. The `render_with` dispatch at `endpoint.rs:194-200` correctly routes `Ready` through `render_ready_with(handler)`, so the `render` arm is genuinely unreachable in production. A future maintainer adding a registry-only dispatch site for `Ready` would hit a runtime panic rather than getting a compile error. The same concern applies to `ConfigDump` / `ServerInfo` / `Clusters` / `Listeners` arms (all handler-scoped + `unreachable!()` in `render`). **Fix sketch:** split `AdminEndpoint` into `enum AdminEndpoint { Registry(RegistryEndpoint), Handler(HandlerEndpoint) }` with separate render fns (~150 LoC; sizable typestate refactor). **Disposition: carry forward indefinitely** — activates only if a future feature requires registry-only dispatch of a currently-handler-scoped endpoint. Named owner: whichever future phase first introduces a synthetic-state admin endpoint requiring registry-only dispatch. Non-blocking; type-safety refactor opportunity only.
