### Phase-09 state-1 brainstorm

Brainstorm session decisions (THIS commit), all per the user's standing preferences `feedback_pick_recommendation` ("always pick the recommended option; do not ask") and `feedback_execution_style` ("default to subagent-driven-development; skip the two-option fork"). This is the **first post-MVP-trunk feature-family brainstorm session** per `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §9 — the cadence-setter for all subsequent feature-family arcs. Mirrors the parent-NN state-1 brainstorm cadence (closest shape precedent: parent-08 state-1 brainstorm at commit `0202e38`):

- **Family pick: HTTP filters family.** Picked directly per `feedback_pick_recommendation`. Alternatives scored across 5 dimensions (carryforward closure value / foundation pressure / architectural risk / contract-surface maturity / first-phase scope tractability):

  - **HTTP filters family (WINNER)** — closes 07.2 REVIEW M1 at named site; zero foundation pressure (hand-roll all filters per D-3.2); low architectural risk (extends 07.x framework); mature contract (Header allow-list + Stat-name mapping populated through MVP trunk); tractable scope (~900-1100 LoC for first filter).
  - Network filters family — no carryforward closure; introduces new network-layer filter chain framework (higher risk); first concrete network filter is larger than first HTTP filter.
  - Load balancing family — strong alternative; low risk (extends 02.x cluster LB seam); ~600-800 LoC for one LB algo (least_request); rejected at the family-pick because HTTP-filter-family's carryforward closure value (07.2 M1) is the load-bearing tiebreaker.
  - Upstream robustness family — closes 06.3 REVIEW I2 (synthetic 5xx backend) BUT scope is multiple subsystems (health checks / outlier detection / circuit breakers / retries / hedging / conn pooling); first phase tightly scoped to active HTTP health checks alone is ~1200-1400 LoC.
  - HTTP/3 + QUIC family — heavy foundation pressure (first `quinn` pull; h3spec gate); high architectural risk (new UDP listener path); LARGE multi-phase scope; rejected — too sprawling for the first post-MVP phase.
  - gRPC family — `tonic` already permitted but no concrete gRPC backend engaged yet; possible but unmotivated for the first.
  - xDS / dynamic config family — HIGHEST architectural risk (entire new state machine); largest by scope per `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §9; rejected for first.
  - Observability family — strong alternative; extends 06.x naturally; rejected at the family-pick for the same tiebreaker as Load balancing.
  - Runtime + hot restart family — hot restart HEAVY; rejected — too sprawling for first.
  - WASM host family — own multi-phase sub-project per §9; rejected — too sprawling for first.
  - Deprecated / edge features — not a substantive feature family (meta-bookkeeping only).

  Top-3 viable: HTTP filters > Load balancing > Observability. HTTP filters wins on carryforward closure value + smallest tractable first-phase scope + most mature contract surface. The 09 SPEC §1 + §3 record the picked family + first-filter scope.

- **First filter pick: `envoy.filters.http.local_ratelimit`.** Picked directly per `feedback_pick_recommendation`. Per the §9 HTTP-filter sub-feature enumeration (header_mutation DONE at 07.2), considered 14 candidate filters along (config shape / foundations needed / framework extension needed):

  - **local_rate_limit (WINNER)** — filter-chain config; no per-route required; zero foundations (hand-roll token bucket via std-lib atomic + Mutex); zero framework extension (Decision::StopAndSend exists from 07.1).
  - cors — per-route CorsPolicy via typed_per_filter_config is primary; rejected — needs new per-route framework primitive.
  - fault — needs `rand` for percentage sampling (deterministic-only scope loses upstream parity); rejected — random sampling forces foundations grant.
  - buffer — tiny config (max_request_bytes); rejected — needs new body-buffering framework extension (larger than the filter itself).
  - csrf — per-route primary; same per-route extension as cors; rejected.
  - compression — needs `flate2`/`brotli`/`zstd` foundations grant + new pluggable-compressor primitive; rejected.
  - rbac — medium principal-matcher primitive; rejected (medium scope).
  - adaptive concurrency — sophisticated gradient-based algorithm; rejected (algorithm-heavy).
  - jwt_authn — needs `jsonwebtoken` foundations grant + JOSE primitive; rejected.
  - ext_authz / ext_proc — needs gRPC client + cross-process call protocol; rejected (depends on gRPC family).
  - oauth2 — needs HTTPS client + auth-state framework; rejected.
  - admission control — probabilistic + stats-heavy (P50/P99); rejected.
  - bandwidth limit — per-stream timing; rejected.
  - global rate limit — needs gRPC client + RLS protocol; rejected (depends on gRPC family).
  - lua / wasm — scripting hosts; own multi-phase sub-projects per §9; rejected.

  Top-3 viable: local_rate_limit > fault > buffer. **local_rate_limit wins** on: pure filter-chain config (no per-route extension); validates `Decision::StopAndSend(FilterResponse)` path with non-trivial 429 + `x-envoy-ratelimited` response shape (fixture 0013 / header_mutation only exercised `Decision::Continue`); 4-counter stat surface matching upstream Envoy v1.33 parity exactly; deterministic semantics (no `rand` foundations grant); no new top-level Cargo deps; ~900-1100 LoC including tests + fixture. The 09 SPEC §3 D3 records the hand-rolled token-bucket primitive design; SPEC §6.3 makes the concurrency torture test (`token_bucket_atomic_compare_exchange_under_concurrency`) REQUIRED per the 08.2 Task 1 fixup `fddabd2` TOCTOU-lesson precedent.

- **Phase id + slug pick:** **`09`** / **`09-http-filter-local-rate-limit`**. The id `09` is next sequential after `08.2` per the project's numbering convention (first post-MVP-trunk phase starts at `09` regardless of family). The slug mirrors `07.2-header-mutation-filter`'s hyphenation pattern — readable English (`http-filter-local-rate-limit`) over upstream-name verbatim (`http-filter-local-ratelimit`). The filter's typed_config `name:` field uses upstream's exact `envoy.filters.http.local_ratelimit` (no underscore between "rate" and "limit"); the slug + readable name + upstream config name are deliberately distinct surfaces per the 07.2 precedent.

- **depends-on pick:** **`07`** (the parent filter-chain framework). Per `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §9 depends-on doctrine (HTTP-filter-family extensions name `07`). The 15-Docker-gated-fixture regression baseline established at parent-08 close carries forward per `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §7.5 (b) (implicit, not in depends-on field).

Both dimensions comfortably under the §6.1 ~25-task / ~1500-LoC gate. - **ADR projection at state-1: NONE.** Recommended posture per SPEC §7 + §5.2 + §5.3 — no foundations grants required at any phase-09 lifecycle state; hand-roll token bucket per D-3.2's "Must be written from scratch" doctrine for filter engines. DECISIONS.md ledger head stays at **ADR-0032** through this state-1 commit. Two conditional ADR slots stay reserved-available:

  - **Conditional ADR-0033 — per-route filter config deferral.** Documents the project-wide deferral pattern for the HTTP-filter-family arc (filter-chain config only at the 09 baseline; per-route `typed_per_filter_config` defers to the future filter that first needs it; CORS is the natural close site). **Mid-execution discovery + ADR-0033 corrective sequence (4 commits over Tasks 5-7).**

Task 5 dispatch (the Docker-gated differential fixture authoring step) surfaced 3 SPEC §2.2 + Task 3 lock-in #13 discrepancies against upstream Envoy v1.33's actual `envoy.filters.http.local_ratelimit` wire shape per empirical Docker observation:

1. **Upstream does NOT emit `x-envoy-ratelimited` from local_ratelimit** (that header belongs to the global ratelimit filter + router-side response-flag handling per upstream v1.33 source).
2. **Upstream's 429 body is the source-hardcoded `"local_rate_limited"` (18 bytes)**, not empty (the upstream proto has no configurable `response_body` field).
3. **envoy-rust's H1 HCM filter-StopAndSend writer-path skips standard-header decoration** — the synth-from-build paths (`synth_status`, `synth_direct_response`) populate the 5 standard HTTP/1.1 response headers inline; the filter-synth path (`RequestPath::SynthFromDecode` arm + encode-side `Decision::StopAndSend` arm) takes `filter_resp.headers` verbatim. A latent 07.x framework defect that 07.2 HeaderMutation never exposed (HeaderMutation's `decode_headers` returns `Decision::Continue` unconditionally — the filter only mutates header lists, never short-circuits); phase 09's LocalRateLimit is the first production filter to surface the gap.

Per `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` D-3.3 ("differential correctness beats internal fidelity") + D-3.5 ("Decisions are written, not remembered"), **ADR-0033** ratified the 4-commit corrective sequence:

- **Commit A (`e9a6cb4`)** — ADR-0033 + SPEC §2.2 revision + PROGRESS mid-execution preamble subsection (docs-only). Voids PLAN lock-ins #13 (429 synth response shape with `x-envoy-ratelimited` + empty body), #30 (`x-envoy-ratelimited` BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT row at Task 5), partial #33 (in-process backstop direct presence assertion). **DECISIONS.md ledger advances `ADR-0032 → ADR-0033`** at this commit.

- **Commit B (`1c1de0f`)** — Task 3 runtime fixup. `LocalRateLimitFilter::decode_headers` drops the `("x-envoy-ratelimited", "true")` header injection from the synth `FilterResponse`; changes `body: Bytes::new()` → `body: Bytes::from_static(b"local_rate_limited")` (18 bytes; static literal; zero-allocation). 2 unit tests updated (`decode_headers_rate_limits_after_max_tokens_and_increments_rate_limited_enforced` drops the x-envoy-ratelimited assertion + adds the body + headers-empty asserts; `decode_headers_appends_configured_response_headers` drops the x-envoy-ratelimited assertion + adds the `headers.len() == 1` + body asserts). Operator-configurable `response_headers_to_add` plumbing PRESERVED.

- **Commit C (`ae2cef0`)** — Task 4 H1 HCM fixup. New `decorate_filter_synth_response(resp: &mut Response, close: bool)` helper at `crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs` (immediately before `synth_400`, after `synth_status`); called from both `RequestPath::SynthFromDecode(resp)` arm (decode-side) + `Decision::StopAndSend(replacement)` arm (encode-side filter substitution). The helper conditionally adds 5 standard headers (`server`, `date`, `content-length`, `content-type`, `connection`) if not provided by the filter (case-insensitive name check matching the 06.1 D1 / 08.1 D1 dedupe precedent); `content-length` is ALWAYS set from `body.len()` (overwrites any stale filter-provided value). 2 new unit tests covering the empty-filter-headers happy path + the filter-provides-overlapping-headers edge case (dedupe + overwrite semantic).

- **Commit D (`1384c48`)** — Task 5 re-attempt. Fixture `tests/fixtures/0016-http-filter-local-rate-limit/{envoy.yaml,envoy-rust.yaml,expectations.yaml,README.md}` per the ADR-0033 revised contract (5-probe burst `[200, 200, 200, 429, 429]` + body `"local_rate_limited"` byte_exact on 429 probes + `set_equal_modulo_allow_list` headers). Docker-gated wrapper at `tests/differential/tests/http_filter_local_rate_limit.rs`. Per-side YAML asymmetry per the fixture-0013 precedent: upstream's `envoy.yaml` has an admin block + `filter_enabled`/`filter_enforced: { default_value: { numerator: 100, denominator: HUNDRED } }` (upstream defaults both to 0%; envoy-rust defaults to always-on); envoy-rust.yaml omits both. Both YAMLs use `tokens_per_fill: 3` (upstream rejects 0 per its `TokenBucketValidator`; envoy-rust accepts 0; intersection picked at 3). **NO BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md row** at this commit per PLAN lock-in #30 voiding.

Items carrying forward (the 3 Minor M1-M3 + 2 doc-staleness D1-D2 + 3 test/audit-trail T1-T3 findings — all awareness-only / close-opportunistically; **none has a hard-gated owner phase; none gated the 09 state-6 close-out**):

- **M1 (Minor; `TokenBucketState::try_acquire` CAS-shape race on the refill path).** `crates/envoy-filter/src/local_rate_limit.rs:215-287` — the CAS at line 263 reads `compare_exchange(current, next, ...)` where `current = self.tokens.load(...)` (pre-refill value) and `next = available - 1`. When `available = current + 1` (exactly one interval elapsed AND `tokens_per_fill = 1`), `next` collapses to `current`, making the CAS `compare_exchange(current, current)` — which succeeds unconditionally for any concurrent thread observing the same `current`. Two threads observing the same `current` value in this scenario both succeed their CAS, both return `true`, and the single refill token is "consumed" twice. **Why it matters:** real concurrent double-consumption bug on the refill path. **Why it does NOT rise above Minor at phase-09 scope:** the bug is exercised only when `tokens_per_fill > 0` AND a refill interval elapses concurrently with multiple acquires AND the refill credit per interval is exactly enough to bridge `current → current + 1`. Phase 09's actual exercise paths all avoid the contested arm (fixture 0016 uses `tokens_per_fill: 3` + `fill_interval: 60s` with sub-1s burst; backstop uses `tokens_per_fill: 2` + 60s same shape; torture test uses `tokens_per_fill: 0`). The token cap at `max_tokens` provides a hard ceiling on over-crediting — blast radius bounded. **Fix sketch:** either (a) require `available > current` precondition for the CAS, OR (b) replace `compare_exchange(current, next)` with a token-decrement loop that re-loads on every iteration AND atomically combines the refill-credit with the consume. ~15-30 LoC + an additional torture test exercising the contested path. **Disposition: close at whichever future HTTP-filter-family phase first exercises non-zero `tokens_per_fill` within a refill-window-spanning burst**, OR at a dedicated token-bucket hardening pass. Named owner: future HTTP-filter-family phase (likely global-rate-limit or fault-injection). Non-blocking.

- **M2 (Minor; H2 HCM writer-arm sites don't decorate filter-synth responses with standard HTTP/1.1 response headers; ADR-0033 Consequences misrepresents this as "H2 naturally inherits").** `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:373-378` (decode-side `H2RequestPath::SynthFromDecode`) returns the filter's response verbatim; `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:436-443` (encode-side `Decision::StopAndSend(replacement)`) constructs `resp` verbatim; both pass through `build_http_response` at `crates/envoy-http2/src/response.rs:29-50` which does NOT add `server` / `date` / `content-type`. An H2 listener exercising the phase-09 LocalRateLimitFilter would emit 429 responses missing those standard headers (the H2-forbidden `connection` correctly stays stripped; `content-length` is implicit from `send_data(end_of_stream=true)`). ADR-0033 Consequences §iii(c)-end (`docs/envoy-rust/DECISIONS.md` ~line 697) claims "the corresponding H2 HCM path naturally inherits via the shared Http1HCMConfig re-export" — but this conflates config re-export with code reuse (H2 writer-arm sites have their own response-construction code that does NOT call `decorate_filter_synth_response`). Will mislead future filter-family phases (fault / ext_authz / oauth2 / rbac) into assuming H2 is already covered. **Why it does NOT rise above Minor at phase-09 scope:** the phase-09 differential surface is HTTP/1.1 only (fixture 0016's `codec_type: HTTP1`); the in-process backstop is HTTP/1.1 only; the H2 gap is genuinely latent and unexercised by phase-09's actual bilateral assertion. **Fix sketch:** either (a) amend ADR-0033 Consequences + PROGRESS Commit C forward-looking note to explicitly record the H2 analogous gap as known-deferred (~10-15 LoC docs edit; preferred per parent-08 SPEC §6.1 alternative (vi) accept-drift), OR (b) land an H2 `decorate_filter_synth_response` analogue (~50-70 LoC + 2 tests; extends the corrective sequence by 1 commit). **Disposition: prefer (a); close at next HTTP-filter-family phase exercising filters on H2** (fault / ext_authz / oauth2 / rbac per ADR-0033 Consequences §5). Named owner: future HTTP-filter-family phase exercising filters on H2. Non-blocking.

- **M3 (Minor; Task 7 in-process backstop subprocess discipline regresses from 07.2 / 08.2 precedents).** `crates/envoy-bin/tests/http_filter_local_rate_limit.rs:30` declares `use std::process::{Command, Stdio};` (no `kill_on_drop` API); lines 180-188 configure `.stderr(Stdio::piped()).stdout(Stdio::piped())` (both pipes; no concurrent drain reader). 07.2 + 08.2 backstops both use `tokio::process::Command` + `kill_on_drop(true)` + `Stdio::null()` for stdout. **Why it matters:** (a) any panic in `send_request_and_collect`'s 8 `.expect(...)` / `.unwrap()` sites before explicit `child.kill()` leaks the envoy-bin subprocess; (b) un-drained stdout pipe doubles the OS-pipe-buffer-fill deadlock surface; (c) PROGRESS Task 7's "same pattern as 07.2 backstop" claim is factually wrong — the discipline is a regression from BOTH 07.2 AND 08.2. **Why it does NOT rise above Minor at phase-09 scope:** test-helper-only; no production-code impact; the state-4 CI anchor ran the backstop GREEN with no leaks observed (the test passed cleanly so no panic sites fired); the CI environment's process-lifecycle cleanup mitigates the leak risk on green-test runs. **Fix sketch:** 3-line patch: `use tokio::process::{Command, Stdio};` + `.stdout(Stdio::null())` + `.kill_on_drop(true)`. ~3 LoC; trivially mechanical. **Disposition: close at next HTTP-filter-family phase touching `crates/envoy-bin/tests/http_filter_*.rs` backstops**, OR opportunistically. Named owner: future HTTP-filter-family phase touching backstops. Non-blocking; test-helper-only.

- **D1 (Minor; ADR-0033 §iii(c) + PROGRESS Commit A discovery point 3 reference fictional `RequestPath::SynthFromEncode` variant).** The actual `crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs::RequestPath` enum has only `Match`, `SynthFromBuild`, and `SynthFromDecode` variants — no `SynthFromEncode`. The implementation is correct (the encode-side decoration site is the `envoy_filter::Decision::StopAndSend(replacement) =>` arm of the encode-side filter dispatch, NOT a separate `SynthFromEncode` variant of `RequestPath`); only the ADR / PROGRESS prose uses fictional variant names; the line-number references are correct. **Disposition: no action; close opportunistically** at whichever future ADR amends or references ADR-0033 (likely never — ADRs are append-only). Named owner: none. Awareness-only narrative cleanup.

- **D2 (Minor; Cargo.lock 2-line metadata delta at Task 2 refines PLAN lock-in #39 from "empty diff" to "metadata-only diff for path-dep additions").** Task 2's `envoy-stats` path-dep on `envoy-filter` produced a 2-line Cargo.lock delta (path-dep metadata only; no new transitive crates pulled). PROGRESS Task 2 deviation #1 honestly discloses this refinement. The 04.1 REVIEW M5/M9 Cargo.lock cadence ratification ADR carries forward unchanged through phase 09 (the cadence pick stays unforced — workspace-internal path-dep additions are not the trigger for the cadence ADR). **Disposition: no action needed.** The refined reading ("metadata-only diff for path-dep additions") is the projection shape for future phases that add workspace-internal path-deps.

- **T1 (Minor; Task 1 `parse_duration` accepts `+`-prefixed numeric values silently).** `crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:1825-1842` — `u64::from_str` accepts `"+60"`, `"0060s"`, and similar non-canonical shapes that upstream Envoy v1.33's protobuf Duration parser would reject. No test covers `"+60s"` or `"-1s"`. **Why it does NOT rise above Minor:** the validator at `validate_local_rate_limit_config` runs after parse and rejects bogus durations (`fill_interval > 0` check); a `+60s` input would produce a `Duration` of 60s and behave identically to `60s`. The `-1s` case fails parse cleanly (negative prefix not valid for `u64`). No phase-09 differential surface exercises non-canonical shapes. **Fix sketch:** either (a) explicitly reject `+`/`-` prefixes, OR (b) add tests pinning the accept-or-reject behavior. ~5-10 LoC. **Disposition: close opportunistically** at whichever future phase touches `parse_duration`. Named owner: none.

- **T2 (Minor; Task 2 torture test exercises only `tokens_per_fill = 0` no-refill path; does NOT cover the contested refill-CAS path documented in M1).** The REQUIRED 8-task × 10_000-acquire torture test fixes `tokens_per_fill: 0`, routing through the else branch where the contested CAS arm always represents a real state change. The refill-path CAS-shape race documented in M1 is unexercised by the torture test. **Why it does NOT rise above Minor:** the SPEC §6.3 prescription was honored exactly within its prescribed scope (the torture test asserts the strong invariant `observed == expected` + `final_bucket_count == 0`); the refill-path coverage gap is a SPEC-projection gap, not a code defect. **Fix sketch:** additional torture test with `tokens_per_fill > 0` + short `fill_interval` so multiple intervals elapse during the burst — would catch the M1 CAS-shape race. ~50-80 LoC. **Disposition: close alongside M1** at whichever future HTTP-filter-family phase exercises non-zero `tokens_per_fill`. Named owner: same as M1.

- **T3 (Minor; Task 3 `decode_headers_appends_configured_response_headers` test uses brittle exact-length assertion `headers.len() == 1`).** `crates/envoy-filter/src/local_rate_limit.rs:536` — the test asserts exact length 1 (the one configured `x-rate-limit-policy` entry). If a future commit adds an operator-configurable third header to the filter's own emit path, this length assertion brittlely breaks even if the new behavior is correct. **Why it does NOT rise above Minor:** the test is narrowly scoped to the post-ADR-0033 contract (verifying no spurious `x-envoy-ratelimited` injection); the exact-length check is one way to verify the absence of the spurious header. **Fix sketch:** replace `assert_eq!(resp.headers.len(), 1, ...)` with set-membership check + absence-of-`x-envoy-ratelimited` check. ~3-5 LoC. **Disposition: close opportunistically** at the next phase that touches `crates/envoy-filter/src/local_rate_limit.rs::tests`. Named owner: future HTTP-filter-family phase extending LocalRateLimit's response-header surface.

The phase-09 brainstorm's "with phase-09 closed, the carryforward-closure dimension is now more balanced" observation pulls LB family closer to viable; the M2 + M3 closures available in HTTP-filter-family still tip the tiebreaker.
  - **Upstream robustness family** — (a) HIGH carryforward closure (closes 06.3 REVIEW I2 — synthetic 5xx backend; the named-owner family); (b) zero foundation pressure; (c) MEDIUM arch risk (health-check task subsystem is new primitive); (d) MEDIUM contract maturity; (e) MEDIUM-tractability scope (~1200-1400 LoC for tightly-scoped active HTTP health checks; at the upper end of §6.1 gate). Rejected on scope-tractability dimension (the upper-end LoC + new task-spawning-per-endpoint primitive combination is higher risk than HTTP-filter-family RBAC's bounded matcher-tree primitive).
  - **HTTP/3 + QUIC family** — VERY HIGH foundation pressure (`quinn` pull) + VERY HIGH arch risk (new UDP listener path; h3spec gate). Rejected per phase-09 brainstorm's identical rejection reasoning.
  - **gRPC family** — `tonic` already permitted but no concrete gRPC backend engaged yet; possible but unmotivated as second standalone phase. Rejected per phase-09 brainstorm's identical rejection.
  - **xDS / dynamic config family** — HIGHEST architectural risk (entire new state machine). Rejected per phase-09 brainstorm's identical rejection.
  - **Observability family** — second-tier alternative at phase-09; same posture applies at phase-10.
  - **Runtime + hot restart family** — hot restart heavy; rejected.
  - **WASM host family** — multi-phase sub-project per §9; rejected.
  - **Deprecated / edge features** — meta-bookkeeping only; not a substantive feature family.

  Top-3 viable: HTTP filters > Load balancing > Upstream robustness. HTTP filters wins on carryforward-closure value (09 REVIEW M2 + M3 close at named sites) + smallest tractable scope-without-foundations (~1100-1300 LoC; no foundations grant) + most mature contract surface (09's HCM helper + 4-counter pattern directly applies). The phase-10 SPEC §1 + §3 record the picked family + first-filter scope.

- **First filter pick: `envoy.filters.http.rbac` (header-based Permission/Principal scope).** Picked directly per `feedback_pick_recommendation`. Per the §9 HTTP-filter sub-feature enumeration (header_mutation DONE at 07.2; local_ratelimit DONE at 09), considered the remaining ~14 candidate filters along (config shape / foundations needed / framework extension needed / carryforward closure):

  - **rbac (WINNER — header-based scope)** — chain-config; no per-route required at phase-10 scope; ZERO foundations (reuses 04.2 HeaderMatcher); ZERO framework extension (Decision::StopAndSend exists from 07.1; H1 HCM `decorate_filter_synth_response` helper exists from 09 ADR-0033 Commit C); closes 09 REVIEW M2 + M3 at named-owner sites; ~1100-1300 LoC including tests + fixture (under §6.1 gate). Header-only Permission/Principal types (Any + Header + AndRules/AndIds + OrRules/OrIds + NotRule/NotId combinators); IP/CIDR + metadata + authenticated + url_path + SNI + CEL + shadow_rules all defer per SPEC §4.
  - **fault (abort-only)** — runner-up; ~700-900 LoC; needs `rand` foundations grant (ADR-0034) OR hand-rolled XorShift32 PRNG (~30-50 LoC primitive); closes 09 M2 + M3 if H1 backstop. Rejected on foundation-pressure dimension — `rand` grant or hand-rolled PRNG primitive both add risk beyond rbac's reuse-only posture.
  - **cors** — needs per-route framework extension (CorsPolicy is primary per-route in upstream Envoy); ~1000-1200 LoC + per-route primitive (~200-300 LoC). Rejected on arch-risk dimension — per-route primitive is load-bearing for many later filters but higher risk than rbac's bounded matcher tree.
  - **rbac (IP-included scope)** — would close 09 M2 + M3 + more; needs IP/CIDR matcher primitive (not currently in envoy-config). Rejected — IP matcher primitive defers per the standing principle that new framework primitives are gating architectural changes; header-scoped rbac is the minimum-viable cut.
  - **buffer** — tiny config; needs new body-buffering framework extension (larger than the filter itself). Rejected.
  - **csrf** — per-route primary; same per-route extension as cors. Rejected.
  - **compression** — needs `flate2`/`brotli`/`zstd` foundations grants + new pluggable-compressor primitive. Rejected.
  - **jwt_authn** — needs `jsonwebtoken` foundations grant + JOSE primitive. Rejected.

  - **oauth2** — needs HTTPS client + auth-state framework. Rejected.
  - **adaptive concurrency** — sophisticated gradient algorithm. Rejected.
  - **admission control** — probabilistic + stats-heavy (P50/P99). Rejected.
  - **bandwidth limit** — per-stream timing; needs body-streaming framework extension. Rejected on framework-extension dimension despite the appealing M1+T2 closure opportunity (TokenBucketState reuse with bytes-as-tokens).
  - **global rate limit** — depends on gRPC family. Rejected.
  - **lua / wasm** — own multi-phase sub-projects per §9. Rejected.

  Top-3 viable: rbac (header-scoped) > fault (abort-only) > cors. **rbac (header-scoped) wins** on: zero foundations grant (reuses 04.2 HeaderMatcher directly); zero framework extension (uses existing H1 HCM helper + StopAndSend); closes 09 REVIEW M2 + M3 at named sites; validates StopAndSend on a non-rate-limit semantic (deny-by-policy vs rate-exhaustion); ~1100-1300 LoC under §6.1 gate. Action-vs-match decision matrix per SPEC §5.6: `Allow+match → ALLOW`, `Allow+no_match → DENY`, `Deny+match → DENY`, `Deny+no_match → ALLOW`. Empirical body bytes (under both `curl -i` default-keep-alive AND Python TCP client mirroring `drive_http_get`'s `Connection: close` framing — identical body): `content-length: 19` + body hex `52 42 41 43 3a 20 61 63 63 65 73 73 20 64 65 6e 69 65 64` = `"RBAC: access denied"` (19 bytes, NO trailing newline). SPEC projected `"RBAC: access denied\n"` (20 bytes). **MATERIAL DIFFERENCE.** **Disposition: ADR-0034 (option A per SPEC §7) lands inline at THIS state-2 PLAN-write commit.** The ADR records the empirical evidence + the 6 inline SPEC.md revisions (each replaces 20-byte projection with 19-byte reality + cross-refs ADR-0034). ### Phase-12 state-1 brainstorm

Brainstorm session decisions (THIS commit), all per the user's standing preferences `feedback_pick_recommendation` ("always pick the recommended option; do not ask") and `feedback_execution_style` ("default to subagent-driven-development; skip the two-option fork" — applies to state-3, not this state-1 controller-run brainstorm). This is the **fourth post-MVP-trunk feature-family brainstorm session** (after phase-09 `3025594` + phase-10 `c73f44f` + phase-11 `1370aaa`; the latter is the freshest shape precedent). The pick was made directly per `feedback_pick_recommendation` — no two-option fork; the alternatives + 5-dimension scoring are documented below.

- **Family pick: Upstream robustness family (FIRST concrete phase; first feature-family phase to LEAVE the HTTP-filter family).** Picked directly per `feedback_pick_recommendation`. **The decisive context shift:** the HTTP-filter family was picked three times running (09/10/11) chiefly to close the 09 REVIEW M2 H2-decoration carryforward — which CLOSED at phase 11 (the H1 + H2 HCM filter-synth writer paths are now at parity). With that driver gone, the pick is free to diversify. Applying the same 5-dimension scoring framework used at phases 09 + 10 + 11:

  - **Upstream robustness family (WINNER) — active HTTP health checking** — (a) carryforward closure **MEDIUM-HIGH** — it is the **named owner of 06.3 REVIEW I2** (the deferred synthetic-backend harness infrastructure; the REVIEW named "the upstream-robustness family" as the close site verbatim). Phase 12 makes the first down-payment (the synthetic health-aware backend); full I2 closure (per-class counter wire coverage + `upstream_cx_total` `value-exact`) remains tied to connection pooling per the REVIEW disposition. (b) foundation pressure **ZERO** — reuses tokio (already permitted) + `envoy-http1::Client` (04.3) for the probe + `envoy-config::parse_duration` + `Int64Range` + `envoy-stats`. (c) arch risk **LOW-MEDIUM** — the integration seam is **PRE-BUILT and annotated for this**: `ClusterHandle::pick_endpoint() -> Option<SocketAddr>` (`cluster.rs:152`, *"preserved for phase-06+ health checking"*) + the existing no-healthy-endpoint → synth-503 path (`router.rs:18-20`, `hcm.rs:580-582`). The genuinely-new surface is the periodic-probe task (the project's first periodic-background primitive) + the `EndpointHealth` state machine + the panic threshold. (d) contract maturity **MEDIUM** — new health-check stats + the no-healthy-upstream body need §6.2 empirical pinning. (e) scope tractability **MEDIUM (upper band; SPLIT projected)** — ~1800-2200 LoC, over the §6.1 gate → likely split into 12.1 + 12.2.
  - **Load balancing family** (`least_request` / `ring_hash` / `random` etc.) — documented "strong second-place" at phases 10 + 11 on the LoC/foundations axes, but **re-scored DOWN this brainstorm on differential-testability**: randomized LBs (`random`, default-P2C `least_request`) produce per-request endpoint picks that CANNOT be matched across two independent proxies (non-differential-testable, same class as fractional fault percentage at phase 11); the deterministic LBs (`ring_hash`, `maglev`) require EXACT hash-algorithm fidelity (xxHash / Maglev permutation) — high arch risk for differential equivalence. Any LB differential test also needs a NEW distinguishable-backend + endpoint-attribution harness primitive. (a) carryforward closure ZERO; (b) zero foundation; (c) LOW-MEDIUM but the differential-observability is fragile; (d) MEDIUM; (e) HIGH LoC tractability. **Rejected** on the differential-testability fragility + zero carryforward closure — a more careful analysis than the prior brainstorms' LoC-focused "second-place" billing.
  - **Continuing HTTP-filter family** (`cors` / `jwt_authn` / `ext_authz` / `csrf` / `compression` / `buffer`) — the low-hanging StopAndSend fruit is EXHAUSTED (header_mutation 07.2, local_ratelimit 09, rbac 10, fault 11 done). The remaining filters each need either a foundations grant (jwt_authn JOSE; oauth2 HTTPS client; compression flate2/brotli), a per-route framework extension (cors/csrf), or the gRPC family (ext_authz/ext_proc/global-rate-limit). So continuing now carries HIGHER foundation pressure / arch risk than before + the decisive 09-M2 driver is gone. **Rejected** — diversifying is the better engineering move.
  - **Network filters family** — HIGH arch risk (new network-layer filter-chain primitive) + LOW contract maturity. Rejected per the 09/10/11 reasoning.
  - **HTTP/3 + QUIC** — VERY HIGH foundation pressure (`quinn`) + VERY HIGH arch risk. Rejected.
  - **gRPC / xDS / Observability / Runtime+hot-restart / WASM / Deprecated** — same dispositions as phases 09/10/11 (unmotivated / highest-risk / multi-phase sub-project / meta-bookkeeping). Rejected.

  Top-3 viable: **Upstream robustness > Load balancing > continuing HTTP filters.** Upstream robustness wins on: closing the named-owner carryforward (06.3 I2); zero foundation pressure; the pre-built integration seam (lowering arch risk); and laying the periodic-task primitive the whole family needs. The SPEC §1 + §3 record the picked family + feature scope.

- **Feature pick: active HTTP health checking (HTTP checker only; minimum-viable).** Picked directly per `feedback_pick_recommendation`. Among the family's features (active HC / outlier detection / circuit breakers / retries / connection pooling), active HTTP health checking is the §9-listed-first + the cleanest first phase: response-based differential observable (200-through vs synth-503-no-healthy, deterministic in steady state), reuses the pre-built `pick()->Option` + synth-503 seam, and builds the periodic-probe primitive the family reuses. **Scope cuts (defer per SPEC §4):** TCP/gRPC/custom checkers; multiple health checks per cluster; outlier detection; circuit breakers; retries; connection pooling; `no_traffic_interval`/jitter/`reuse_connection`; event logging; degraded/excluded host states; HC over H2 upstream. HTTP-only + binary Healthy/Unhealthy + single fixed interval + fresh-connection-per-probe is the minimum-viable cut (consistent with the rbac "header-scope only" + fault "deterministic-only" minimum-viable discipline).

- **Phase id + slug pick:** **`12`** / **`12-upstream-active-health-check`**. id `12` is next sequential after `11` (the next standalone-phase id is the next integer; sub-phases get `.N` on split). The slug names the family (`upstream`) + the feature (`active-health-check`) per the readable-English hyphenation pattern (`11-http-filter-fault` / `10-http-filter-rbac` analogue). HTTP-checker scope (TCP/gRPC defer) is conveyed in the title/SPEC, not the slug.

- **depends-on pick:** **`02 04`** — phase `02` (cluster manager + round-robin LB seam being extended) + phase `04` (04.3's `envoy-http1::Client`, reused for the HTTP probe). Phase `06` (`envoy-stats`) is load-bearing for the health-check stats but is implicit (the schema captures the primary direct foundations; cross-deliverable reuse — `envoy-stats`, `parse_duration`, `Int64Range` — is implicit per the phase-11 "implicit 05 dep" precedent).

### Phase-12 state-2 split decision

This subsection records the phase-12 state-2 PLAN-write commit (`phase 12: state-2 split decision + sub-phase SPECs (12.1/12.2) [ADR-0036, ADR-0037]`) — the fifth project SPLIT state-2 (after phases 02/03/07/08), all per the user's standing preferences `feedback_pick_recommendation` (pick the recommendation; no two-option fork) + `feedback_execution_style` (the state-2 PLAN-write is the controller's authoring pass; subagent-driven execution applies at state 3). Docs-only; 5 files; ADR-0036 (split) + ADR-0037 (no-healthy-body reconciliation); no SPEC edit to the parent-12 SPEC; no PLAN/PROGRESS (those land at the 12.1 state-2 PLAN-write next session).

**§6.2 empirical-verification findings (HEAVY; 6 items; against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`).** Performed at THIS commit by the controller directly (per the parent SPEC §6.2 + the phase-10/11-ratified verify-at-PLAN-write discipline). Methodology: a Docker bridge network with (a) a synthetic health-aware backend container (returns 200 on `/`, a configurable status on `/healthz`, logs every probe) and (b) an `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` container running an active-HC cluster pointing at the backend by container name (STRICT_DNS); admin `/stats` scraped + data-plane `GET /` probed across the convergence window. *(Initial host-networking attempts via `host.docker.internal` network-failed because it resolves IPv6-only on this Docker Desktop; resolved by co-locating both containers on a shared bridge network.)*

| # | Item | Finding | Disposition |
|---|------|---------|-------------|
| 1 | **Initial endpoint health state** (the single most load-bearing) | **Unhealthy/pending-until-first-pass.** An unhealthy backend with a 3 s probe delay → data-plane `no healthy upstream` (503) from t=0, *before* the first probe resolves. Hosts with active HC configured begin not-healthy; the first passing check (`healthy_threshold` consecutive successes) marks them healthy. | **MATCHES** the parent SPEC's recommended projection. Drives D3 (`EndpointHealth` initial state = Unhealthy) + the 12.1 inert-and-unexercised-seam note. No ADR. |
| 2 | **No-healthy-upstream synth body** (the byte-precision item) | status **503**; body **`no healthy upstream`** = **19 bytes**, hex `6e 6f 20 68 65 61 6c 74 68 79 20 75 70 73 74 72 65 61 6d`, **no trailing newline**; headers `{ content-length:19, content-type:text/plain, date, server:envoy, connection:close }`; **no wire `x-envoy-*` flag header**. | **DIVERGES from envoy-rust's existing synth-503** (`hcm.rs:918 synth_status` = EMPTY body, content-length:0). → **ADR-0037**: reconcile envoy-rust to emit the 19-byte body on the no-healthy-upstream path (impl in 12.2 D6.2, only the `hcm.rs:582` arm — NOT global `synth_status`). Fixture 0019 asserts byte-exact. |
| 3 | **Panic threshold** | default **50 %**; comparison **strictly-below** (`healthy% < threshold`: `value:0` → `0%<0%`=false → no panic → 503; default 50 % → `0%<50%`=true → panic → 200 routed to all); `Percent` shape **`{ value: <double> }`**; panic = round-robin over ALL; bonus stat `cluster.<n>.lb_healthy_panic` (not wired at phase-12 scope). | **MATCHES** projection. Drives D1 (`CommonLbConfig`/`Percent`) + D5 (panic logic). Fixture uses `{ value: 0 }` (disable panic). No ADR. |
| 4 | **Health-check stat names** | `cluster.<n>.health_check.{attempt,success,failure,passive_failure,network_failure,verify_cluster,healthy,degraded}` + `membership_{healthy,total,degraded,excluded,change}`. `membership_healthy` = count of currently-healthy endpoints (1 healthy / 0 ejected). | **MATCHES** projection. 12.1 wires the minimum-viable subset: `attempt`/`success`/`failure` counters + `membership_healthy` gauge (rest defer per parent §4). No ADR. |
| 5 | **HTTP probe shape** | `GET /healthz`, `:authority`/`Host: <cluster-name>` (default when `http_health_check.host` unset), `user-agent: Envoy/HC`; default `expected_statuses` = **exactly 200** (201 → unhealthy); `Int64Range` **half-open `[start, end)`** (`[200,201)` excludes 201; `[200,202)` includes it — reusable directly). | **MATCHES** projection. Drives D1 (`HttpHealthCheck`) + D4 (probe). No ADR. |
| 6 | **Duration config shape** | Envoy accepts decimal-second protobuf-JSON durations (`1s`/`0.5s`/`0.25s`) but **REJECTS `500ms`**; envoy-rust's `parse_duration` accepts `1s`/`500ms`/`500us` (integer + s/ms/us) but **REJECTS `0.5s`** (parses the numeric part as `u64`). **Shared form = integer seconds only.** | **DIVERGES from the parent SPEC fixture sketch's `interval: 0.5s`** (which envoy-rust would reject). → **PLAN-time correction (no ADR):** the 12.2 fixture uses integer-second durations (`interval: 1s`, `timeout: 1s`) on both sides (identical YAMLs); 12.1 reuses `parse_duration` as-is (no `0.5s` support added — scope creep). |

**Disposition:** items 1/3/4/5 MATCHED → no ADR. Item 2 → **ADR-0037** (the load-bearing wire-level body bytes pinned; the ADR-0034-class durability decision; reconcile-by-implementation per D-3.3). Item 6 → PLAN-time fixture-shape correction (no ADR). DECISIONS.md ledger head **ADR-0035 → ADR-0037** (ADR-0036 split + ADR-0037 reconciliation, consecutive numbers at this commit per the parent SPEC §6.2 "if both fire at the PLAN-write commit").

### Phase-13 state-1 brainstorm

**Family pick.** `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §9 enumerates the eight feature families. At the post-12.2 close-out boundary the slate is fully open — all MVP-trunk phases 00-08 + the three HTTP-filter-family phases (09 `local_ratelimit`, 10 `rbac`, 11 `fault`) + the first Upstream-robustness-family phase (parent-12; sub-phases 12.1 + 12.2) all stand `done`. The candidates for the next phase were: (i) continue the Upstream-robustness family with `13-outlier-detection` (per-endpoint ejection on consecutive 5xx / per-host success-rate thresholds — natural family-list order after active HC) OR `13-connection-pooling` (per-protocol upstream connection pools — the named-owner phase for 06.3 REVIEW I2's residual); (ii) enter a new family (HTTP/3+QUIC, gRPC, xDS, Observability, Runtime+hot-restart, WASM-host).

**Five-dimension scoring:**

| Dimension | `13-outlier-detection` | `13-connection-pooling` | new family (HTTP/3+QUIC, gRPC, xDS, Observability, Runtime, WASM) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Carryforward closure value** | Zero (no named carryforward closes). Outlier detection is a fresh subsystem; would reuse the 12.1 `EndpointHealth` ejection seam but doesn't close anything from the standing inventory. | **HIGH.** Connection pooling is the **named-owner phase for 06.3 REVIEW I2 residual** per the 06.3 REVIEW.md §3 disposition + the 12.2 down-payment scoping. Closes BOTH (a) per-class `downstream_rq_3xx/4xx/5xx` + `cluster.<name>.upstream_rq_5xx` wire bilateral coverage AND (b) `cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_total` `value-exact` tightening. This is the single highest-value closure currently available in the standing inventory. | Zero direct closures. Some families surface their own internal carryforwards (e.g. Observability would tighten the StatsTagExtractor allow-list residual) but none close the 06.3 I2 residual. |
| **Foundation pressure (new top-level Cargo deps)** | LOW. Reuses the 12.1 `EndpointHealth` ejection seam + the 12.2 periodic-task primitive. No new crate. No ADR. | **LOW.** Reuses the 12.2 `HealthAwareHttp1Backend` harness primitive (extend in place) + the existing `ConnGaugeGuard` RAII pattern + `envoy-http1::Client` + `envoy-http2::Client`. Pool primitives live inside `envoy-http1`/`envoy-http2` (`pool.rs` modules). No new top-level Cargo dep. No new ADR projected at SPEC time (conditional ADR-0038 split LIKELY at PLAN-write; conditional ADR-0039 §6.2 revision PLAUSIBLE). | HIGH (variable). HTTP/3+QUIC needs `quinn` foundations grant; gRPC needs additional `tonic` features; xDS needs from-scratch state-machine atop `tonic` transport; Observability needs OTLP/Datadog/XRay; Runtime+hot-restart is significant new infrastructure; WASM-host is its own multi-phase sub-project. Each new family carries a foundations-grant ADR. |
| **Architectural risk** | MEDIUM. The passive-vs-active distinction is subtle (outlier detection observes data-plane responses; doesn't probe); needs careful interaction with the 12-active path. Cross-proxy timing-dependent ejection windows are hard to make deterministic for the differential harness (would need §Timing tolerances opt-in). | **MEDIUM-HIGH.** Pool primitives are the most-complex piece — H2 multiplexed-streams pool with peer-SETTINGS coordination + GOAWAY handling. But the surface is well-understood (Envoy's pool model is documented) + the per-protocol crate placement avoids cycles cleanly. The `upstream_cx_total` increment-site migration (from per-call to per-connection at pool create) is mechanical but must be atomic to avoid double-counting. The cycle-resolution decision (§5.1) is well-anticipated. | HIGH (variable). HTTP/3 introduces a new downstream listener type + a new conformance suite. gRPC complicates the H2 path. xDS introduces dynamic-config state. WASM is a full ABI + engine binding effort. |
| **Contract-surface maturity** | The `outlier_detection.*` Envoy stat tree is documented but timing-dependent. Differential observability is largely stats-based (which counter increments on which trigger) + ejection-window-bounded — harder than connection-pooling's deterministic-pool-state observable. | **HIGH.** The `cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_*` stat tree is fully documented + matures cleanly under pooling. Per-class HCM counters are already 06.3-defined and BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT-locked; phase 13 just realizes them at fixture level. The synthetic-backend pattern is 12.2-precedented. | Variable. xDS has the most mature contract (ADS state machine + effective-config diff). Observability and Runtime have moderate maturity. WASM is least-mature (ABI conformance suite still evolving upstream). |
| **First-phase scope tractability** | Tractable as a single phase if scoped to consecutive-5xx ejection only (split-gate plausible at PLAN-write but not certain). Reuses 12.x infrastructure heavily. | **MEDIUM.** ~1800-2400 LoC projected — over the §6.1 ~1500 gate. SPLIT into 13.1 + 13.2 LIKELY at PLAN-write (recommended seam: H1-only / H2-only, alternative seam: foundation-slice). Each sub-phase comes in at ~1000-1200 LoC each — manageable. | Variable. xDS family is its own multi-phase sub-project at minimum. Observability could fit as ~3 sub-phases. Runtime+hot-restart is moderate. WASM is multi-phase by design. HTTP/3+QUIC is moderate (probably 2 sub-phases — downstream H3 + upstream H3). |

**Decision: `13-connection-pooling`.** Per `feedback_pick_recommendation` (always pick the recommendation; no two-option fork). The recommendation is unambiguously connection pooling because: (1) it's the **named-owner phase for the highest-value standing carryforward** (06.3 REVIEW I2 residual, deferred from 06.3 and named again at 12.2); (2) it **reuses the freshest landed harness primitive** (12.2's `HealthAwareHttp1Backend`); (3) its scope is **tractable with a known SPLIT seam** (H1-only / H2-only at sub-phase 13.1/13.2); (4) the **foundation pressure is LOW** (no new top-level Cargo dep; pool primitives are protocol-internal); (5) it **continues the Upstream-robustness family** in a natural way (active HC at 12 → pooling at 13; outlier detection + circuit breakers + retries defer to follow-up phases — all reuse the 12.x + 13.x infrastructure when they land). The decision is **NOT** "outlier detection" — outlier detection has zero carryforward closure value and timing-dependent observability that the differential harness handles less cleanly; it defers to a follow-up Upstream-robustness phase. The decision is **NOT** "enter a new family" — the project's standing posture (per `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §9 family ordering + the established Carryforward-closure-value-first heuristic from the 11/12 brainstorms) favors closing named residuals before opening new families when both are tractable.

**SPLIT projection at state-2.** The SPEC §6.1 LoC estimate (~1800-2400) is materially over the §6.1 ~1500-LoC gate. **The state-2 PLAN-writer is expected to SPLIT phase 13 into `13.1` + `13.2`** at the standalone-PLAN-write commit, mirroring the parent-12 split `4f9ba04` (ADR-0036) + the parent-08 / parent-07 / parent-03 / parent-02 split precedents. **Recommended seam:** `13.1` = H1 pool primitive + envoy-config `circuit_breakers.thresholds` schema + H1 router-arm pool integration + the configurable-status synthetic-backend harness extension + fixture 0020 (H1-only; per-class counter bilateral coverage); `13.2` = H2 pool primitive + H2 router-arm pool integration + the `cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_total` BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT row tightening to `value-exact` (the 06.3 REVIEW I2 (b) full-closure site — lands when both protocols pool) + parent-13 close. Each sub-phase comes in at ~1000-1200 LoC — comfortably under the §6.1 gate. **Alternative seam (foundation-slice):** `13.1` = H1 + H2 pool primitives + envoy-config schema + NO new fixture (regression-equivalence via existing 19 fixtures — the 05.1 / 07.1 / 12.1 foundation-slice pattern); `13.2` = router-arm wiring + new fixture + per-class bilateral coverage + parent-13 close. State-2 PLAN-writer picks; **recommended: H1-only / H2-only seam** (narrower per-protocol sub-phases; foundation-slice alternative documented). The SPLIT decision lands at the state-2 PLAN-write per the parent-12 / parent-08 precedent — NOT at THIS state-1 brainstorm.

**ADR projection.** **No ADR landed at THIS state-1 commit** — the parent SPEC itself is the design artifact (mirrors the phase-12 state-1 precedent at `edd654c` which landed no ADR). Conditional ADRs reserved for state-2 / state-3 landing:

- **Conditional ADR-0038 (split). LIKELY TO FIRE at state-2 PLAN-write** if the SPLIT executes (per §6.1 projection). Mirrors ADR-0036 (parent-12 split).
- **Conditional ADR-0039 (§6.2 empirical-verification revision). PLAUSIBLE at state-2 PLAN-write** if any of the 9 §6.2 items (esp. the `circuit_breakers` shape or the `upstream_cx_total` default-pool behavior) differs materially from the SPEC's state-1 projection. Mirrors ADR-0034 (phase-10 §6.2 revision) + ADR-0037 (phase-12 §6.2 revision).

**§6.2 empirical-verification findings (HEAVY; 9 items; against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`).** Performed at THIS commit by the controller directly (per the parent SPEC §6.2 + the phase-10/11/12-ratified verify-at-PLAN-write discipline). Methodology: a Docker bridge network (`p13net`) with (a) a Python-based configurable HTTP/1.1 backend container (Python 3.12-alpine; `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` with `protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"` for keep-alive support; serves 200 on `/`, 301/404/500/503 on `/301`/`/404`/`/500`/`/503`, configurable status on `/healthz` via `HEALTHZ_STATUS` env) and (b) an `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` container running an HTTP/1.1 HCM listener routing through a STRICT_DNS cluster with `circuit_breakers: { thresholds: [{ priority: DEFAULT, max_connections: 2 }] }` pointing at the backend container by container name; admin `/stats` + `/config_dump` scraped + data-plane requests driven from the host via curl + Python `http.client.HTTPConnection`. *(Initial container-name resolution attempts via `backend` failed because Docker's DNS resolves the container's full name `p13-backend`; resolved by updating the YAML.)* For item (vi) — H2 cluster stats namespace — booted a second Envoy with `typed_extension_protocol_options.envoy.extensions.upstreams.http.v3.HttpProtocolOptions.explicit_http_config.http2_protocol_options: {}` and scraped the cluster stat namespace (no H2C backend reach needed; the stat names are registered at cluster-construct time).

| # | Item | Finding | Disposition |
|---|------|---------|-------------|
| i | **`circuit_breakers.thresholds` shape + max_connections default** | `circuit_breakers: { thresholds: [{ priority?: <RoutingPriority>, max_connections?: u32, max_pending_requests?: u32, max_requests?: u32, max_retries?: u32, ... }] }`. The `priority` field defaults to `DEFAULT` (and is omitted from `/config_dump` when DEFAULT). `max_connections` default 1024 (per Envoy docs; not observed empirically because the harness load is below the cap). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. Schema D1 lands as projected (`Cluster.circuit_breakers: Option<CircuitBreakers>` with `Thresholds` carrying `priority?: Option<RoutingPriority>` + `max_connections?: Option<u32>`; phase-13 supports DEFAULT + max_connections only; other threshold fields rejected by `deny_unknown_fields`). No ADR. |
| ii | **H1 default pool behavior under NO `circuit_breakers`** | Envoy ALWAYS pools regardless of `circuit_breakers` config (a no-`circuit_breakers` cluster + 5 requests over a single downstream keep-alive conn → `upstream_cx_total: 1`; full pool reuse). `circuit_breakers` is OPTIONAL at config-time; absence means defaults. `/config_dump` shows `circuit_breakers: "<absent>"` when not configured (Envoy doesn't echo defaults). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. § 5.4 default-enabled-pool decision: phase-13's H1 pool runs **with hardcoded defaults when `circuit_breakers` is absent** (NOT pool-gated by the field). The 19 existing fixtures (none configures `circuit_breakers`) pool transparently. Regression-equivalence guaranteed by the existing presence-only `upstream_cx_total` assertions (no value-exact assertion to regress). No ADR. |
| iii | **H1 idle_timeout knob + default** | Knob lives at `typed_extension_protocol_options.envoy.extensions.upstreams.http.v3.HttpProtocolOptions.common_http_protocol_options.idle_timeout` (a Duration; nested deep). NOT at the cluster top-level. Default: 1 hour (3600s) per upstream Envoy docs. /config_dump shows `<absent>` for the nested field when not explicitly set. | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. §4 deferral: phase-13 (13.1 + 13.2) does NOT add the config-side `idle_timeout` knob; the pool uses a hardcoded sensible default (60s — short enough to test idle eviction in a deterministic test, long enough to not fire under fixture settle windows). The config-side knob defers to a follow-up phase. No ADR. |
| iv | **`upstream_cx_total` increment semantics + discriminating differential observable** | One increment per established upstream TCP connection. Discriminating observable shape: with a **SINGLE downstream keep-alive conn** issuing 5 sequential requests → `upstream_cx_total: 1` (full pool reuse via 1 upstream connection). With **separate downstream conns** (curl invocations) → `upstream_cx_total: N` (one upstream connect per downstream-side conn — Envoy's H1 pool returns the connection to idle AFTER the downstream conn closes, by which point the next downstream conn has already triggered a fresh upstream connect). Concurrent 4 curl jobs with `max_connections: 2` → `upstream_cx_total: 4` + `upstream_cx_overflow: 2` (max_connections is ADVISORY: Envoy increments the overflow counter but still completes the request). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection but with **CRITICAL NUANCE**. **PLAN-time fixture-shape lock-in:** fixture 0020 driver MUST issue multiple requests over a SINGLE downstream keep-alive conn to make `upstream_cx_total` the discriminating differential observable (1 vs. N). The differential harness's existing `Driver::Http1` opens one conn per request — **13.1 D10 extends the driver with `Driver::Http1KeepAlive`** (~30 LoC; mirrors 12.2's `Driver::Http1AfterSettle` precedent). NOT a wire-contract change → NO ADR fires. |
| v | **`upstream_cx_destroy` + sibling counter names + fire-sites** | Full sibling set per-cluster: `upstream_cx_destroy`, `_destroy_local`, `_destroy_remote`, `_destroy_with_active_rq`, `_destroy_local_with_active_rq`, `_destroy_remote_with_active_rq`, `upstream_cx_close_notify` (counts peer-initiated Connection: close). All fire when a pool connection is destroyed (different sub-counters for local-initiated vs remote-initiated destruction; the per-`_with_active_rq` variants fire only when destruction happens while a request was outstanding). All per-cluster (NOT per-endpoint). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. D7 (stats): phase-13 wires the parent `upstream_cx_destroy` (always-fire sibling) + `upstream_cx_http1_total` (H1 pool connect counter) + the 13.2-landed `upstream_cx_http2_total`. The 5 sub-siblings defer to follow-up phases (no fixture deterministically forces local-vs-remote-destroy at phase-13 scope). No ADR. |
| vi | **H2 pool default behavior + max_concurrent_streams + multi-conn per endpoint** | H2 cluster stat namespace (no H2 traffic needed; Envoy registers at cluster-construct time): `cluster.<n>.upstream_cx_http1_total` (always registered; even on H2 cluster — for cross-protocol fallback), `upstream_cx_http2_total` (H2 partition), `upstream_cx_http3_total` (H3 — registered for future use). Default `max_concurrent_streams`: Envoy-as-client honors peer's `SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` (default 100 per RFC 7540 §6.5.2 if peer doesn't send SETTINGS). Per-endpoint multi-conn threshold: Envoy spawns 2nd upstream H2 conn only when 1st is at peer's cap. Legacy cluster-field `http2_protocol_options` stays absent in `/config_dump` when `typed_extension_protocol_options` is used (Envoy's modern path). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. 13.2 D5 H2 pool primitive design: per-endpoint connection list with `active_streams: AtomicU32` tracking + spawn 2nd conn only when 1st at peer's `SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` cap (or cluster's `max_connections` cap, whichever is lower). 13.2 D7.2 lands the `cluster.<n>.upstream_cx_http2_total` BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT row. No ADR. |
| vii | **Per-class HCM counters under synthetic 5xx backend fixture** | Drove 6 requests through a single downstream keep-alive conn: 2× GET /(200), 1× GET /301(301), 1× GET /404(404), 1× GET /500(500), 1× GET /503(503). HCM scrape: `http.ingress_http.downstream_rq_2xx: 2`, `_3xx: 1`, `_4xx: 1`, `_5xx: 2`, `_total: 6`. Listener-namespace mirror: `listener.0.0.0.0_10000.http.ingress_http.downstream_rq_{2,3,4,5}xx` — same values. Bilateral byte-exact achievable under deterministic load. | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. 13.1 D9.1 fixture 0020 lands the per-class workload; the existing BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT rows at `:96-100` (06.3-landed `value-exact`) are EXERCISED bilaterally at the wire level for the FIRST time at this fixture — the **06.3 REVIEW I2 (a) full-closure site**. No ADR. |
| viii | **`cluster.<name>.upstream_rq_5xx` + siblings** | Same 6-request workload: cluster scrape `cluster.backend_cluster.upstream_rq_2xx: 2`, `_3xx: 1`, `_4xx: 1`, `_5xx: 2`, `_total: 6`. Cluster-namespace per-class counters match HCM-namespace per-class counters byte-exact under deterministic load (because router-proxy passes through every upstream status). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. Fixture 0020 also asserts the cluster-namespace per-class values (a second I2 (a) closure surface). The existing BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT row at `:106` (06.3-landed `upstream_rq_5xx: value-exact`) is EXERCISED bilaterally at the wire level here for the first time. No ADR. |
| ix | **HCM filter-synth bypass on per-class counters** | **CONFIRMED.** Shut down backend → GET / → synth-503 `no healthy upstream` (body verified byte-exact = ADR-0037's 19 bytes; bonus phase-12 ADR-0037 bilateral re-confirmation). HCM `downstream_rq_5xx`: 2 → 3 (synth INCLUDED at HCM); HCM `downstream_rq_total`: 6 → 7. Cluster `upstream_rq_5xx`: 2 → 2 (synth NOT INCLUDED at cluster); Cluster `upstream_rq_total`: 6 → 6 (synth bypasses upstream → no upstream counter increment). | **MATCHES** the existing 06.3 BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT note at `:96-106` exactly ("the per-class counter is symmetric on `response_status_for_log`, agnostic to synth-vs-proxy origin" applies at HCM; cluster-level upstream_rq_* is upstream-only). Phase-13 preserves the bypass unchanged. **Bonus: ADR-0037's 19-byte `no healthy upstream` body bilaterally re-confirmed in passing** (a useful re-validation of the 12.2 implementation). No ADR. |

**Cycle-resolution decision (PLAN lock-in #1) — picked per `feedback_pick_recommendation`:** the 13.1 SPEC §5.1 left the seam open between (a) a new trait declared in `envoy-cluster` (`H1ClientPool` trait implemented by `envoy-http1::H1Pool`; held as `Cluster.h1_pool: Option<Arc<dyn H1ClientPool>>`) vs (b) bin-wired injection via an external `H1PoolManager` registry sibling-to-`ClusterManager`. PLAN-time PICK: option (b). Rationale: (1) option (a) requires interior mutability on `Cluster` (the `Arc<Cluster>` from `from_bootstrap` has no setter), OR widening `from_bootstrap`'s signature to take a `pool_builder` callback, OR chicken-and-egg pre-building with `Cluster.cx_total` registration — all intrusive. (3) NO new trait in `envoy-cluster`; only `ConnGaugeGuard` gains a public `from_gauge` constructor (4-line addition) so pools can construct guards against the shared cluster gauge handle. (4) NO new top-level Cargo dep (per lock-in #9). (5) NO ADR fires (per lock-in #16). Sequential ejection→un-eject→re-eject sequences showed ejection-duration ≈ 5-6s regardless of N (the `* num_ejections` multiplier exists in Envoy docs but is NOT material at minimum-viable). | **MATCHES** parent SPEC projection. 14.2 D7 sweeper locks: each `interval` tick, re-eval each ejected endpoint; un-eject if `now_monotonic - eject_time >= base_ejection_time`. Per-endpoint counters reset on un-eject AND on any 2xx/3xx/4xx response (D4). The `* num_ejections` multiplier is out per parent §4. No ADR. |
| 6 | **Discriminating observable for fixture 0022** | Exact byte-level capture (4-request sequence over single keepalive conn, `consecutive_5xx: 3`, single endpoint serving 500 on `/fail`): request 1-3 = status 500 + len 13 + body `server error\n` + `x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 2/0/0`; request 4-5 = status 503 + len 19 + body `no healthy upstream` + `x-envoy-upstream-service-time` ABSENT. Synth-503 headers: `content-length: 19`, `content-type: text/plain`, `server: envoy`, NO upstream-service-time. The 19-byte body matches ADR-0037 projection exactly. Counter values after 4 requests: `ejections_active: 1`, `ejections_consecutive_5xx: 1`, `ejections_detected_consecutive_5xx: 1`, `ejections_enforced_consecutive_5xx: 1`, `ejections_enforced_total: 1`, `ejections_total: 1`, `ejections_consecutive_gateway_failure: 0` (backend 500 ≠ gateway-failure 502/503/504). | **MATCHES** parent SPEC projection completely. 14.2 D8.1 fixture-0022 bilateral assertions lock-in: request 1-3 status 500 + body `server error\n` + upstream-service-time PRESENT; request 4 status 503 + body `no healthy upstream` (19 bytes) + upstream-service-time ABSENT; post-settle counters `ejections_active == 1`, `ejections_enforced_total == 1`, `ejections_enforced_consecutive_5xx == 1`, `ejections_detected_consecutive_5xx == 1`, `ejections_overflow == 0`. No ADR. |
| 7 | **Composition with active HC** | 2-endpoint cluster with HC + OD both configured (18080 HC-bad+data-bad; 18081 HC-good+data-bad): both `cluster.<n>.health_check.*` AND `outlier_detection.*` stat trees emit simultaneously. 18080 (HC-failing): `health_check.failure` ticks; `/clusters` admin shows `health_flags::/failed_active_hc`; excluded from `pick()` so receives no data-plane traffic → its OD counters stay at 0. 18081 (HC-ok, data-bad): after 3 `/fail` via `pick()`, OD ejects it; `/clusters` shows `health_flags::/failed_outlier_check`; `membership_healthy: 0/2`; 4th request returns synth-503. HC continues probing OD-ejected endpoints (the two systems operate independently; AND-composition computed at `pick()` time via union of health-flag bits). | **MATCHES** parent SPEC projection. 14.1 D5 locks the AND-composition at `pick()`: candidate iff `EndpointHealth::is_healthy() AND !EndpointEjection::is_ejected()`; both signals are independent bits; HC continues probing OD-ejected endpoints (no coupling). No ADR. |
| 8 | **H1 vs H2 sibling consistency** | H2 upstream cluster (`typed_extension_protocol_options...http2_protocol_options: {}`) + same OD config. H1-only helper backend doesn't speak H2c → connect-failure → Envoy emits synth-503 `upstream connect error`. After 3 such requests: identical `cluster.<n>.outlier_detection.*` stat namespace emitted (same 21 names); ejection-on-failure semantics identical (`ejections_active: 1`, `ejections_enforced_consecutive_5xx: 1`); subsequent requests get synth-503 `no healthy upstream` (19 bytes). True H2 200/500 mix not tested (out of time budget; needs H2-speaking backend) but stat-namespace parity + ejection-on-failure parity confirmed. OD logic is protocol-agnostic in Envoy. | **MATCHES** parent SPEC projection. The state-machine + sweeper + stat namespace are protocol-agnostic; the response-receipt hook surface differs (H1 router vs H2 HCM post-dispatch) but both call the same `Cluster::record_response`. 14.2 D4 wires both. The split-seam decision picked foundation-cohesion (NOT protocol-cohesion as 13.x picked) explicitly because of this protocol-agnosticity. No ADR. |
| 9 | **Synth-status bypass + connect-failure classification** | `consecutive_5xx: 1`, `consecutive_gateway_failure: 1`, endpoint = `127.0.0.1:1` (unreachable). Request 1: status 503 + len 167 + body `upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers...`. After this single request: `ejections_active: 1`, `ejections_detected_consecutive_5xx: 1` AND `ejections_detected_consecutive_gateway_failure: 1` (BOTH detectors fire — connect-fail classified as BOTH 5xx-equivalent AND gateway-failure for the picked endpoint), `ejections_enforced_consecutive_5xx: 1`, `ejections_enforced_total: 1`. Request 2: status 503 + len 19 + body `no healthy upstream` — all counters UNCHANGED (the synth-503 from `pick() -> None` does NOT feed back; no endpoint to attribute). | **DIVERGES MATERIALLY** from parent SPEC §5.7 uniform-bypass projection. **ADR-0041 ratifies** the nuanced classification: connect-failure synth paths (picked endpoint failed to connect) DO call `Cluster::record_response` with status 503 classified as BOTH `consecutive_5xx` AND `consecutive_gateway_failure`; `pick() -> None` no-healthy-upstream synth-503 path does NOT call `record_response` (no endpoint to attribute). 14.2 D4 wires the bypass at the router-arm dispatch site explicitly. |

**Critical scoping finding → ADR-0042 (landed at THIS commit).** The brainstorm verified the code directly (read-only `Explore` survey + controller verification of `crates/envoy-http1/src/pool.rs:177-398` + `crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:525-559`) and found the charter framing *"`max_connections` — parsed but NOT enforced"* **FALSE at HEAD `b575bdc35`**: the cap is ALREADY ENFORCED, landed at phase 13 — `H1Pool::acquire`/`H2Pool::acquire` check `established >= max_connections` → `PoolError::Overflow`; `for_bootstrap` sources the cap from `circuit_breakers.thresholds[0].max_connections` (default 1024); both router arms reject overflow with a synth-503; the schema + validator landed at 13.1. **Phase 15 therefore re-scopes from *implement-enforcement* to *observability + differential-coverage*:** (1) two minimum-viable circuit-breaker stats — `cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_overflow` (counter, at the pool cap-check site) + `cluster.<name>.circuit_breakers.default.cx_open` (gauge, edge-driven; the 14.1 namespace-subset precedent — emit the names Envoy emits for the breaker enforced, allow-list the rest); (2) the project's first CONCURRENT differential driver `Driver::Http1Concurrent` (+ a `--hold-ms` backend knob) to force concurrent upstream-connection demand > cap, since every existing driver is sequential and cannot trip it; (3) a schema carve-out accepting `max_pending_requests: 0` ONLY (the no-queue config making Envoy reject overflow immediately, matching envoy-rust, WITHOUT the deferred pending-request queue); (4) fixture `0023-upstream-circuit-breaker-max-connections` (K=2 concurrent / cap=1, single-endpoint cluster) proving the `{200, 503}` status multiset + `upstream_cx_overflow: 1` bilaterally. ADR-0042 records the finding + the minimum-viable scope boundary (defers: `max_pending_requests>0` queue; `max_requests`; `max_retries`/`retry_budget`; `max_connection_pools`; `track_remaining`/`remaining_*`; non-DEFAULT priority; per-endpoint-vs-per-cluster `cx_open` reconciliation). The brainstorm-time ADR is a cadence DEPARTURE from phases 12/13/14 (whose brainstorms landed no ADR), justified by the non-obvious scope finding per D-3.5 + the cold-readability correction of the durable record per D-3.4.

### Phase-15 state-2 PLAN-write

THIS commit is the **phase-15 state-2 standalone PLAN-write** (`phase 15: state-2 standalone PLAN-write — PLAN.md + PROGRESS.md skeleton + Task 1 preamble [ADR-0043]`) per `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §5 state 2 + `SKILL_ROUTING.md` state 2 + `superpowers:writing-plans` + `feedback_pick_recommendation` (no fork) + `feedback_execution_style` (the state-3 implementation is subagent-driven; this controller-direct PLAN-write dispatched ONE foreground general-purpose subagent for the §6.2 Docker verification per the 14.x precedent). Controller-direct (no implementer subagents at state 2).

**The HEAVY §6.2 empirical verification falsified the SPEC's central premise → ADR-0043 (landed at THIS commit).** A foreground general-purpose subagent ran `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (sibling-container Docker topology — `host.docker.internal` resolved to an unreachable IPv6 on this macOS host) against a `max_connections:1` + `max_pending_requests:0` cluster + concurrent/sequential drivers + admin `/stats` scrapes + a `%RESPONSE_FLAGS%` access log + `curl -i`/`wc -c`/`hexdump` body capture + a control run with `max_pending_requests` removed. **Findings 1/2/3 diverged materially:**

1. **`max_pending_requests:0` rejects EVERY request** (K=1, K=2, sequential) with a 503 — NOT "serve one, reject the over-cap one." The pool never warms; the backend is never contacted; `upstream_cx_total:0`, `upstream_cx_overflow:0`. The live counter is **`cluster.<name>.upstream_rq_pending_overflow`** (= reject count). (Control — `max_pending_requests` removed, default 1024, cap=1, K=2 → both served 200, `upstream_cx_overflow:1`, `upstream_cx_total:2`: the cap-overflow connection demand is COUNTED in `upstream_cx_overflow` but then QUEUED as pending and SERVED.)
2. The overflow-503 body is **NON-EMPTY**: the byte-exact 81-byte `upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: overflow` (no trailing newline) + the `x-envoy-overloaded: true` header. The `UO` (UpstreamOverflow) flag is access-log-only; on the wire it surfaces as `x-envoy-overloaded`.
3. There is **no `max_connections` config** under which both proxies produce an identical response-status multiset on the overflow path WITHOUT the deferred pending-request queue (Envoy queues a cap-overflow → may serve 200; envoy-rust 503s immediately). The SPEC's bilateral `{200,503}` fixture is unachievable as specified.

**Findings 4–7 matched the projection** (no SPEC revision): `cx_open` at-cap inclusive (`1` when `upstream_cx_active == max_connections`); `max_connections` per-cluster/per-priority (single-endpoint fixture coincides); full `circuit_breakers.*` = 10 always-emitted gauges (`{default,high}.{cx_open, cx_pool_open, rq_open, rq_pending_open, rq_retry_open}`); overflow-rejected request does NOT increment `upstream_cx_total`.

**Re-scope (ADR-0043 option c — partially supersedes ADR-0042's §2.1 star-stat + §2.3 carve-out model; RETAINS the observability charter).** Phase 15 now delivers: (1) `envoy-config` `Thresholds.max_pending_requests: Option<u32>` (accept 0/absent; reject `>0` → `ConfigError::UnsupportedNonZeroMaxPendingRequests`); (2) a FAITHFUL `max_pending_requests:0` reject-on-establish gate in the H1 + H2 pools + the `cluster.<name>.upstream_rq_pending_overflow` counter; (3) the ADR-0042 `cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_overflow` counter + `cluster.<name>.circuit_breakers.default.cx_open` gauge (RETAINED — at-cap inclusive, edge-driven, inert-when-unconfigured); (4) a `synth_overflow()` 503 helper (81-byte body + `x-envoy-overloaded`; H1 + H2; corrects the pre-existing H2 overflow-**502**→503 bug — PLAN §0.B C-1); (5) bilateral fixture `0023-upstream-circuit-breaker-max-pending-requests` (SINGLE GET, `max_pending_requests:0` → both 503; timing-robust, no concurrency/slow-backend); (6) fixture-0020 inert-0 assertions on the two new gauges/counters; (7) an in-process backstop validating BOTH overflow paths (pending-overflow single-GET + cx-overflow cap=1/K=2-concurrent with `cx_open` both edges). DEFER: the `max_pending_requests > 0` pending-request QUEUE + the `{200,200}` queue-and-serve bilateral overflow fixture; `max_requests`/`max_retries`/`track_remaining`/multi-priority; the multi-endpoint per-cluster `cx_open` reconciliation.

**§6.1 split-gate: NO SPLIT** (10 impl tasks + close-out; ~1100–1250 LoC; under the ~1500-LoC / ~25-task gate). **ADR ledger:** `ADR-0042` → **ADR-0043** (count 44; next available **ADR-0044**, reserved-but-not-fired). **PLAN-time SPEC corrections** (PROGRESS Task 1 preamble C-0…C-5): C-0 the ADR-0043 re-scope; C-1 the H2 overflow-502→503; C-2 the existing deny-unknown test re-pointed `max_pending_requests:5` → `max_requests:5`; C-3 the fixture rename; C-4 `Driver::Http1Concurrent` + `--hold-ms` DROPPED; C-5 fuzz seed extended in place (corpus stays 22). **Carryforward (none gate):** per-endpoint-vs-per-cluster `cx_open` + the `max_pending_requests>0` queue → future phases; the standing multi-phase Minor inventory + the `upstream_cx_total` TCP carve-out + **ADR-0028** carry forward unchanged.

THIS subsection landed at the **phase-16 state-1 NEW-PHASE brainstorm** (commit `phase 16: state-1 brainstorm — http-retries SPEC.md (Upstream-robustness family; HTTP retry policy retry_on/num_retries + upstream_rq_retry* stats + x-envoy-attempt-count + fixture 0024) [ADR-0044]`), which advanced the Active-phase pointer from "AWAITING NEXT PLANNING" to phase `16` state-1-complete / state-2-next. It records the family-pick + feature-pick rationale, the critical body-replay feasibility finding (ratified in ADR-0044), the §6.1 split projection, and the carryforward inputs consulted.

**The pick — phase `16 — HTTP retries` (the FIFTH concrete Upstream-robustness-family phase).** With phases 12 (active HTTP health checking) / 13 (per-protocol connection pooling H1+H2) / 14 (outlier detection consecutive-5xx/gateway-failure) / 15 (circuit-breaker observability + `max_pending_requests:0` reject) all `done`, the brainstorm continued the Upstream-robustness family with **HTTP retries** — the `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §9 charter's *"retries + hedging"* member. **Alternatives weighed + rejected for the next pick:** (a) open a NEW family (HTTP/3+QUIC, gRPC, xDS, Observability, Runtime+hot-restart, WASM-host) — rejected as the next pick (large foundation lifts; high architectural risk; better taken deliberately AFTER the in-flight family is wrapped; remain seeded §9 headings); (b) circuit-breaker-budget expansion (`max_requests`/`max_retries`/`track_remaining`/multi-priority + the pending-request queue) or TCP-proxy pooling — rejected for the next pick because `max_retries` (the retry circuit breaker) DEPENDS on retries existing (so retries comes first), the pending-queue is the more complex deferred surface, and TCP-proxy pooling is a narrower opportunistic close; (c) the FULL Envoy retry surface — rejected as over-scoped (bundles `per_try_timeout`, custom back-off, retry budgets, host-predicates, header overrides, hedging — blows the §6.1 gate). **Chosen rationale:** retries is the family's natural capstone at the LOWEST architectural risk (a retry loop wraps the EXISTING H1 `hcm.rs:465-706` + H2 `hcm.rs:238-481` dispatch seams — no new crate/transport/periodic-background primitive), the HIGHEST foundation reuse (the 12.x health + 14.x ejection `pick_endpoint()` seam, the 13.x pools, the 14.2 `record_response` hook, the 04.2 config patterns, the configurable-status synthetic backend), an excellent TIMING-ROBUST differential (a single GET against a 503→200 stateful backend — no concurrency, avoiding the phase-15 concurrent-driver flakiness vector), and it UNBLOCKS the deferred `max_retries` circuit-breaker budget.

**Critical scoping finding — the body-replay feasibility finding (ADR-0044).** A retry feature is feasible only if a failed request is replayable. A read-only `Explore` subagent survey + controller cross-check found retries are ALREADY body-replay-safe: **H1 DRAINS the downstream body and dispatches an EMPTY body** (`crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:401-420`, `:488`; chunked rejected with synth-501 at `:375-381` — a phase-04.3 scope choice), and **H2 BUFFERS the body and dispatches a CLONE** (`crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:153-162`, `:290`). **Phase 16 therefore needs NO new request-body buffering machinery** — the retry loop re-sends the same captured request shape per attempt. This non-obvious finding (analogous to phase-15's "enforcement-already-landed-at-13") makes a minimum-viable retry phase tractable as a single un-split (or thin 2-way-split) phase. The minimum-viable scope (ADR-0044): deliver retry-on-(`5xx`/`gateway-error`/`connect-failure`/`reset`/`retriable-status-codes`) + `num_retries` + `retriable_status_codes` + the 3-stat subset (`upstream_rq_retry{,_success,_limit_exceeded}`) + the per-attempt `upstream_rq_total`/`upstream_rq_5xx` counting reconciliation (§6.2-CRITICAL) + `x-envoy-attempt-count` + a default back-off + fixture 0024 (success + limit-exceeded). DEFER: `per_try_timeout`, custom `retry_back_off` intervals, retry budgets (`retry_budget` + `upstream_rq_retry_overflow`), `retry_priority`/`retry_host_predicate`, `x-envoy-retry-on`/`x-envoy-max-retries` overrides, vhost-level policy, `retriable_headers`, gRPC retry, and hedging.

**§6.1 split projection — single phase, but genuinely close.** SPEC-time estimate ~12–16 tasks / ~1300–1600 LoC (production ~470, tests ~600, fixture/harness/backstop ~510, docs ~120) — NEAR the §6.1 ~1500-LoC / ~25-task gate. **Projected single un-split phase, with the split valve held in reserve:** the state-2 PLAN-write re-evaluates against the §6.2-refined estimate and splits into `16.1` (config + validator + H1 retry loop + stats foundation + back-off + fixture-0024 success path) / `16.2` (H2 retry loop + per-attempt counter reconciliation + limit-exceeded coverage + parent close) + **ADR-0046** if it lands over ~1500. The §6.2 reconciliation ADR is reserved as **ADR-0045** (PLAUSIBLE — finding 4, the per-attempt `upstream_rq_total`/`5xx` counting, is the most likely trigger).

**ADR posture.** **ADR-0044 landed at THIS brainstorm commit** (the scoping ADR — the body-replay finding + the minimum-viable scope boundary; a brainstorm-time-ADR cadence mirroring phase-15's ADR-0042, justified by the non-obvious feasibility finding). DECISIONS.md ledger head advances **ADR-0043 → ADR-0044** (count 45; next available **ADR-0045**). **ADR-0028** (H1-listener × H2-cluster dispatch deferral) REMAINS OPEN — phase 16 does not engage it.
