### Phase-30 state-1 brainstorm (pick + scope; the subset-LB / maximal-reuse rationale)

> Authored at the phase-30 state-1 brainstorm (`superpowers:brainstorming`). Records WHY phase 30 is `subset LB` + the alternatives weighed; the full reasoning is **ADR-0073**. (Relocates to `STATE_HISTORY.md` per ADR-0035 / §4.1 inv. 9 at the phase-30 state-6 close-out, when row `30` flips `done`.)

- **The pick continues the Load-balancing family with `subset LB`** — the next DETERMINISTIC, byte-exact-differentiable, LOCALLY-observable LB step after the two consistent-hash policies (RING_HASH 28 + MAGLEV 29). Among the remaining LB family, subset LB is the ONLY policy that needs neither a contract-relaxation ADR nor active-HC health state to be differentially exercised: a route `metadata_match` selects a FIXED metadata-matched endpoint subset (deterministic). `least_request`/`random` are non-deterministic (P2C-random / random host → need a contract-relaxation ADR); `priority`/`panic-thresholds`/`locality-weighted` LB cannot be EXERCISED differentially without active-HC/outlier health state or weighted-random — all deferred.
- **subset LB is NOT a `LbPolicy` value** — it is an ORTHOGONAL layer: BEFORE the cluster's existing `lb_policy` picks, it narrows the candidate endpoints to those whose `envoy.lb` metadata is a SUPERSET of the matched route's `metadata_match`, then runs the inner `lb_policy` (MVP ROUND_ROBIN) within the subset. A cluster with no `lb_subset_config` ignores the narrowing → the no-op regression proof (all 37 existing fixtures stay green, round-robin AND RING_HASH/MAGLEV paths).
- **Maximal reuse:** the two-distinguishable-backend `--body-marker` fixture harness (fixtures 0036/0037 + `discover_host_lan_ip`/`{{BACKEND_IP}}`), the `*LbConfig` config pattern, the `pick()`/`pick_endpoint()` threading template (phase-28's `Option<u64>` hash key → the route `metadata_match`), and the no-host 503 path (for NO_FALLBACK) ALL already exist. New surface = endpoint `metadata` + `lb_subset_config` + route `metadata_match` + the `subset.rs` engine + the 3 fallback dispositions.
- **Rejected (ADR-0073):** least_request/random (non-deterministic — a contract-relaxation phase); priority/panic-thresholds/locality-weighted LB (need HC/outlier — post-upstream-robustness); the deferred xDS CDS/LDS hot-reload arc (heavy, split-prone, CI-only differential); other §9 families (network-filters low-leverage; heavier HTTP filters needing external services; gRPC still ADR-0014/H2-trailers-blocked).
- **MVP scope (ADR-0073 / SPEC §2):** endpoint `metadata` (envoy.lb) + `lb_subset_config` (subset_selectors[keys], fallback_policy [NO_FALLBACK/ANY_ENDPOINT/DEFAULT_SUBSET], default_subset) + route `metadata_match` + `subset.rs` (subset index + superset-match) + the `metadata_match`→`pick()` threading + the 3 fallback dispositions + fixture 0038 (two metadata'd backends [stage: prod/canary] + metadata_match routes + a fallback probe) + backstop + a `parse_bootstrap` fuzz seed + a BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT subset row. **Deferred non-goals:** least_request/random; priority/panic/locality-weighted; subset+consistent-hash-inner-LB; multiple overlapping selectors / per-selector fallback / single_host_per_subset / list_as_any / metadata_fallback_policy / scale_locality_weight; subset+EDS-hot-reload; subset+HC/OD differential; CDS/LDS hot-reload.
- **The core differential risk** (envoy-rust must replicate Envoy's EXACT subset selection + fallback to select the SAME backend) is de-risked by the **state-2 §6.2 LOCAL reconnaissance** (record metadata_match→backend mappings + the fallback dispositions + the wire shape against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`). **ADR-0074 reserved** (§6.2 reconciliation), **ADR-0075 reserved** (§6.1 split — projected NOT to fire but the closest call since phase 22; ~1100–1500 LoC / ~12–15 tasks; seam 30.1 config+engine / 30.2 pick-threading+fallback+fixture+close). The SPEC was spec-reviewed → APPROVED (0C/1I/4 Minor; ALL folded — the I-1 single_host_per_subset terminology collision + 3 Minors).
- **M29-1/M29-2** (the shared `Http1HashSweep` differential driver's RING_HASH-worded `bail!` diagnostics) are weighed at this phase — SPEC §2.1.9 folds them into policy-agnostic wording IF fixture 0038 reuses/extends that shared driver; else they carry forward.

### Phase-30 state-2 PLAN-write (the §6.2-locked subset algorithm + the 9-task plan)

> Authored at the phase-30 state-2 PLAN-write (`superpowers:writing-plans`). Records the §6.2 reconnaissance result + the PLAN shape; the full algorithm lock is **ADR-0074** and `PLAN.md §A`. (Relocates to `STATE_HISTORY.md` per ADR-0035 / §4.1 inv. 9 at the phase-30 state-6 close-out, when row `30` flips `done`.)

- **The §6.2 reconnaissance CRACKED Envoy's subset-LB semantics** (run LOCALLY against live `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` in Docker with two distinguishable marker backends + routes with `metadata_match`; delegated to a read-only subagent to preserve context budget). Every fact was OBSERVED via curl → the **STRONG** differential target FIRES (cross-proxy byte-identical selection).
- **The locked semantics (`subset.rs` reproduces them; ADR-0074 / `PLAN.md §A`):** SUPERSET match (an endpoint is a candidate iff its `envoy.lb` metadata is a SUPERSET of the route `metadata_match`); the `subset_selectors` entry USED is the one whose `keys` SET EQUALS the `metadata_match` keys; build groups endpoints per selector by the value-tuple of its keys (an endpoint MISSING a selector key is EXCLUDED); lookup = the value-tuple → the subset, inner `lb_policy` (ROUND_ROBIN) within it; fallback — NO_FALLBACK no-match → `503 no healthy upstream`, ANY_ENDPOINT → round-robin all, DEFAULT_SUBSET → the `default_subset` subset.
- **TWO SPEC-projection corrections (ADR-0074):** (1) subset-config validation is NOT startup-fatal — Envoy BOOTS for empty `subset_selectors`/`keys`, an uncovered `default_subset`, and DEFAULT_SUBSET-without-default (consequences are request-time) → envoy-rust ACCEPTS all (NO fatal validator), per ADR-0049 fatal-only-where-Envoy-rejects; (2) `lb_subsets_active`/`created` read an opaque **66** (non-portable) → emit NO subset LB stat (the phase-21/24/28/29 discipline; the fixture ignore-lists `lb_subsets_*`).
- **PLAN = 9 tasks / ~900–1100 LoC** (1 LbMetadata+endpoint metadata / 2 `lb_subset_config` [accept-all] / 3 route `metadata_match` / 4 `subset.rs` [the §A oracle — the correctness gate] / 5 `pick()` subset narrowing [eligible-set; no-`lb_subset_config` no-op preserves all 37 fixtures] / 6 HCM threading [the phase-28 `request_hash_key` template] / 7 fixture `0038-lb-subset` [STRONG; a NEW route-selection driver, NOT the hash-sweep; `/nope`→503 NO_FALLBACK probe] / 8 backstop / 9 fuzz seed + BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT subset row). Plan-reviewed by a fresh subagent → APPROVED (0 Critical / 3 Important / 4 Minor); the 3 Important FOLDED — the slow-path/HC-OD subset composition (intersect `idxs` with the eligibility loop or `debug_assert!` no-HC), the StrictDns endpoint-fan-out metadata alignment (collect metadata in the same nested loop as `endpoints`), and the missing-selector-key exclusion rule (+ a T8 backstop).
- **§6.1 split did NOT fire — ADR-0075 reserved + UNFIRED** (~9 tasks, lighter than the SPEC upper-edge ~12–15-task projection since the validation task collapsed [non-fatal] and there is no stat task). **M29-1/M29-2 do NOT fold here** (fixture 0038 uses a non-hash-sweep driver) → they carry forward.

### Phase-31 state-1 brainstorm (pick + scope; the cdn_loop / cleanest-self-contained-differential rationale)

> Authored at the phase-31 state-1 brainstorm (`superpowers:brainstorming`). Records WHY phase 31 is `cdn_loop` + the alternatives weighed; the full reasoning is **ADR-0076**. (Relocates to `STATE_HISTORY.md` per ADR-0035 / §4.1 inv. 9 at the phase-31 state-6 close-out, when row `31` flips `done`.)

- **The pick continues the HTTP-filters family with `cdn_loop`** — the next DETERMINISTIC, byte-exact-differentiable, LOCALLY-observable, maximal-reuse filter. The Load-balancing family's three deterministic policies (RING_HASH 28 + MAGLEV 29 + subset 30) are done; its remaining policies need a contract-relaxation ADR (`least_request`/`random`) or active-HC health state (`priority`/`panic`/`locality-weighted`). The HTTP-filters family is the project's most-developed surface (the H1/H2 pipeline, the 23.x per-route `typed_per_filter_config`, the `StopAndSend` synth helpers, 8 shipped filters), so a new deterministic filter is the lowest-risk maximal-reuse step.
- **cdn_loop is the cleanest fully-SELF-CONTAINED byte-exact differential** among the remaining deterministic filters — a decode-side, header-only RFC 8586 `CDN-Loop` filter: parse the inbound header → count this CDN's `cdn_id` → reject a loop (`count > max_allowed_occurrences`, default 0; projected 502) / reject a malformed header (projected 400) / else append `cdn_id` and forward. Every output (the appended `cdn_id`, the reject body) is static config or a fixed string → cross-proxy byte-identical, with NONE of the per-side host-address dependence that weakened the 28/29 endpoint-strings or the rejected `stateful_session` cookie. LOCALLY observable (no reload trigger).
- **Maximal reuse:** the entire H1/H2 filter pipeline + the decode-side `Decision::StopAndSend` + the H1/phase-11-H2 filter-synth local-reply decorators + the request-header-append path (`header_mutation`) + the `@type`-tagged HTTP-filter config enum + the deterministic HTTP-filter fixture harness (0031/0032/0033 + the echo `--body-marker` backend) ALL already exist. New surface = `CdnLoopConfig` + the RFC 8586 `CDN-Loop` parser + the `CdnLoopFilter` variant + fixture 0039. NO new pipeline machinery.
- **Rejected (ADR-0076):** `header_to_metadata` (internal dynamic-metadata output → needs a cross-cutting `%DYNAMIC_METADATA%` access-log operator [the existing `envoy-accesslog` formatter has none] to be observable — a deferred coupling); `set_metadata` (same, worse — no header input); `stateful_session` (cookie encodes the per-side host address → non-byte-exact); `compressor`/`decompressor` (byte-identical-gzip risk); the remaining LB policies (non-deterministic / HC-dependent); the Observability access-log-operators phase (a viable higher-value family-opener, but moderate differential risk from excluding timing operators — a STRONG future pick, deferred); the network-filters opener (low-leverage); `grpc_*`/`ext_authz`/`ext_proc`/`lua`/`wasm`/`oauth2` (gRPC-blocked or external).
- **MVP scope (ADR-0076 / SPEC §2):** `CdnLoopConfig { cdn_id, max_allowed_occurrences = 0 }` + the `@type`-tagged enum variant + a `cdn_id` validator + the RFC 8586 `CDN-Loop` parser (the correctness gate) + the `CdnLoopFilter` decode-side count/append/reject + fixture `0039-http-filter-cdn-loop` (4 probes: no-header→append / self-`cdn_id`→loop-reject / foreign-id→append-after / malformed→parse-reject) + an in-process backstop + a `parse_bootstrap` fuzz seed (+ a dedicated parser fuzz target if §3 decides) + a BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT cdn_loop subsection. **Deferred non-goals:** per-route `typed_per_filter_config` for cdn_loop (additive later); RFC 8586 `cdn-info` parameter semantics beyond counting; other deterministic filters (header_to_metadata/set_metadata/stateful_session/compressor); gRPC/external filters. Load-bearing invariant: all 38 existing fixtures `0001`–`0038` stay green (the filter is INERT when not in the chain).
- **The core differential risk** (envoy-rust must replicate Envoy's EXACT reject status/body + `CDN-Loop` append formatting) is de-risked by the **state-2 §6.2 LOCAL reconnaissance** (record the four probe outcomes + the parser strictness + the config-validity disposition against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`). **ADR-0077 reserved** (§6.2 reconciliation), **ADR-0078 reserved** (§6.1 split — projected NOT to fire; ~600–900 LoC / ~6–8 tasks, comparable to csrf/buffer). The SPEC was spec-reviewed → APPROVED (0 issues; the loop→502 / malformed→400 projections independently confirmed vs Envoy + RFC 8586; 2 advisory notes → the PLAN includes a near-malformed probe).
- **Carry-forwards (NOT consumed this phase):** cdn_loop is an HTTP-filter fixture, NOT an LB hash-sweep, so it does NOT touch the shared `Http1HashSweep` differential driver → **M29-1/M29-2 + M30-1** (the RING_HASH-worded `bail!` diagnostics + the duplicated `extract_marker`) carry forward again; the empty-`metadata_match`→fallback doc-comment + **M30-2** (`lb_policy` serde-default) are unrelated → carry forward.

### Phase-31 state-2 PLAN-write (the §6.2-locked CDN-Loop wire facts + the ~6–8-task plan)

> Authored at the phase-31 state-2 PLAN-write (`superpowers:writing-plans`). Records the §6.2 reconnaissance result + the PLAN shape; the full wire-fact lock is **ADR-0077** and `PLAN.md §A`. (Relocates to `STATE_HISTORY.md` per ADR-0035 / §4.1 inv. 9 at the phase-31 state-6 close-out, when row `31` flips `done`.)

- **The §6.2 reconnaissance CONFIRMED Envoy's cdn_loop behavior** (run LOCALLY against live `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` in Docker — an H1 listener with the `cdn_loop` filter [`cdn_id: mycdn.example`, `max_allowed_occurrences: 0`] + a header-reflecting echo backend; delegated to a read-only subagent to preserve context budget). Every fact was OBSERVED via curl → the **STRONG** differential target FIRES (cross-proxy byte-identical reject/append; cdn_loop is locally observable — a normal request/response, no file-watch/reload trigger).
- **The locked facts (ADR-0077 / `PLAN.md §A`):** loop (`count(cdn_id) > max_allowed_occurrences`) → **502** `The server has detected a loop between CDNs.` (44B, no newline, `cdn_loop_detected`); malformed `CDN-Loop` → **400** `Invalid CDN-Loop header in request.` (35B, no newline, `invalid_cdn_loop_header`); within limit → append `cdn_id` **COMMA-ONLY** (`{existing},{cdn_id}`, or bare `{cdn_id}` if absent). Parser = strict RFC-7230 token `cdn-id` (quoted-string/non-tchar id → 400; bare param without `=value` → 400; empty list entries [`a,,b`, trailing/leading comma] are NOT malformed → append; OWS trimmed); matching is CASE-SENSITIVE and IGNORES parameters; multiple `CDN-Loop` request headers are coalesced before counting. Config validity ALL BOOT-FATAL (empty / comma / invalid-token `cdn_id`, ADR-0049). NO stat. `@type` = `type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.cdn_loop.v3.CdnLoopConfig`.
- **ONE SPEC correction (ADR-0077):** the SPEC §1.3 example wrote the append as `<foreign-id>, <cdn_id>` (comma-SPACE) — WRONG; the wire truth is COMMA-ONLY (`<foreign-id>,<cdn_id>`). No other material divergence — the headline shape (loop→502, malformed→400, append, no stat, all-fatal validity) all matched the SPEC projection; ADR-0077 LOCKS the open §3 calls (the ADR-0070/0072 pattern).
- **PLAN = ~6–8 tasks / ~600–900 LoC** (1 the RFC 8586 `CDN-Loop` parser [`crates/envoy-filter/src/cdn_loop.rs` — the §A oracle, the correctness gate] / 2 `CdnLoopConfig` + the `@type` enum variant + the all-fatal `cdn_id` validator / 3 the `CdnLoopFilter` [9th `HttpFilterInstance` variant] decode count/append/reject [reusing `StopAndSend` + the H1/phase-11-H2 filter-synth decorators] / 4 fixture `0039-http-filter-cdn-loop` [the 0013-header-mutation echo-observation + the 0032-csrf reject shape; 5 probes incl. a near-malformed boundary] / 5 backstop [parser edges + the no-`cdn_loop` no-op witness] / 6 `parse_bootstrap` seed + a dedicated `cdn_loop_parse` fuzz target [the untrusted-request-input parse surface; the jwt_parse §7.4 precedent] / 7 BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT + close). Plan-reviewed by a fresh subagent → APPROVED; two advisories FOLDED into Task 4 — the reject probes both carry driver-forced `connection: close` (value-compared, resolves clean on both sides, the 0032-csrf precedent), and the append observation uses the 0013 sorted-echo-body `byte_exact` mechanism.
- **§6.1 split did NOT fire — ADR-0078 reserved + UNFIRED** (~6–8 tasks, comparable to csrf/buffer; the RFC parser is bounded). **Carry-forwards NOT consumed** (cdn_loop is an HTTP-filter fixture, NOT an LB hash-sweep → it does not touch the `Http1HashSweep` differential driver): the empty-`metadata_match` doc-comment; M29-1/M29-2 + M30-1 (the driver's RING_HASH-worded diagnostics + `extract_marker`); M30-2 (`lb_policy` serde-default) all carry forward.

## Relocated from STATE.md `## Notes` — closed-phase subsections (phase 35)

> Relocated at the phase-35 state-6 close-out (when ROADMAP row `35` flipped `done`) per ADR-0035 / §4.1 inv. 9. The phase-35 state-1..5 Notes subsections below were the active phase's working notes through phases 35's lifecycle; phase 35 is now CLOSED.

### Phase-35 state-1 brainstorm

- **Pick (ADR-0085):** phase `35-rbac-dynamic-metadata` — the FIRST dynamic-metadata CONSUMER. Extend the EXISTING phase-10 `envoy.filters.http.rbac` filter (NO new `HttpFilterInstance` variant) with a string-only `metadata` Permission/Principal condition that reads the phase-33 dynamic-metadata store (written mid-chain by phase-34 `header_to_metadata`). Closes the produce→consume loop the phase-33/34 arc teed up; opens the metadata-consumer vein in the HTTP-filters family.
- **Pivotal feasibility fact (verified at the brainstorm by reading `pipeline.rs` + `rbac.rs`):** the decode pipeline iterates `self.filters.iter_mut()` passing ONE `&mut FilterRequest` to every filter in chain order (`crates/envoy-filter/src/pipeline.rs:77`), so a filter placed AFTER `header_to_metadata` reads the `req.dynamic_metadata` it wrote in the same pass. The fixture chain order `[header_to_metadata, rbac, router]` (producer before consumer) is REQUIRED. `eval_permission`/`eval_principal(p, &FilterRequest)` already receive the metadata-carrying request.
- **Implementation surface (projected):** config — a `Metadata(MetadataMatcher)` variant on the `Permission` + `Principal` enums (the hand-rolled "exactly one map key" `Deserialize` visitors, `crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs`) + a `MetadataMatcher`/`MetadataPathSegment`/`ValueMatcher` struct trio (single-segment path, `string_match`-only, reusing the 04.x `StringMatcher`, `deny_unknown_fields`); runtime — `RuntimePermission::Metadata`/`RuntimePrincipal::Metadata` + eval arms reading `req.dynamic_metadata.get(filter)?.get(path[0].key)` + the existing `lower_*` arms (`crates/envoy-filter/src/rbac.rs`); the RBAC decision matrix + `403`+`RBAC: access denied` local reply UNCHANGED. Fixture `0043` + an in-process backstop + a `parse_bootstrap` seed + a BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT extension.
- **Scope (ADR-0085 minimum-viable):** single-segment path + `string_match`-only `ValueMatcher`. DEFERS: non-string `ValueMatcher` variants (null/double/bool/present/list/or_match — `present_match` the cheapest follow-up); multi-segment/nested path; `MetadataMatcher.invert`; the other RBAC condition types (IP/port/url_path/SNI); `shadow_rules`; per-route `typed_per_filter_config`; other producers/consumers (jwt_authn `payload_in_metadata`, ext_authz/ext_proc [gRPC-blocked]); `json_format`/gRPC-ALS/OTLP/tracing/stats-sink/tap.
- **State-2 (next session, `superpowers:writing-plans`):** run the §6.2 LOCAL reconnaissance against live `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (the `MetadataMatcher`/`ValueMatcher` wire shape, the `filter`→namespace correspondence, the present/absent match semantics, the StringMatcher modes, the config-validity disposition; confirm the 200/403 verdict byte-exact), fire **ADR-0086**, author `PLAN.md` with the facts inline. §6.1 split projected NOT to fire (~500–900 LoC / ~7–9 tasks).
- **Spec-review:** the SPEC was spec-reviewed by a fresh subagent at this state-1 close — disposition folded (see the brainstorm commit).

### Phase-35 state-2 PLAN-write

- **§6.2 reconnaissance (run LOCALLY this session against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`, the ENVOY_TARGET pin):** stood up an H1 `direct_response` listener + a `[header_to_metadata, rbac, router]` chain with an `action: ALLOW` single-policy `metadata` Permission `{ filter: envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata, path: [{ key: tier }], value: { string_match: { exact: prod } } }`; drove `curl` probes; captured bytes with `od -c`; round-tripped via `/config_dump`; tested the Principal placement, a custom `metadata_namespace`, a reversed `[rbac, header_to_metadata]` chain, and a `prefix` matcher with live probes; tested malformed variants (empty/missing `filter`, empty `path: []`, multi-segment `path`, `present_match` value, missing `value`) via `--mode validate`. All containers torn down.
- **§6.2 RESULT (locked by ADR-0086) — STRONG differential FIRES.** CONFIRMED: the `metadata: { filter, path: [{ key }], value: { string_match } }` wire shape round-trips verbatim; accepted under BOTH `permissions`/`principals`; `filter`→namespace correspondence holds (default `envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata` per ADR-0084 + a custom `my.custom.ns` both matchable); **producer-before-consumer chain order REQUIRED** (reversed `[rbac, header_to_metadata]` → `X-Tier: prod` gets 403); the full 04.x `StringMatcher` modes flow through (`exact` + `prefix` confirmed live); `X-Tier: prod`→`200`+`ok\n`(3B) / `dev`/absent/present-empty→`403`+`RBAC: access denied`(19B, `od -c`) byte-exact; empty `filter` / empty `path: []` / missing `value` boot-fatal (Envoy PGV; ADR-0049).
- **THREE MATERIAL divergences (ADR-0086 FIRES):** (i) `rbac.v3.Permission.metadata` AND `Principal.metadata` are DEPRECATED in v1.33.0 (boot `warning`, "will be removed from Envoy soon") but FULLY FUNCTIONAL at the pin — the warning is stderr-only → **NON-DIFFERENTIAL** (envoy-rust does not emit it; flag for the future pin-refresh phase D-3.7); (ii) a MULTI-SEGMENT `path` is ACCEPTED by Envoy (SPEC projected boot-fatal) → the flat string-only store can't resolve it, so envoy-rust MVP is STRICTER: `path.len() != 1` boot-fatal (`ConfigError::RbacMetadataMatcherInvalid`); (iii) a NON-`string_match` `value` (e.g. `present_match`) is ACCEPTED by Envoy → the string-only `ValueMatcher` rejects it boot-fatal via its hand-rolled "exactly one key" visitor. All three are documented stricter-than-Envoy / non-differential (the phase-34 `cookie`/typed-values precedents); none affects fixture 0043 (which exercises only the in-scope single-segment `string_match` surface).

**(R-0.6)** `--mode validate` proves ALL FOUR network filters envoy-rust supports (`echo`, `tcp_proxy`, `http_connection_manager`, `direct_response`) are **TERMINAL** upstream (`terminal filter named <X> … must be the last filter in a network filter chain`), while envoy-rust validates **none** of them — `crates/envoy-bin/src/main.rs:214-218` reads only `filter_chains.first().and_then(|c| c.filters.first())`, silently ignoring trailing filters; **The PLAN-write MUST re-confirm SPEC §3's PLAN-VERIFY items V-1 … V-8 fresh against the live tree** (line-number drift is routine). Two deserve special attention:
- **V-3 — the load-bearing implementation risk: the unread-data RST hazard.** On Linux, closing a socket with unread bytes in its receive queue sends an RST, which can destroy a payload the peer has not yet read. Upstream Envoy closes with `FlushWrite` and the state-0 `client-sends-first` probe saw a clean EOF with a complete payload; envoy-rust's naive `write_all(payload).await; shutdown().await; drop(stream)` may RST where Envoy does not. **Settle this EMPIRICALLY — do not assume the naive path works** — and pin the outcome with a test that writes client bytes BEFORE reading. If it forces a behavior-contract amendment, **ADR-0124** fires.
- **V-2** — `crates/envoy-config/src/error.rs` does **NOT** exist; locate the real `ConfigError` definition site before planning the new `NetworkFilterNotTerminal` variant.

**§6.1 split gate:** projected **NOT to fire** (~650 net LoC / ~9 tasks vs. the ~1500 LoC / ~25 task thresholds). If it does fire, **ADR-0124** fires with it.

### `## Notes` — `### Phase-66 state-0/1 brainstorm (active phase)` (superseded in place by the state-2 PLAN-write)

### Phase-66 state-0/1 brainstorm (active phase)

- **The pick.** Phase 66 opens the **Network filters family**, which had ZERO ROADMAP rows despite being a `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §9 family heading since phase 00. Its first member is `envoy.filters.network.direct_response`. The phase also closes a live-witnessed config-validation parity gap (network-filter terminal validation) and adds the differential harness's first read-to-EOF raw-TCP driver.
- **Why this, not a heavier pivot.** xDS CDS hot-reload was the strongest alternative and was REJECTED for a single phase: the phase-26/27 watcher core (`crates/envoy-cluster/src/xds_watch.rs`, `XdsFileWatcher`) IS generic and reusable, but `ClusterManager { clusters: HashMap<String, Arc<Cluster>> }` (`crates/envoy-cluster/src/cluster.rs:908-910`) is a plain immutable map — NOT behind `ArcSwap`/`RwLock` — shared as `Arc<ClusterManager>` to the pool managers, health-check scheduler, and outlier manager. Unlike EDS (which swaps a `RwLock<Arc<Vec<SocketAddr>>>` INSIDE an existing cluster, `cluster.rs:131`), CDS has no map-level swap primitive; the real cost is cluster-lifecycle churn (pool spawn/teardown, health-check probe-task lifecycle, outlier-sweeper lifecycle, in-flight-request safety on a removed cluster) at ~800-1200 LoC with a near-certain §6.1 split. **It loses nothing by waiting** and remains a strong pick for a later multi-sub-phase arc.
- **Why not the cheap leaves.** M64-2 / M57-1 / M53-2 / M64-3 are cosmetic or doc-only and light up **no differential surface**. Phases 53/54/64/65 each added a real cross-proxy witness; a phase whose entire content is doc polish breaks that pattern. None of them touches this phase's surface, so folding them in would be scope creep — they stay LIVE.
- **The empirical target was proven BEFORE the spec was written** (D-3.3: the contract is what Envoy does, not what we remember). Live-Envoy probes against the pinned image established that `direct_response` writes its payload immediately on connect, is byte-identical across connections, ignores client input entirely, is insensitive to client read timing, and closes with a **clean EOF, no RST**. Separately, `--mode validate` established that `direct_response`, `echo`, `tcp_proxy`, AND `http_connection_manager` are ALL terminal upstream. Full evidence: `SPEC.md` §0, R-0.1 … R-0.11.
- **The one real risk is V-3, the unread-data RST hazard.** On Linux, closing a socket with unread bytes in its receive queue sends an RST that can destroy a payload the peer has not yet read. Envoy closes with `FlushWrite` and survives the client-sends-first probe; envoy-rust's naive `write_all` → `shutdown` → `drop` may NOT. **The state-2 PLAN must settle this empirically and pin it with a test that writes client bytes before reading. Do not assume the naive path works.**
- **Do NOT "fix" the `echo` `typed_config` asymmetry.** Upstream Envoy REQUIRES `typed_config` on `envoy.filters.network.echo`; envoy-rust forbids it (`UnexpectedTypedConfig`). Fixture `0001`'s two sides differ accordingly — that is the pre-existing ADR-0014 YAML shim, not a bug. `direct_response` introduces no such asymmetry: both sides of fixture `0071` are identical.
- **`crates/envoy-config/src/error.rs` does not exist.** Locate the real `ConfigError` definition site before planning the new `NetworkFilterNotTerminal` variant (PLAN-VERIFY V-2).

**The PLAN is authoritative and complete — do not re-derive it.** 9 TDD tasks: (1) `envoy-config` schema (`DIRECT_RESPONSE_FILTER` const + `TypedConfig::DirectResponse` + `DirectResponseConfig`); (2) the `validate()` arm; (3) network-filter **terminal validation** (`is_terminal_network_filter` + `ConfigError::NetworkFilterNotTerminal` + an immutable pre-pass BEFORE the existing mutating filter loop); (4) `crates/envoy-bin/src/direct_response.rs` (write → flush → FIN → **drain**); (5) the `main.rs` dispatch arm + in-process backstop; (6) `Driver::TcpDirectResponse` + `drive_tcp_direct_response`; (7) fixture `0071` + the differential test; (8) the fuzz corpus seed; (9) `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md`.

**Three things the implementation MUST NOT get wrong:**
- **The drain is load-bearing (ADR-0124).** `direct_response_once` must `write_all` → `flush` → `shutdown()` (FIN) → **read-and-discard until EOF** → drop. - **`crate::parse_bootstrap` parses AND validates** (`crates/envoy-config/src/lib.rs:769-782`). There is no `load_bootstrap_from_str`, and `crates/envoy-config/src/error.rs` does not exist (`ConfigError` is at `lib.rs:60`). Task-1's schema tests therefore use `serde_yaml::from_str::<Bootstrap>`; Tasks 2-3 use `parse_bootstrap`.
- **`cargo build -p envoy-bin` before ANY local differential run** (memory `differential-harness-uses-debug-envoy-bin`) — the harness executes `target/debug/envoy-bin`, and this phase adds a new config key AND a new filter name, so a stale binary REDs with `unsupported network filter` / `unknown field`.

### Phase-66 state-2 PLAN-write (active phase)

- **`PLAN.md` is authoritative and complete.** 9 TDD tasks, ~700 net LoC, exact file paths + complete code + exact commands + expected output in every step. The state-3 implementer should execute it, not re-derive it.
- **The drain is the phase's one real subtlety (ADR-0124).** `direct_response_once` must `write_all` → `flush` → `shutdown()` [FIN] → **read-and-discard until EOF** → drop. The naive `write_all` → `shutdown` → `drop` RSTs a client that upstream Envoy does not RST. This was measured, not reasoned: Envoy accepts a post-EOF client write at 0 / 21 / 200 000 unread bytes; the naive path raises `BrokenPipeError` **even at ZERO unread bytes**. Fixture `0071` CANNOT catch this (its driver never writes after EOF) — which is exactly why PLAN Task 4 Step 5 is a mandatory mutation check.
- **Two entry-point facts that a plausible-looking plan got wrong.** `crate::parse_bootstrap` **parses AND validates** (`crates/envoy-config/src/lib.rs:769-782`) — there is no `load_bootstrap_from_str`; and `crates/envoy-config/src/error.rs` does **not** exist (`ConfigError` lives at `lib.rs:60`). Task-1's schema tests consequently use `serde_yaml::from_str::<Bootstrap>` (7 existing call sites establish the convention); Tasks 2-3 use `parse_bootstrap`.
- **Terminal validation is an immutable PRE-PASS**, placed before the existing `for filter in &mut chain.filters` loop (which borrows mutably — the HCM arm calls `as_mut()`). That ordering also reproduces upstream Envoy's error precedence: a chain of `[direct_response, echo]` reports the TERMINAL error even when the trailing filter is itself malformed.
- **Do NOT "fix" the `echo` `typed_config` asymmetry** (upstream requires it; envoy-rust forbids it — the pre-existing ADR-0014 YAML shim behind fixture `0001`'s two-sided divergence). `direct_response` needs no shim: both sides of fixture `0071` are identical.
- **§7.4 gate (d) is satisfied by the pre-existing `parse_bootstrap` fuzz target** — `direct_response` parses nothing. No new target; a corpus seed lands instead, and it needs an explicit `!`-un-ignore line or it is silently untracked.

**BLOCK-66-1 is CLEARED — root-caused, fixed, and CI-confirmed green on attempt 1 (run `29025781624`, `b9f8f6e`). See ADR-0126.** The CI log settles it quantitatively: the pre-build reports `Finished dev profile … in 33.63s` immediately before `test upstream_h2_connection_pooling ... ok` — **33.63s of compiling against a 30s readiness budget**, overshooting by ~3.6s and matching the observed 30.35/30.35/30.37s timeouts. That run also exercised the full suite for the first time in four attempts (`envoy-config` `548 passed` + h2spec present; zero `panicked at` lines). The detail: The diagnostics fired on run `29023995517` and printed a **live** child (`exit status: None`) with an **empty** stderr that never opened its port — matching NONE of ADR-0125's three predicted readings, so that triage table was wrong. Root cause, measured: `spawn_backend` ran `cargo run --quiet --manifest-path <helper>`, a **single-package selection** whose resolver-v2 feature unification differs from `cargo build --workspace --all-targets`'s. A recursive-fingerprint diff of the two `--unit-graph` outputs shows **46 of the helper's 116 build units have no counterpart in the workspace build**, and **7 are warmed by no sibling test** (`futures-util`, `tokio-util`, `h2`, `envoy-cluster`, `envoy-http1`, `envoy-http2`, the bin). `.spawn()` returns immediately, so that compile ran **inside** `wait_ready`'s 30s budget — and `--quiet` suppresses `Compiling …` **and** `Blocking waiting for file lock` (both verified empirically), which is exactly why the child looked live, silent and dead. `rust-cache` saves only on success, so once cold it stayed cold: *flaky → permanently deterministic*, and reruns provably could not recover it. **An earlier hypothesis in that same session — "a nested `cargo run` recompiles nothing" — was asserted, not measured, and is REFUTED.** The fix hoists the build out of the readiness budget (bounded `PREBUILD_TIMEOUT = 240s`, loud on failure) and passes `--quiet` nowhere; **the 30s budget and every assertion are unchanged**. **§7.5 gate (e) should now be assessable**; (a)/(c)/(d) already have positive CI/fuzz evidence, (b) is unproven because the suite aborted early. Note `cargo test --workspace` stops at the first failing binary.

### Phase-66 state-3 implementation (active phase)

- **The drain is the phase's one real subtlety, and it is now PINNED (ADR-0124).** `direct_response_once` does `write_all` → `flush` → `shutdown()` [FIN] → **read-and-discard until EOF** → drop. The mandatory PLAN Task-4 Step-5 mutation check was performed: commenting out the drain loop makes `post_eof_client_write_is_accepted_not_reset` fail with `Os {code: 32, kind: BrokenPipe}`. Fixture `0071` CANNOT catch this (its driver never writes after EOF) — the in-process test is the only guard. **Do not remove it; do not re-litigate the drain.**
- **`envoy_config::DirectResponse` already existed** — it is the HCM **route-level** `direct_response` action (phase 04). The phase-66 network-filter type is deliberately `DirectResponseConfig`; `TypedConfig::DirectResponse` is an enum *variant* in a different namespace. `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md`'s new `## Network filters` section opens with a do-not-conflate banner because every other `direct_response` row in that document refers to the route-level action.
- **Terminal validation is an immutable PRE-PASS**, placed before the existing `for filter in &mut chain.filters` loop (which borrows mutably — the HCM arm calls `as_mut()`). That ordering also reproduces upstream Envoy's error precedence: a chain of `[direct_response, echo]` reports the TERMINAL error even when the trailing filter is itself malformed. R-0.8 safety was re-confirmed EMPIRICALLY (envoy-admin, envoy-cluster, tls_sni, xds_file_based_lds, xds_file_based_rds all green).
- **`cargo build -p envoy-bin` before ANY local differential run** (memory `differential-harness-uses-debug-envoy-bin`) — the harness executes `target/debug/envoy-bin`, and this phase adds a NEW config key AND a NEW filter name, so a stale binary REDs with `unsupported network filter` / `unknown field`.
- **§7.5 gate (d) is satisfied by the pre-existing `parse_bootstrap` fuzz target** — `direct_response` parses nothing. No new target; the corpus seed needed an explicit `!`-un-ignore line and was proven tracked with `git ls-files`. The state-4 session must RECORD gate (d) explicitly rather than skip it silently.
- **Do NOT "fix" the `echo` `typed_config` asymmetry** (upstream requires it; envoy-rust forbids it — the pre-existing ADR-0014 YAML shim behind fixture `0001`'s two-sided divergence). `direct_response` needs no shim: both sides of fixture `0071` are identical.

- **One reviewer filed the `JoinSet`-non-reaping finding as Important. It was DOWNGRADED to Minor (M66-3) with reasons recorded, not silently softened.** Justification, verified by reading both files in full: `direct_response::serve` (`direct_response.rs:36-74`) is **structurally identical** to `echo::serve` (`echo.rs:21-59`) — neither reaps completed tasks during normal operation, and neither bounds the per-connection read. It is therefore a property of the **pinned structural model**, not code phase 66 authored; it has **zero differential observable**; and repairing `direct_response.rs` alone would break the "echo is the model" invariant that ADR-0123 §2.1(B)(6) rests on. **Repair both files together**, in the phase that next touches the network-filter data plane (natural home: CF-66-2).
- **The terminal pre-pass is COMPLETE, including the path nobody had checked.** The listener loop chains static AND dynamic listeners (`bootstrap.rs:2967-2969`), and `load_dynamic_resources` (`lib.rs:844`) re-invokes `bootstrap::validate` (`lib.rs:1053`) — so **LDS/xDS-loaded listeners get the terminal check too**; a chain cannot escape it. This is the phase's most load-bearing property and it currently rests on **manual tracing, not a test** (carry-forward **M66-6**).
- **Fixture `0071` is a NON-VACUOUS witness.** `assert_body_rule`'s `ByteExact` is a bare `if envoy_body != rust_body { bail! }`, so an empty-vs-empty compare WOULD pass vacuously — but the fixture configures a **non-empty 39-byte payload** that the authoritative upstream reference deterministically emits, so any regression that drops, truncates or mutates it is caught.
- **M66-2 is CONFIRMED and SHARPENED** (a carry-forward description update, NOT an amendment to the append-only ADR-0126, which it confirms): all four latent siblings — `upstream_connection_pooling.rs`, `upstream_active_health_check.rs`, `upstream_outlier_detection.rs`, `tests/differential/src/backend.rs` — not only nest a `cargo run --manifest-path`, they **also still pass `--quiet` under the same 30s readiness budget**. `--quiet`, not the stdio posture, is the silencing factor in every case. A single mechanical sweep (hoist the build out of the budget; drop `--quiet`) neutralizes the class.
- **M66-5 records envoy-rust's behavior on two config edges and DELIBERATELY DECLINES to assert Envoy's** (D-3.3: the contract is what Envoy *does*, and neither edge was probed): an empty network `filters: []` chain **is accepted** (the only `filters.is_empty()` guard, `bootstrap.rs:3618`, is `validate_http_filters` — HTTP filters INSIDE HCM, not network chains), and `response: {}` is rejected with `missing field inline_string`. A future phase should probe the pinned image with `--mode validate` before matching or recording a divergence.
- **Numbering: M66-1 was never allocated** — ADR-0126 opened `M66-2` directly. The new REVIEW.md Minors start at **M66-3**. The ledger advances monotonically and does not backfill lapsed numbers. Do not "fix" the gap.
- **The drain is PINNED (ADR-0124) and CI-green. Do not re-litigate it.** `direct_response_once` does `write_all` → `flush` → `shutdown()` [FIN] → **read-and-discard until EOF** → drop. Commenting out the drain loop makes `post_eof_client_write_is_accepted_not_reset` fail with `Os {code: 32, kind: BrokenPipe}`. Fixture `0071` CANNOT catch this (its driver never writes after EOF) — the in-process test is the only guard. **Do not remove it.**
- **`envoy_config::DirectResponse` already existed** — it is the HCM **route-level** `direct_response` action (phase 04). The phase-66 network-filter type is deliberately `DirectResponseConfig`; `TypedConfig::DirectResponse` is an enum *variant* in a different namespace. `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md`'s `## Network filters` section (`:229`) opens with a do-not-conflate banner.
- **`cargo build -p envoy-bin` before ANY local differential run** (memory `differential-harness-uses-debug-envoy-bin`) — the harness executes `target/debug/envoy-bin`.
- **Do NOT "fix" the `echo` `typed_config` asymmetry** (upstream requires it; envoy-rust forbids it — the pre-existing ADR-0014 YAML shim behind fixture `0001`'s two-sided divergence). `direct_response` needs no shim: both sides of fixture `0071` are identical.
- **BLOCK-66-1 is CLEARED (ADR-0126).** Do not re-add `--quiet` to `spawn_backend`, do not remove the pre-build, do not widen the 30s readiness budget. *Log-reading trap:* CI interleaves ANSI escapes between `Compiling` and the crate name — grep the crate name alone.

## Relocated from STATE.md `## Notes` — superseded active-phase subsection (phase 67 state-0/1 brainstorm)

_The `### Phase-67 state-0/1 brainstorm (active phase)` subsection, superseded in place at the phase-67 §6.1-split session by `### Phase-67.1 state-2 PLAN-write — the §6.1 split (active phase)`. Phase 67 is NOT closed — it was SPLIT into `67.1` + `67.2` per ADR-0129, and parent row `67` stays `in-progress` until both sub-phases are `done`. Relocated verbatim per ADR-0035._

### Phase-67 state-0/1 brainstorm (active phase)

- **`rbac` must NOT be added to `is_terminal_network_filter`** (`crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:825`). Its **absence** is what makes it non-terminal — and that predicate's own doc comment names `rbac` as the intended drop-in. Phase 66 wrote it as a per-name predicate rather than a `len <= 1` check precisely so this phase would not have to re-litigate the rule.
- **The bilateral chain-termination rule is NEW and was undiscoverable at phase 66.** Upstream rejects `[rbac]` alone: `non-terminal filter named envoy.filters.network.rbac ... is the last filter in a network filter chain.` Phase 66 enforced only *a terminal filter must be last*; upstream ALSO enforces *a chain must END in a terminal filter*. Phase 66 had no non-terminal filter, so nothing could violate it. Error precedence, probed: a chain breaking **both** rules reports the **terminal-not-last** error.
- **The protocol needs `on_new_connection` ONLY.** Network RBAC decides once per connection, before any downstream byte is read (SPEC R-0.2). Adding an `on_data` hook with no filter to exercise it is the §6.3 anti-pattern; it is deferred as **CF-67-3** to the first payload-parsing network filter (`mongo_proxy`/`zookeeper_proxy`/`kafka_broker`).
- **`rules` omitted ⇒ the filter is INERT.** The connection is allowed and **neither `allowed` nor `denied` increments** (SPEC R-0.13, measured). Do **not** materialise a default `Rules { action: ALLOW, policies: {} }` and tick `allowed` — that is a **stat divergence with no body divergence**, invisible to a body-only fixture.
- **The DENY fixture is vacuity-prone.** `assert_body_rule`'s `ByteExact` is a bare inequality check, so *both proxies returned zero bytes* passes **even if envoy-rust never implemented RBAC**. The `<stat_prefix>.rbac.denied == 1` assertion is what makes fixture `0072` a witness — and **no raw-TCP `Driver` variant carries `expected_stats` today** (only three HTTP ones do). Extending the raw-TCP driver family is an **in-scope hard requirement**, not polish.
- **Fixtures use `any: true` ONLY.** `direct_remote_ip` sees the Docker bridge address (`192.168.65.2` on this host — a documented fragility) and `destination_port` sees a `{{PORT}}` that **differs between the two proxies**. Every IP/port matcher is covered **in-process**, bound to `127.0.0.1`.
- **NAMING HAZARD, the `direct_response` lesson repeating.** `crates/envoy-filter/src/rbac.rs` (1270 lines) is **`envoy.filters.http.rbac`** — a different feature sharing the name. `crates/envoy-filter/` models HTTP filters only and has no network-filter abstraction. `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` must gain a do-not-conflate banner for `rbac` mirroring the `direct_response` one.
- **V-1 is the biggest unknown:** `Principal`/`Permission` are **shared** with the HTTP RBAC filter; adding L4-only arms may break it if it matches exhaustively. **V-2 is the biggest architectural risk:** `echo::serve` and `direct_response::serve` each own an accept loop while `tcp_proxy`/HCM use `ConnectionHandler`. SPEC recommends **hoisting the accept loop out once** — which also turns **M66-3** into a single fix rather than two, preserving the "echo is the structural model" invariant.
- **M66-5 is CLOSED by recon, not by code.** The empty-`filters: []` chain is **accepted by upstream Envoy** (parity — the phase-66 reviewer's intuition that Envoy rejects it was **wrong**), and `response: {}` is rejected by both. This is why the phase-66 review recorded envoy-rust's behavior and **declined to assert Envoy's**: D-3.3 means the contract is what Envoy *does*, measured.
- **The §6.1 split is projected to FIRE** (~1740 LoC). The PLAN-write owns the decision and must re-derive the estimate. **ADR-0129 is RESERVED** for it.

### Phase-67.1 state-2 PLAN-write — the §6.1 split (active phase)

- **The §6.1 split FIRED, and the re-derived estimate is why.** `SPEC.md` §8 projected ~1740 net LoC; the live-tree re-derivation returned **~2130** against a ~1500 threshold. The SPEC explicitly forbade inheriting its own number — re-deriving found what it had missed.
- **The finding the SPEC missed: a THIRD exhaustive match site.** `define_rbac_tree_validator!` (`crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:4087-4148`) is a **single macro instantiated for BOTH `Permission` and `Principal`**. Its shared body matches `Any`/`Header`/`Metadata`/`UrlPath` plus macro-parameterized `$and | $or` / `$not`, exhaustively. The five new L4 arms are **asymmetric** — 3 `Principal`-only, 2 `Permission`-only — so the shared body **cannot name them uniformly**. It needs a variadic extra-leaf parameter, or the two validators must be de-macro'd. `lower_permission` / `lower_principal` (`crates/envoy-filter/src/rbac.rs:262-314`) are the other two sites; **neither carries a `_ =>` catch-all**, so adding arms is a hard compile break — which is the *good* failure mode, and `67.2`'s **X-4** guards against a sibling phase silently adding a catch-all.
- **CF-67-4 MOVED from `67.2` into `67.1`, and this is a correctness decision, not a preference.** `67.1` reuses the existing enums, whose arms include `header`. Upstream Envoy **rejects** `header` matchers in a network `rbac` config (`Found header(name: ":path"…`, measured). Without an L4 leaf allow-list in `67.1`, envoy-rust would accept a config upstream rejects — a **config-load divergence sitting in `main`** for the whole interval between the sub-phases. D-3.3 makes the measured upstream behavior the contract.
- **`67.2` ships no new differential fixture, and that is forced.** The IP arms see the Docker bridge address (`192.168.65.2` on this host) and `destination_port` must match a `{{PORT}}` that **differs between the two proxies** by construction. Not host-deterministic under the harness. Witnessed in-process at `127.0.0.1` with a known port; differential surface is regression-only. Same posture as the phase-`25.1` foundation slice — **recorded in the SPEC and BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT, never silent.**
- **A three-way split was considered and rejected.** The candidate cut — hoisting the accept loop + M66-3 into its own foundation slice — has **no independent observable**: it exists to host the chain pre-hook, and a slice with neither a fixture nor a filter to exercise it is precisely the §6.3 anti-pattern. `67.1` at ~1455 LoC sits under the gate, and §6.1's **mid-execution** valve stays available.
- **`67.1`'s ~1455 LoC is CLOSE to the ~1500 gate.** Its state-2 PLAN-write must re-derive once more, and must remember the mid-execution split valve fires if any single task's sub-steps blow past ~10 items.
- **Both sub-phase directories exist while `67.2`'s row reads `planned`.** §6.2 steps 2-3 mandate creating both directories and both `SPEC.md` files at the split; §6.2 governs over invariant 4.1.3 for splits. The same shape phase `25` took. **Expected state — do NOT invoke `superpowers:systematic-debugging` on it** (§1 Step E).
- **`67.1` is `planned`, not `in-progress`, and that differs from ADR-0064's phase-25 split.** That session *also* landed `25.1`'s `PLAN.md` in the same commit, so STATE pointed at an actively-executing sub-phase. Here §6.2 step 7 mandates an **exit before the PLAN-write**, so `67.1` flips `in-progress` at its own state-2 PLAN-write commit — consistent with invariant 4.1.2's *"only when"* being a **necessary, not sufficient**, condition.
- **Do NOT add `rbac` to `is_terminal_network_filter`** (`bootstrap.rs:825`) — its **absence** is its non-terminality, and the predicate's doc comment names `rbac` as the intended drop-in. **Do NOT add an `on_data` hook** (§6.3; deferred as CF-67-3). **Do NOT materialise a default `Rules`** when `rules` is omitted — the filter is INERT and ticks **neither** counter. **Do NOT let the DENY fixture assert bodies only** — empty-vs-empty passes vacuously; the `rbac.denied == 1` stats assertion is what makes `0072` a witness.

### `## Notes` subsection (superseded — `### Phase-67.1 state-2 PLAN-write (active phase)`)
### Phase-67.1 state-2 PLAN-write (active phase)

- **The §6.1 gate does NOT fire, and the re-derivation is why.** `SPEC.md` §7 projected ~1455 net LoC; the live-tree re-derivation returned **~1442 / 14 tasks** against ~1500 LoC / ~25 tasks. The SPEC forbade inheriting its own number — re-deriving is what found the correction below.
- **The finding that moved it: `envoy_listener::accept_loop` ALREADY REAPS.** Its `select!` carries `Some(done) = join_set.join_next(), if !join_set.is_empty()` (`crates/envoy-listener/src/lib.rs:565`), and `tcp_proxy`/HCM already flow through it via `bind_and_spawn_listener` (`main.rs:854-887`). **M66-3's non-reaping defect lives ONLY in the two standalone loops** (`echo.rs:21-59`, `direct_response.rs:36-74`). So D5's "accept-loop hoist" is **mostly deletion**, not construction: ~170 LoC, not the SPEC's ~280. **M66-3 is consumed by REMOVAL.**
- **`cx_active` cannot witness reaping.** It is decremented *inside* each spawned task, so it reads 0 while a completed `JoinSet` entry still lingers. The M66-3 witness therefore needs `join_set.len()`, published on a `watch<usize>` and exposed as `Listener::pending_tasks()`. A non-reaping loop reads N after N sequential connections; the reaping one reads ≤ 1.
- **envoy-rust PANICS at startup on `filters: []`.** Measured this session: `thread 'main' panicked at crates/envoy-bin/src/main.rs:219:14: validator guarantees ≥1 filter`. The validator does **not** guarantee it — `filters: []` is ACCEPTED (SPEC R-7), and **upstream Envoy accepts the same config and STARTS**. M66-5 closed *config-load* parity; **runtime parity was never checked.** Fixed in `67.1` (the crash is on the very `expect()` D5 deletes). The fix must **not** invent unmeasured behavior: warn + bind no data listener; what upstream does with a *connection* to such a listener is **CF-67-5**.
- **W-1 is a decision, not an accident.** The six shared RBAC `ConfigError` variants render `"HCM listener {listener:?}"` for a filter that has no HCM. The prefix is generalized. **Blast radius was measured, not assumed**: every landed assertion over those six is `matches!`-shaped, never a string comparison (`bootstrap.rs:13092-13188`).
- **Two `NetworkFilter`s.** `envoy_config::NetworkFilter` is a config **struct**; `envoy_listener::NetworkFilter` is the new runtime **trait**. Task 10 uses both. **Always fully qualify.**
- **The DENY fixture is vacuity-prone, and `scrape_admin_stat` returns `Ok(0)` for an unregistered name.** So `rbac_deny.rbac.denied == 1` is the witness; every `value: 0` assertion is a consistency check that passes vacuously on an absent name. The fixture READMEs say which is which.
- **Do NOT add `rbac` to `is_terminal_network_filter`** (`bootstrap.rs:825`) — its **absence** is its non-terminality. **Do NOT add an `on_data` hook** (§6.3; CF-67-3). **Do NOT materialise a default `Rules`** when `rules` is omitted — the filter is INERT and ticks **neither** counter. **Do NOT weaken or delete `post_eof_client_write_is_accepted_not_reset`** (ADR-0124) while restructuring `direct_response.rs`.
- **§6.1's mid-execution valve stays armed** for state-3: it fires if any single task's sub-steps blow past ~10 items. No task in `PLAN.md` exceeds 7 steps as written.

All 14 `PLAN.md` tasks are landed, TDD on every one; the state-4 verification is next.** This session ran `superpowers:executing-plans` (+ `superpowers:test-driven-development` per task, + `superpowers:systematic-debugging` twice). **`envoy.filters.network.rbac` now exists end-to-end:** the config surface + the bilateral chain-termination rule + the CF-67-4 L4 leaf allow-list (`envoy-config`), the network-filter **chain iteration protocol** + `ChainHandler` + `close_with_drain` (`envoy-listener`), the `network_rbac.rs` engine + 4 counters and the reshaped `main.rs` chain dispatch (`envoy-bin`), `Driver::TcpWithStats` (`tests/differential`), fixtures **`0072`** (DENY) + **`0073`** (ALLOW), 10 in-process backstops, and the `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` rows + fuzz corpus seed. **Both new fixtures are GREEN against upstream Envoy `v1.33.0`, and both are PROVEN NON-VACUOUS** (disabling `wrap_in_chain` REDs each). **THE HEADLINE FINDING — `SPEC.md` R-2 WAS WRONG, and fixture `0072` caught it (ADR-0131).** R-2 concluded network RBAC *"decides once per connection, at establishment, before any downstream byte is read"*, and `PLAN.md` promoted that to the hard rule *"do NOT add an `on_data` hook"*. **Every probe in that recon sent a payload first.** Measured this session against the pinned image: a client that **connects and sends nothing** leaves the connection **OPEN** with **no counter ticking**; a client that **half-closes without sending** gets a **clean EOF** and **no counter ticks**; the decision fires **exactly on the FIRST DOWNSTREAM BYTE**, immediately or after an arbitrary delay — upstream Envoy's `ONE_TIME_ON_FIRST_BYTE`. Symmetric for `action: ALLOW`. **envoy-rust now matches**: `ChainHandler` **peeks** (without consuming) for the first byte before running the chain, and skips the chain entirely when the client closes without sending. **The `NetworkFilter` trait shape is UNCHANGED and filters still never see payload, so CF-67-3 remains correctly deferred.** Two further corrections landed with it: fixture `0072`'s probe must **write** before reading to EOF (new `TcpProbeKind::WriteThenReadToEof`), and `Driver::TcpWithStats`'s `expected_stats` are asserted as **post-probe DELTAS**, not absolute values. **ADR-0130 §2's `filters: []` startup panic is FIXED** (reproduced at `0230db2`, then repaired: warn + bind no data listener). **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0131**; next available **ADR-0132** (unreserved).

It was a **stale test binary**: cargo skipped the rebuild, so the *unmutated* code ran. **A mutation check must confirm that cargo recompiled THE CRATE THAT WAS MUTATED** (grep the run for `Compiling <that crate>`) — checking the wrong crate's `Compiling` line produced the false pass twice. A standalone TCP probe independently established the kernel semantics (no-drain ⇒ `EPIPE` even at 0 unread bytes).

### `## Notes` — superseded active-phase subsection (phase 67.1 state-3 implementation, superseded IN PLACE by the state-4 verification)

### Phase-67.1 state-3 implementation (active phase)

- **`SPEC.md` R-2 was wrong, and the fixture found it (ADR-0131).** R-2's clause *"the decision is taken once per connection, at establishment, before any downstream byte is read"* was inferred from probes that **always sent a payload first**. Measured this session against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`: (A) connect + send nothing → connection stays **OPEN**, `denied` stays 0; (B) send one byte → zero bytes, **clean EOF**, `denied` = 1; (C) connect + half-close, no data → **clean EOF**, `denied` stays 0; (D) idle 2 s then one byte → decision then. Symmetric for ALLOW. **The verdict fires on the FIRST DOWNSTREAM BYTE** (`ONE_TIME_ON_FIRST_BYTE`).
- **envoy-rust matches by peeking, not by exposing payload.** `ChainHandler::handle` awaits `TcpStream::peek(&mut [0u8;1])` before invoking any filter; `peek` does not consume, so the terminal handler still receives the whole stream. `Ok(0)` (client closed/half-closed without sending) skips the chain and closes via `close_with_drain`. **The `NetworkFilter` trait shape is UNCHANGED**; filters see only `ConnectionInfo`. **CF-67-3 (payload-visible `on_data`-time iteration + buffering) remains correctly deferred and its scope is unchanged.**
- **A mutation check can report a FALSE PASS from a stale binary.** The ADR-0124 drain mutation initially passed — which would have meant `post_eof_client_write_is_accepted_not_reset` was vacuous. Root-caused with `superpowers:systematic-debugging`: cargo had skipped the rebuild. **Always grep the run for `Compiling <the crate you MUTATED>`** — twice I watched `envoy-bin` while the mutation lived in `envoy-listener`. A standalone TCP probe independently established that no-drain ⇒ `EPIPE`, even at 0 unread bytes.
- **`cx_active` cannot witness reaping**, so the M66-3 witness reads `join_set.len()` via `Listener::pending_tasks_watch()`. Deleting `accept_loop`'s `join_next()` select arm makes it fail with `JoinSet leaked 50 completed tasks`.
- **`expected_stats` on `Driver::TcpWithStats` are post-probe DELTAS.** `run_fixture` opens a readiness `TcpStream::connect` to each proxy's data port before the probe. The witness property survives: `scrape_admin_stat` returns `Ok(0)` for an unregistered name, so an unimplemented filter snapshots 0 and finishes at 0 — a delta of 0, which fails any non-zero expectation.
- **Two pre-existing artifacts had to move, neither weakened.** `rejects_unknown_filter_name` used `envoy.filters.network.rbac` as its example of an *unknown* filter name; it now uses `sni_cluster`, placed **before** a terminal `echo` (every unknown name is non-terminal, so a trailing one would trip the new chain-termination rule first). And `validate_config` in the new backstops captures **stdout and stderr** — envoy-bin's tracing subscriber writes the `ConfigError` line to **stdout**.
- **Exhaustiveness is compiler-enforced, and it was verified.** Adding a `Permission::DestinationPort(_)` arm breaks the build with `error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns` at `validate_l4_permission` and the shared tree validator. **Never add a `_ =>` catch-all** — that break is what forces `67.2` to classify every new arm. `clippy::only_used_in_recursion` is allowed on `permission_matches`/`principal_matches` with a note: `conn` is unread by `67.1`'s arms and read by `67.2`'s.
- **§6.1's mid-execution valve did NOT fire.** No task's sub-steps blew past ~10 items; Task 12's ADR-0131 rework was ~7. **It stays armed for state-4's re-entry into state-3 if `REVIEW.md` finds issues** (§5.2: review feedback re-enters at step 3, not step 4).

**The state-3 re-entry session's REQUIRED items (from `REVIEW.md` §5):**

1. **Fix C-1** (Critical). `envoy_listener::ChainHandler::handle` must not make the TERMINAL `ConnectionHandler` wait for the first downstream byte. The RBAC *verdict* is a first-byte event (**ADR-0131 stands, and is re-confirmed — do NOT revert it**); the terminal filter's establishment-time work is not. Author **ADR-0132** recording the measurement and **explicitly superseding ADR-0130 Decision 2's "uniformly for all four" claim** (append-only; never edit ADR-0130). **Probe upstream before choosing a model, and probe ALL FOUR terminal filters** — that is the lesson of both ADR-0131 and C-1. Note the measured subtlety: with `direct_response` terminal, upstream **never enforces RBAC**, because the terminal filter writes and closes before any `onData`; a fix that merely avoids the hang but denies the connection would still diverge.
2. **Add the missing composition tests (I-5).** At minimum an in-process backstop for **`[rbac, direct_response]`** (cheapest — needs no backend) and one for **`[rbac, tcp_proxy]`** against a server-speaks-first backend. Without them this bug class returns at `67.2`.
3. **Fix I-2.** Generalize `RbacMetadataMatcherInvalid`'s message to `"listener {listener:?}: …"` (a seventh shared scope-neutral variant) and correct the inverted comment at `crates/envoy-config/src/lib.rs:505-514`. **Do NOT** reorder the L4 walk ahead of `validate_rbac_rules` — the current order is what bounds tree depth before the L4 recursion, and that is pinned by `network_rbac_depth_bound_precedes_the_l4_walk`.
4. **Resolve I-3.** Either bound `close_with_drain`'s steady-state drain (upstream's analogue is `delayed_close_timeout`, default 1s) **or** narrow the ledger claim to "M66-3 reaping consumed; steady-state drain bound deferred as CF-67-6". A carry-forward is an acceptable resolution; a silent over-claim is not. **Do NOT weaken or delete `post_eof_client_write_is_accepted_not_reset` or `deny_post_eof_client_write_is_accepted_not_reset`** while doing it — the drain itself is ADR-0124.
5. **Address I-4** (`pending_tasks()` under fan-out: aggregate, or document as per-socket last-writer-wins) and the eight Minors as budget allows.

**Then, and only then, a SEPARATE session runs state-4 again** (`superpowers:verification-before-completion`, full §7.5 (a)-(f)). Per §5.1 the fix session must **not** chain into it — ADR-0127 names 3→4 explicitly as un-chainable.

**§6.1's mid-execution valve is ARMED for the re-entry.** If the C-1 redesign blows any single task past ~10 sub-steps, **split** (§6.2) rather than push through.

### Phase-67.1 state-5 code-review (active phase)

- **The verdict is NOT APPROVED. §7.5 (f) is UNMET, and per §5.2 the phase re-enters at state 3 — implementation + TDD — NOT state 4.** `REVIEW.md` is standalone (D-3.4) and carries the measured evidence tables verbatim, so the fix session need not re-probe.
- **A green (a)-(e) gate proved the code does what its tests ask. It could not prove the tests ask the right questions.** That gap is exactly what state-5 exists to close, and here it found a Critical the gate structurally could not see: **`rbac` is composed with `echo` in every fixture and every backstop and nothing else, anywhere.**
- **C-1: the first-byte gate was applied to the CHAIN, when it belongs to the FILTER's decision.** `ChainHandler::handle` peeks before delegating to the terminal `ConnectionHandler`, so `direct_response` never writes and `tcp_proxy` never connects upstream until the client speaks. Upstream Envoy runs every filter's `onNewConnection` at establishment. **ADR-0131's first-byte finding is CORRECT and is re-confirmed — do not revert it.** What was wrong is the *scope* it was applied to.
- **This is ADR-0131's own mistake, one level up.** ADR-0131 fired because every probe in the R-2 recon happened to send a payload first. C-1 fires because every probe in the ADR-0131 recon happened to use `echo` — the one terminal filter with no establishment-time behavior. **The general lesson: when a measurement generalizes over a population of one, it has not been measured.**
- **Measure before redesigning, and measure ALL FOUR terminals.** The state-3 re-entry must probe upstream, not reason from it. Note the sharpest measured subtlety: with `direct_response` terminal, upstream **never enforces RBAC at all** (the terminal filter writes and closes before any `onData`; all four counters stay `0`, even on `action: DENY`). A fix that merely avoids the hang but still denies the connection would remain divergent.
- **`[direct_response]` alone is correct on both proxies** — `wrap_in_chain` returns `inner` for an empty prefix — so **fixture `0071` is unaffected and nothing landed regressed.** C-1 is a latent divergence in configs no test exercises, not a regression.
- **A reviewer subagent's mitigating hypothesis (upstream RBAC `StopIteration`s from `onNewConnection`, making envoy-rust parity) was MEASURED AND IS FALSE.** Subagent findings were adjudicated, not accepted; the two load-bearing ones were verified first-hand against the pinned image and the live binary. Do the same with this review.
- **ADR-0132 is RESERVED** for the state-3 re-entry's C-1 decision, and must explicitly supersede **ADR-0130 Decision 2**'s falsified "works uniformly for all four terminal filters" claim. Append-only: never edit a landed ADR (D-3.5).
- **§6.1's mid-execution valve is ARMED** for the re-entry: if the C-1 redesign blows any single task past ~10 sub-steps, **split** rather than push through.

(ii) **The data-less-FIN semantic is a PER-TERMINAL property** (half-close propagation), not a chain property — nobody knew this. **WHY THE VALVE FIRED:** `direct_response` is a trivial repair (bypass the chain; exact measured parity). **`tcp_proxy` is not.** `ConnectionHandler::handle(&self, downstream: TcpStream)` **fuses establishment and data into one future that owns the socket** — there is no seam — and `envoy_tcp::TcpProxy::handle::<S>` is **generic over the stream type** (for upstream TLS) and therefore **cannot `peek` at all**; its connect / `cx_total` / bidirectional-copy body must be split. The work reaches `envoy-listener` (trait + `ChainHandler`), `envoy-tcp`, and `envoy-bin` (`TlsAcceptingHandler`, whose pre-handshake chain placement is itself **UNMEASURED**), plus the FIN semantics and their tests — **well past §6.1's "~10 sub-steps" trigger.** **§6.2 step 1: *"Stop. ### Phase-67.1 state-3 re-entry / §6.1 split (active phase)

- **`67.1` is MID-STATE-3.** `REVIEW.md` stays **NOT APPROVED** and is **never edited** — a review is superseded only by a LATER review (D-3.5). §7.5 (f) remains the only unmet gate.
- **The recon C-1 demanded was performed on ALL FOUR terminals, and it paid for itself twice.** Beyond confirming C-1, it established two facts nobody had: **`echo`/`hcm` are already exactly correct** (so `ADR-0131` stands, re-confirmed, and fixtures `0072`/`0073` are valid witnesses), and the **data-less-FIN semantic is a PER-TERMINAL property** (it evaluates for `tcp_proxy`, not for `echo`/`hcm`), not a chain property.
- **Scrape stats MID-FLIGHT, not after the client closes.** The state-5 review's `tcp_proxy` `allowed: 1` reading was taken after a client close and could not distinguish *first byte* from *FIN* as the trigger. Holding the connection open and scraping while it lives separated them — and revealed the FIN asymmetry. **A counter read after the connection ends cannot tell you when it ticked.**
- **§6.1's MID-EXECUTION VALVE FIRED, and §6.2 says the response is "Stop", not "push through".** `direct_response` is a one-line repair; **`tcp_proxy` is an architecture change**: `ConnectionHandler::handle` fuses establishment and data into one socket-owning future, and `envoy_tcp::TcpProxy::handle::<S>` is **generic over the stream type** (for upstream TLS) and therefore cannot `peek` at all. Carved into **`67.3`**, with its own SPEC and ROADMAP row.
- **The interim posture is a LOUD REJECTION, not a stub.** `[rbac, tcp_proxy]` is rejected at config load until `67.3` lands (`ADR-0049` fail-loud). Upstream accepts that config, so this IS a divergence — but the alternative is the shipped **runtime deadlock**, and §6.3's anti-pattern is a silent stub, not an honest refusal with a named owner.
- **`ADR-0132` supersedes `ADR-0130` Decision 2, and RE-CONFIRMS `ADR-0131`.** Do not revert the first-byte finding: the RBAC *verdict* really is a first-byte event. Only the *scope* it was applied to was wrong.
- **`M66-3` is PARTIALLY consumed** (reaping half only). The unbounded steady-state `close_with_drain` drain is now **`CF-67-6`**. `ADR-0124` is untouched and both post-EOF-write tests stay unweakened.
- **THE LESSON, because it has now recurred twice.** `ADR-0131` fired because every probe in the `SPEC.md` R-2 recon happened to **send a payload first**. **C-1 fired because every probe in the `ADR-0131` recon happened to use `echo`.** **When a measurement generalizes over a population of one, it has not been measured.** A phase adding a handler over N pre-existing consumers has **N-1 untested compositions**, and the §7.5 (a)-(e) gate — green and truthful throughout — cannot see them.
- **The valve stays ARMED** for the rest of `67.1`'s state-3.

### Phase-67.1 §5.2 state-3 re-entry — C-1 REPAIR COMPLETE (active phase)

- **`67.1` is IMPLEMENTATION-COMPLETE and UNVERIFIED → §5 state 4.** Every blocking finding in `REVIEW.md` has landed. `REVIEW.md` stays **NOT APPROVED** and is **never edited** — a review is superseded only by a LATER review (D-3.5). **§7.5 (f) remains the only unmet gate.**
- **The C-1 repair has two halves, and only one of them is code that runs.** `direct_response` **bypasses** the chain (exact measured parity, incl. under DENY); `[rbac, tcp_proxy]` is **rejected at config load** until `67.3` lands. The rejection is a divergence — upstream accepts that config — but the alternative is the shipped **runtime deadlock**, and §6.3's anti-pattern is a silent stub, not an honest refusal with a named owner.
- **`ADR-0131` is NOT reverted and `echo`/`hcm` are NOT touched.** The first-byte rule is real; it governs the RBAC **verdict**, not the chain's hand-off to the terminal filter. That distinction is the whole of C-1.
- **A test that cannot fail is worse than no test — M-1 proved it in this very phase.** `shadow_counters_register_at_zero_and_never_tick` asserted registration through `register_counter`, which is **get-or-create**: it would have minted each counter and read `0` even had `NetworkRbacFilter::new` registered nothing. The behavioral half was sound the whole time, which is exactly why nobody looked.
- **A hang is a test failure that destroys its own evidence.** Task 16's RED run hung rather than failed, because `validate_config` ran an ACCEPTED config to completion. That is **M-2's failure mode, encountered one task before M-2 was fixed.** Every read in the backstop file, and the config-validation helper itself, are now bounded.
- **A nondeterministic panic passes on the first run.** Task 18's `PendingTasks` rewiring left the in-crate `mk_multi_socket_listener` helper with ONE slot and N sockets; `reuseport_fanout_serves_and_drains` panicked `index out of bounds` on a `tokio-rt-worker` **only when the kernel steered the connection to socket #2**. It passed, then failed. Re-run a fan-out test several times before believing it, and `debug_assert` invariants **at the seam where they are established**, not where they are consumed.
- **A mutation check can lie.** Both mutation checks this session (`PendingTasks::publish`, the `shadow_allowed` registration) were confirmed honest by grepping the run for `Compiling` of the **mutated** crate. `cargo` will happily re-run a stale test binary.
- **`§6.1`'s valve stayed ARMED all session and did not need to fire again.** It remains armed for `67.2` and `67.3`.
- **THE LESSON, recorded because it recurred TWICE and the fix is now landed.** `ADR-0131` fired because every probe in the `SPEC.md` R-2 recon happened to **send a payload first**. **C-1 fired because every probe in the `ADR-0131` recon happened to use `echo`** — the one terminal filter with no establishment-time behavior. **When a measurement generalizes over a population of one, it has not been measured.** A phase that adds a handler over N pre-existing consumers has **N-1 untested compositions**, and the §7.5 (a)-(e) gate — green and truthful throughout — cannot see them. `67.1`'s composition matrix is now closed; **`67.2` widens the matcher arms and `67.3` re-opens `[rbac, tcp_proxy]`.**

- **C-1 (Critical, blocking) — a config-reachable release-mode data-plane PANIC**, found by PROBING the untested compositions (memory `state5-must-probe-untested-compositions`), not re-reading. `CidrRange::validate` sizes `prefix_len` against the pre-canonicalised address family (V6 `::ffff:127.0.0.0` → ≤128 OK), but `contains` canonicalises the mapped prefix to a 4-byte IPv4 before indexing, so `prefix_len` in `33..=128` on a v4-mapped `address_prefix` VALIDATES yet panics `prefix_match` (`bootstrap.rs:1691`, `net[..full]` with `full = 5..16` on a 4-byte slice). Affects all four IP arms (`destination_ip` on `local_addr`; `direct_remote_ip`/`remote_ip`/`source_ip` on `peer_addr`). **Reproduced end-to-end** against `target/debug/envoy-bin` (`range end index 5 out of range for slice of length 4`) **and independently CONFIRMED** by an adversarial `general-purpose` subagent (which derived the `33..=39` conditional sub-range and found no other validated-but-panics input). **Fix (state-3 re-entry):** size `validate` against the CANONICAL family — a v4-mapped prefix bounded at 32, `prefix_len > 32` rejected fail-loud.
- **I-1 (Important) — coverage blind spot.** `CidrRange::contains` is data-plane-only; the `parse_bootstrap` fuzz target only reaches deserialize+`validate`, so gate (d)'s "20000 runs, no crash" is structurally incapable of finding C-1. The re-entry adds a mapped-prefix regression test + a `contains`-level property/fuzz check. Advisory Minor **N-1** (defensive `prefix_match` bounds guard).
- **Everything else is well-built** — exhaustive catch-all-free classification at every site; the HTTP-rejects-L4-arms behavior is a deliberate FAIL-LOUD DIVERGENCE (upstream ACCEPTS them, measured; `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` item 14, ADR-0133), CONFIRMED WAI (do NOT "fix" toward parity); `destination_port: u16`; the shared source-IP evaluation; the `extra_leaves` macro. `REVIEW.md` §5 records the findings explicitly considered and REJECTED (HTTP-accepts-L4 parity, the wrapper-`prefix_len`, a differential fixture, a `_ =>` catch-all).

- **Re-entry output:** REVIEW.md's Important **I-1** FIXED under TDD via `superpowers:test-driven-development` (code commit `e0c6885`) — three tests added to `crates/envoy-health/src/probe.rs`'s `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, pinning the SPEC §2.1(8)/PLAN-Task-5-committed `grpc_probe_once` arms that were dropped and relabeled "indirect coverage" (CF-69-4→I-1). **NO product-logic change; NO new ADR** (ADR-0139 governs; ADR-0140 reserved-unfired).
- **The three tests:** **`grpc_probe_serving_is_ok`** — a loopback `h2::server` helper `spawn_grpc_verdict_server` (mirroring the `envoy-http2::grpc` `call_serving_verdict` body) replies `08 01` (SERVING) + `grpc-status:0` ⇒ `grpc_probe_once(addr, "hc.local", "", 2s).is_ok()`, pinning the `Ok(Serving)⇒Ok(())` arm (`probe.rs:313`); **`grpc_probe_not_serving_is_err`** — replies `08 02` (NOT_SERVING) + `grpc-status:0` ⇒ `matches!(err, GrpcProbeError::NotServing)`, pinning the `Ok(_other)⇒Err(NotServing)` eject-vs-keep arm (`:314`) — the arrow that turns a probe result into keep-vs-eject; **`grpc_probe_hang_times_out`** — an H2 backend that handshakes + accepts the request but never responds ⇒ `Err(GrpcProbeError::Timeout)` under a 300ms `probe_timeout`, the gRPC analogue of `tcp_probe_receive_mismatch_times_out`, pinning the whole-probe `timeout(probe_timeout, ...)` wrap (`:324`-`327`).
- **RED→GREEN discipline (D-3.1):** the product is verified-correct (state-5 found no live bug), so the tests were driven RED-first by TEMPORARILY mutating the product — swapping the two verdict arms + widening the timeout wrapper to `Duration::from_secs(30)` — against which all three FAIL for the exact right reasons (`expected Ok, got Err(NotServing)` / `got Ok(())` / `got Err(Rpc(...broken pipe))`), directly proving the review's claim that a verdict-flip mutation currently passes the whole suite. Reverting the mutation → all three GREEN (`cargo test -p envoy-health --lib grpc_probe_` → 5 passed). The final `probe.rs` diff is entirely within the `#[cfg(test)]` module (`@@ -518`; the module starts `:372`); the `grpc_probe_once`/codec/validator PRODUCT logic is byte-identical to the state-5 head.
- **Dev-deps + hygiene:** `h2 = "0.4"` / `http = "1"` / `bytes = "1"` added to `crates/envoy-health/Cargo.toml` `[dev-dependencies]` (test-only, for the loopback `h2::server`; the product path reaches `h2` transitively via `envoy-http2`). `cargo fmt -p envoy-health --check` + `cargo clippy -p envoy-health --tests` clean. ### Phase-74 §5 state-2 PLAN-write (active phase)

- **Artifact:** `docs/envoy-rust/phases/74-accesslog-metadata-filter/PLAN.md` — 10 numbered TDD tasks, authored SOLO (subagents returned EVIDENCE only, ADR-0127). ADR-0155 records the §6.2 empirical reconciliation of `SPEC.md` §3's PV-1..PV-8. NO code changed this session.
- **Two SPEC corrections a naive read would have shipped.** (1) The RBAC-scoped `validate_metadata_matcher` checks only `filter.is_empty()` and `path.len() != 1` — it does **NOT** check that a path segment's `key` is non-empty, though upstream PGV enforces `min_len 1`. The access-log validator adds that check natively; the RBAC gap opens **CF-74-4**. (2) Fixture `0082` must **OMIT `on_header_missing`**: envoy-rust requires a `value` on that block (as fixture `0042` supplies), so cloning `0042` would WRITE the metadata key on the no-header probe — the key would RESOLVE, the probe would be dropped by the VALUE path, and the fixture would PASS while silently vacating the `match_if_key_not_found` witness.
- **Two alternatives MEASURED-REJECTED, not assumed away.** A recon fan-out correctly observed that no `Option<bool>` matcher contract exists anywhere in the tree and proposed reusing `ValueMatcher::matches_resolved(Option<&str>) -> bool`; that maps an UNRESOLVED path to `false`, which would DROP every key-absent record — the exact opposite of the measured default `true` (R-0.4). And the record-based `should_log(&AccessLogRecord, …)` consolidation is BLOCKED, not merely costlier: `AccessLogRecord` deliberately has no `Default` and its only test constructor is `pub(crate)`, invisible to `envoy-http1`'s 49 test sites.
- **Census reconciled:** `rg -n "should_log" crates/ tests/` → 104 raw hits, of which **102 are code** (`envoy-http1` 49, `envoy-accesslog/filter.rs` 42, `file_sink.rs` 7, `envoy-http2` 4 — only 1 of those 4 is a call) and 2 are README prose. The SPEC's "102 call sites" is CONFIRMED, not corrected. `&record.dynamic_metadata` verified in scope at BOTH emit gates; `envoy-http2` wraps the H1 config (`HCMConfig { inner: Arc<Http1HCMConfig> }`), so `compile_access_log_filter` stays the ONLY compile site.
- **Split gate:** re-derived at **10 tasks / ~1135 net LoC** (code-only subtotal ~700) → well under the ~1500 LoC / ~25 task gate → single phase, **ADR-0156 stays UNFIRED**. ROADMAP row `74` unchanged.
- **Carry-forwards:** **N73-R1 FOLDED** into T1 (the stale "THREE oneof arms" doc → SIX). **NEW: CF-74-4** (the RBAC empty-segment-`key` gap) and **CF-74-5** (`present_match` on the RESOLVED branch is DERIVED from the measured rule, pinned in-process only). **M71-3 / M73-R2 / M70-R4 / M70-R9 NOT folded** — carry forward (M73-R2 is partially advanced by T4/T6's in-process composition pins but still wants a committed FIXTURE).
- **Next:** the §5 state-3 implementation (a SEPARATE session) — execute the 10 TDD tasks in order, append to `PROGRESS.md` per task, and do NOT run the §7.5 gate (that is state-4).
